The cumulative 18,867 source-expression comparisons include 1,600 trace, 6,400 detection and 222 successor comparisons. The entry is complete at its finite structural boundary; stochastic frequencies, physical noise mechanisms and asymptotic reliability remain outside that original claim.


At an initial index k, the position-pair recursion emits (k,s_0,v_0) and continues at k+1 on the two tails; it stops when either word ends. Its indexed membership theorem is

\[
 (i,a,b)\in Q_k(s,v)\iff\exists j,\ i=k+j\land s[j]=\operatorname{Some}(a)\land v[j]=\operatorname{Some}(b).
\]

The head case has j=0; the tail case increments j and uses k+1+j=k+(j+1). For equal-width words, induction also gives |Q_k(s,v)|=|s|. Filtering Q_k by a≠b gives exactly the changed positions, retaining order and both labels. Presentation maps (i,a,b) to ("position-" followed by the decimal representation of i+1,a,b).

For equal widths, the changed list is empty iff s=v: identical heads are removed and induction applies to the tails; unequal heads would be retained and contradict emptiness. Conversely, identical words have no unequal head at any step. Consequently

\[
 \operatorname{errorTrace}(s,v)=\operatorname{ok}(\mathrm{emptyOne})\iff s=v.
\]

For equal-width unequal words, the trace is the complete mapped changed list. Unequal widths return the common-position-carrier error before presentation. For any supplied valid-word list B, detection therefore satisfies

\[
 \operatorname{detectable}(B,s,v)=\operatorname{ok}
 \left(\begin{cases}\mathrm{true},&s=v,\\v\notin B,&s\ne v\end{cases}\right)
 \quad\text{when }|s|=|v|.
\]

The unequal-width error propagates unchanged; no membership guard on s is introduced.

For appended action cells A, the exact extension is

\[
 S'=S,\qquad V'=F(V\mathbin{++}[v:(s,v,a)\in A]),\qquad R'=R\mathbin{++}A.
\]

Assume the original relation is admitted, A is distinct and disjoint from R, and every added cell has its source in S and a nonempty action label. Concatenation preserves distinct triples; first-occurrence filtering preserves a nonempty distinct received carrier. Old endpoints remain admitted, new images enter V' by construction, and every old totality witness remains in R'. These facts prove extension admission.

Distributing filter and map over concatenation gives the exact order equations

\[
 P_{R'}(v)=F([s:(s,v,a)\in R]\mathbin{++}[s:(s,v,a)\in A]),
\]
\[
 I_{R'}(s)=F([v:(s,v,a)\in R]\mathbin{++}[v:(s,v,a)\in A]).
\]

Membership is consequently old membership or existence of a matching added action cell, in both directions. Shared images retain every predecessor through this same construction. At the identity base, S=V=[s] and R=[(s,s,"identity")]. The guards hold directly, P_R(s)=[s], correction returns uniqueSource(s), and the unchanged word has empty-One trace. This proves the base and finite action-successor clauses on the registered domain.

105. Complete coding support and held codebooks

Coding support enumerates the full ordered Cartesian product of at least two distinct labels over a nonempty position list. Its native membership characterization retains exactly every word of the held width whose labels belong to the alphabet. The cardinality is the alphabet size raised to that width, and distinct alphabet labels give duplicate-free support. The original position-list domain is preserved, including repeated position names.

A codebook returns the original held selection, in order, when it is nonempty, duplicate-free and contained in the supplied support. Native admission and membership proofs show that selecting from complete coding support gives every retained codeword the same position width and allowed labels. No additional guard is imposed on the supplied support itself.

Codeword difference retains the complete indexed changed-position trace and both labels at each change. Equality gives empty One; unequal widths retain Coding's original common-carrier error. The general position correspondence follows the established exact Noise and Error derivation.

The repetition constructor maps each supplied label to its constant word over the full position list. Its original helper accepts repeated labels, preserving output multiplicity and order. Under complete support's distinct-label condition, nonempty width makes the repetition map injective and its words distinct; each word belongs to the generated support. Independent source-expression comparisons pass 600 complete-support cases, 600 repetition cases, 1,785 held-codebook cases and 1,600 difference cases.


For an alphabet list A and position list P, coding support succeeds precisely when

\[
 |A|\ge2\land\operatorname{Distinct}(A)\land P\ne[].
\]

Put n=|P|. The output is the complete ordered word list W_n(A), with W_0(A)=[[]] and W_{n+1}(A)=concat_{a∈A}[a::w:w∈W_n(A)]. The head/tail decomposition proves by induction

\[
 w\in W_n(A)\iff |w|=n\land\forall a\in w,\ a\in A,
 \qquad |W_n(A)|=|A|^n.
\]

For distinct A, different leading labels separate the generated blocks and the tail induction excludes repeats within each block. Thus the complete support is distinct. Position names enter this constructor through their list length; no distinct-position-name condition is added.

For an arbitrary supplied support U and held list H, the codebook result has the exact characterization

\[
 \operatorname{codebook}(U,H)=\operatorname{ok}(K)
 \iff H\ne[]\land\operatorname{Distinct}(H)\land H\subseteq U\land K=H.
\]

The operation therefore retains the exact order and contents of H. If U=W_n(A) is admitted complete support, every w∈K belongs to U, so the preceding membership theorem gives |w|=n and every cell in A. For two retained words u,v, their two width equalities imply |u|=|v|. No guard on U beyond held-list membership is introduced by codebook itself.

For equal-width u,v, differenceTrace uses exactly the Noise and Error changed-position construction. Consequently

\[
 \operatorname{differenceTrace}(u,v)=\operatorname{ok}(\mathrm{emptyOne})\iff u=v,
\]

and its changes result consists exactly of the one-based printed positions where u and v differ, with both labels retained. On unequal widths it returns Coding's own common-position-carrier error, rather than substituting Noise and Error's error text.

Define the constant word r_P(a)=map(λp.a,P). Repetition admission requires only |A|≥2 and P≠[], and returns [r_P(a):a∈A] in alphabet-list order. Induction on P gives

\[
 |r_P(a)|=|P|,\qquad b\in r_P(a)\Longrightarrow b=a.
\]

Thus any emitted word from a label a∈A belongs to admitted W_n(A). Since P is nonempty, equality r_P(a)=r_P(b) forces equality of their first cells, a=b. The map is therefore injective, and distinct A yields a distinct repetition list. Repeated labels in the broader repetition helper remain repeated output words; this proof uses the distinctness already supplied by complete-support admission and does not change that helper's guard.

106. Complete single-label error images and exact decoding

Single-label image generation begins with the unchanged source word, then visits every retained position and every supplied label in order, skipping only labels equal to the held label at that position. Native membership is equivalent to identity or to a decomposition into an unchanged prefix, one different supplied replacement label and an unchanged suffix. This equivalence includes both completeness and exclusion of unregistered replacements. Every image has the source width, and generated changes are nonidentity. A source in complete coding support has all its images in that support. The raw helper retains repeated supplied labels and their repeated outputs.

The complete error family retains each source occurrence with its full image list. Detection holds exactly when each image is either its source or outside the codebook. Correction holds exactly when every positional pair of source image families has no common received word. Native equivalences establish these conditions over the full generated lists, including raw duplicate source occurrences.

Decoding filters source occurrences in their original order by exact received-image membership. A singleton gives the original unique-source record; any other length gives the entire closed source class. The native correction theorem proves that disjoint source families yield an empty or singleton filtered list. Consequently, every registered received image of a correctable code decodes to its source. Conversely, every unique decoded source is a retained codeword with that received image in its registered family. No distance or prior is used. Independent source-expression comparisons pass 1,600 image lists, 465 complete families, 465 detection decisions, 465 correction decisions and 2,790 decoding records.


For the supplied label list A, the complete changed-image recursion is

\[
 D_A([])=[],\qquad D_A(h::t)=[a::t:a\in A,\ a\ne h]\mathbin{++}[h::v:v\in D_A(t)].
\]

The image list is E_A(w)=[w]++D_A(w). The first branch changes the first position; the second retains it and recursively changes a later position. Induction, splitting on whether the unchanged prefix is empty, proves the exact equivalence

\[
 v\in D_A(w)\iff\exists p,h,t,a,\ w=p\mathbin{++}(h::t)
 \land a\in A\land a\ne h\land v=p\mathbin{++}(a::t).
\]

The forward proof extracts the replacement from the head filter or prepends the unchanged head to the tail induction's prefix. Conversely, an empty prefix selects the head branch; a nonempty prefix selects the recursive branch. Thus E_A(w) contains precisely identity and every registered single-label replacement. Mapping and filtering retain the original label multiplicities and visit order.

Each branch preserves length, giving |v|=|w| for every v∈E_A(w). A changed image cannot equal w: cancelling the unchanged prefix would give a=h, contradicting the replacement guard. If all labels of w lie in A, each changed image also uses only A, since its unchanged cells retain that property and its replacement was selected from A. Together with preserved width, complete-support membership proves closure of all images inside the admitted support.

For a code list C, the family [(w,E_A(w)):w∈C] has exactly |C| rows, one per source occurrence. Expanding the Boolean all/any tests yields

\[
 \operatorname{Detect}(C,A)\iff\forall w\in C,\forall v\in E_A(w),\ v=w\lor v\notin C,
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Correct}(C,A)\iff\forall(u,w)\in P(C),\
 \neg\exists v,\ v\in E_A(u)\land v\in E_A(w),
\]

where P(C) is the full positional pair list. The pair condition retains raw source occurrences rather than silently deduplicating C.

The received source class is the ordered filter

\[
 H_{C,A}(v)=[w\in C:v\in E_A(w)],\qquad
 w\in H_{C,A}(v)\iff w\in C\land v\in E_A(w).
\]

Decoding applies the singleton/closed-class record constructor to this exact list. Hence decode(v)=uniqueSource(w) iff H_{C,A}(v)=[w]; every nonsingleton result retains H_{C,A}(v) intact.

To prove correct decoding, induct on C. If its head has no image v, the filtered list equals the tail's class and correction restricts to the tail's positional pairs. If the head does have image v, every tail occurrence must reject v: accepting it would give a shared image for that head–tail positional pair, contradicting Correct. The filtered tail is therefore empty and the whole class is the head singleton. Thus

\[
 \operatorname{Correct}(C,A)\Longrightarrow
 H_{C,A}(v)=[]\ \lor\ \exists w,\ H_{C,A}(v)=[w].
\]

When w∈C and v∈E_A(w), class membership excludes the empty case and identifies the singleton as w, proving decode(v)=uniqueSource(w). Conversely, a unique-source record gives that singleton class; its member must be a retained source with v in its generated family. This proves both recovery and provenance using the full registered image enumeration.

107. General coding action succession and retained source provenance

A registered error family assigns its complete finite image list to each retained codeword. The general native detection, correction and decoding loops are definitionally the original single-label loops when instantiated with those original images. The singleton-action base supplies one image per codeword; correction then holds exactly when every positional pair has different action images.

Appending an action's registered images preserves the old image list and its order. The detection successor theorem is an equivalence: extended detection holds exactly when both prior and added images satisfy the original codebook-membership rule. The correction successor theorem checks every old–old, old–new, new–old and new–new pair of image supports. Their joint disjointness is equivalent to correction of the extended family. The received source class extends by exactly the sources whose new image lists contain that form. These proofs apply to arbitrary finite registered actions and preserve raw list multiplicity.

The stated total source/codeword relation retains one codeword for each registered source. Native recovery proves that every received image of that codeword in a correctable family decodes to the held codeword while preserving the source row. The same recovery result follows after an action addition precisely when the complete successor disjointness conditions hold. No injective message assignment beyond the stated source-map constraint is imposed.

The original width-three repetition example is a held codebook and its complete single-label image families are disjoint. The one-position uncoded control fails correction; a width-two repetition family also fails, giving the exact finite separation witness for the retained width. Coding includes all 2,048 original kernels and all six original operational witnesses. The cumulative 19,745 source-expression comparisons include 9,375 action-successor detection, correction and decoding outputs. Coding remains within the original finite classical boundary, without a stochastic error model, metric threshold, imported asymptotic rate or quantum-code claim.

Fresh native execution of the complete Coding program matches all 2,048 original candidate lookups together with every registration, census, closure, control and digest field and the unknown-identifier rejection. These results accompany the native source derivations and complete the Coding entry on its original finite classical domain.


Let F(w) be the ordered image list registered for codeword w. For action cells R, its registered-image constructor is [v:(w,v,a)∈R], retaining all matching occurrences. Membership is equivalent to existence of a matching action a. The general detection, correction and source-class definitions are exactly those of section 106 with E_A(w) replaced by F(w); substituting E_A recovers the original single-label operations by definition.

For a singleton action f, put F_f(w)=[f(w)]. Two such lists overlap iff their sole values agree, so

\[
 \operatorname{Correct}(C,F_f)\iff\forall(u,w)\in P(C),\ f(u)\ne f(w).
\]

For old and added families F,G, define (F⊕G)(w)=F(w)++G(w). Membership splits into the old or added list. Applying that split to the universal detection condition proves both directions of

\[
 \operatorname{Detect}(C,F\oplus G)\iff
 \operatorname{Detect}(C,F)\land\operatorname{Detect}(C,G).
\]

Define X_C(F,G) to mean that, for every positional pair (u,w)∈P(C), no received word belongs to both F(u) and G(w). Expanding the two append memberships yields precisely four cases:

\[
 \operatorname{Correct}(C,F\oplus G)\iff
 \operatorname{Correct}(C,F)\land X_C(F,G)\land X_C(G,F)\land\operatorname{Correct}(C,G).
\]

For the forward direction, each alleged shared image in one case embeds into the two extended lists and contradicts their disjointness. Conversely, an overlap in the extended lists belongs to one of old–old, old–new, new–old or new–new, and the corresponding conjunct excludes it. Both cross orientations are retained because P(C) uses source order.

The extended source class remains the single ordered filter

\[
 H_{C,F\oplus G}(v)=[w\in C:v\in F(w)\lor v\in G(w)].
\]

Each source occurrence is tested once against the disjunction; the two separate filtered lists are not concatenated. This preserves the actual source-list multiplicity even when both families contain v for the same source.

For registered source labels S, code list C and row list E, the source-map condition is

\[
 \forall s\in S,\ \exists c\in C,\ (s,c)\in E
 \land\forall d,\ (s,d)\in E\Rightarrow d=c.
\]

Select that retained c for a source s. Under Correct(C,F), the general source-class induction proves that every v∈F(c) decodes to uniqueSource(c). The row (s,c) is retained alongside this recovery statement. Different source labels are not required by this condition to have different codewords. Under the four successor conditions, apply the same result to F⊕G; this establishes recovery after the action addition without strengthening the source-map domain.

For the concrete alphabet [a,b] and width three, the complete lists are

\[
 E(aaa)=[aaa,baa,aba,aab],\qquad E(bbb)=[bbb,abb,bab,bba].
\]

They are disjoint; every changed word lies outside [aaa,bbb], and baa occurs only in the aaa family. The complete support has 2^3=8 distinct words, while aaa and bbb differ at all three positions. These computations give the retained support, difference, detection, correction and decoding witnesses. For width two,

\[
 E(aa)=[aa,ba,ab],\qquad E(bb)=[bb,ab,ba],
\]

so ab and ba witness failure of correction. At width one, E(a)=[a,b] and E(b)=[b,a] overlap as well. These full finite lists establish the protected and unprotected witness results directly.

Let S be the ordered support and O the observation rows. Validation succeeds exactly when

 S\ne[]\land\operatorname{Distinct}(S)\land\operatorname{Distinct}(\operatorname{keys}(O))
 \land\operatorname{keys}(O)\subseteq S\land S\subseteq\operatorname{keys}(O).
\]

 \operatorname{accept}(c)\iff\bigwedge_{i=1}^{10}(c_i=\mathrm{admitted})
 \iff c=(\mathrm{admitted},\ldots,\mathrm{admitted}).

Any rejected field contradicts the corresponding projection of that equality and therefore rejects the candidate. 113. Exact conservation and loss of source distinctions

A transformation assigns exactly one image to each member of complete duplicate-free source support. The native validator preserves the original source-first and map-second guard order and errors. Image names remain unrestricted strings. Complete source pairs visit each source form followed by every later source form in the original order.

The transformation ledger classifies each pair by exact image equality. Different images retain the distinction; equal images close it. Native membership equivalences prove that these two ledgers disjointly exhaust the complete source-pair list. Empty ledgers have the original empty-One presentation. The full record retains source support, first-occurrence image support, both pair ledgers and exact predecessor fibres.

For an admitted transformation, a closed pair lies in a common image fibre. Conversely, every source pair whose two members lie in a common image fibre is closed. These statements retain the exact source provenance of loss. Independent comparisons pass 813 validations, 121 complete ordered pair outputs and 813 full transformation records, including empty-string and literal empty-One labels, reversed mappings and invalid source/map cases.


For source list S and transformation rows T, admission requires S≠[], distinct S, distinct keys(T), and key-set equality with S. Support is checked before the map, and success retains T unchanged. Let f_T(s) denote its admitted image. The complete pair recursion is

\[
 P([])=[],\qquad P(x::R)=[(x,y):y\in R]\mathbin{++}P(R).
\]

The two ordered subledgers are

\[
 R_T=[(x,y)\in P(S):f_T(x)\ne f_T(y)],\qquad
 C_T=[(x,y)\in P(S):f_T(x)=f_T(y)].
\]

Filter membership proves each defining equivalence. Decidable equality places every pair in one of the two lists; simultaneous membership would assert both equality and its negation. Thus these ledgers exhaust the original pairs without overlap, retaining their source traversal order. Empty lists are presented as structural empty One, and nonempty lists are retained intact.

The full record is (S,L_T,present(R_T),present(C_T),[(a,F_T(a)):a∈L_T]), where L_T is the first-occurrence image-label list and F_T(a)=[s∈S:f_T(s)=a]. For a closed pair, total lookup supplies its first endpoint's label a; equality gives that same label for the second endpoint, placing both in F_T(a). Conversely, two endpoints of a source pair in F_T(a) have equal images and the pair is closed. This proves the correspondence between closed distinctions and their exact predecessor fibres.

114. Composition and downstream retention

Transformation composition first validates the source map, derives its middle support in source-order first occurrence, and validates the second map on that complete middle support. Its output retains one row per original source form in the original order. Native proofs establish exact successive lookup and preservation of transformation admission.

When two source forms have equal first images, their composed images are equal. Every closed upstream pair therefore remains closed. Since the retained and closed ledgers are disjoint and exhaustive, each retained composite pair must have been retained upstream. The native downstream-retention theorem proves this subset relation for arbitrary finite admitted compositions, and establishes that the original executable law returns true. No external record or newly created distinction is introduced. Independent comparisons pass 648 complete compositions and 648 downstream results, including the original validation errors and reordered maps; the cumulative comparison total is 3,043.


Composition validates T on S, forms its complete first-occurrence image support L_T, and validates U on L_T. The emitted rows are

\[
 V=[(s,f_U(f_T(s))):s\in S].
\]

The implementation's lookup default is unreachable on these admitted queries: totality supplies f_T(s), its occurrence puts it in L_T, and U is total on L_T. Induction on the row construction gives keys(V)=S and image_V(s)=Some(f_U(f_T(s))) for s∈S. Therefore V preserves distinct keys, coverage and source order and is an admitted transformation.

If (x,y)∈C_T, then f_T(x)=f_T(y). Applying f_U yields f_U(f_T(x))=f_U(f_T(y)), so

\[
 C_T\subseteq C_V.
\]

Suppose a retained composite pair were not retained upstream. Its source-pair membership and exhaustive equality split would place it in C_T, hence C_V, contradicting disjointness of R_V and C_V. Consequently

\[
 R_V\subseteq R_T.
\]

The executable downstream law removes only the presentation constructor and tests membership in R_T for every pair of R_V. The subset result supplies every test, so the all predicate returns true for admitted compositions. Validation errors retain their original order through the ledger, composition and final-ledger calls.

115. Exact predecessor records and recovery

The reverse record visits the predecessor fibres in their original order. A singleton fibre returns its source label directly; every other fibre returns the original held-predecessor-labels record with its complete ordered member list. Native equivalences establish precisely when each form is produced. Every source with the recorded image equals the unique predecessor in a singleton record. For a held record, membership is exactly source membership together with the recorded image. Two distinct retained predecessors exclude a unique record.

The executable reversibility decision retains V3's comparison of the number of distinct admitted dictionary images with the number of source forms. Independent comparisons pass 813 such decisions and 813 complete reverse records, including original errors and unrestricted string labels. The cumulative transformation comparison total is 4,669. The native count-decision equivalence with singleton fibres is established below.


For a predecessor member list M, the exact record cases are

\[
 B(M)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{unique}(s),&M=[s],\\
 \operatorname{heldLabels}(M),&|M|\ne1.\end{cases}
\]

Splitting M into empty, singleton and longer lists proves B(M)=unique(s) iff M=[s], and B(M)=heldLabels(H) iff H=M and |M|≠1. Reverse rows map (a,F_T(a)) to (a,B(F_T(a))) without reordering fibres. Thus a unique record for a supplies F_T(a)=[s]. Any source t with image a belongs to that fibre and hence equals s. A held record satisfies

\[
 t\in H\iff t\in S\land f_T(t)=a.
\]

If two different predecessors lie in M, uniqueness would force both to equal its alleged singleton member and contradict their difference. No member is selected from a merged fibre.

Let D=map(second,T) be the dictionary-value list, and let L(D) retain its first occurrences. After validation, the executable reversibility result is exactly

\[
 \operatorname{isReversible}(S,T)=\operatorname{ok}(|L(D)|=|S|).
\]

This is the original count expression; the next derivation relates it to the fibre-based recovery records.

116. Reversibility is equivalent to singleton fibres

For every transformation admitted by the original validator, the executable distinct-image count test returns true exactly when every observed predecessor fibre contains one source form. The native proof retains the original dictionary-value count. First-occurrence deduplication preserves list length exactly when the value list has no repetitions. Unique source keys establish exact correspondence between dictionary values and the images obtained by traversing the admitted source support. Their distinct-image counts are equal, regardless of dictionary row order.

Distinct mapped source values are equivalent to injectivity on the held source support. Injectivity makes each nonempty image fibre a singleton; conversely, singleton fibres identify any two sources with the same image. These implications prove both directions of V3's reversibility statement on arbitrary finite admitted supports, without a new guard or an assumed inverse. The established reverse-record recovery theorems then give direct recovery for singleton fibres and complete retained predecessor alternatives for merged fibres.


A first-occurrence scan can never lengthen a list. If it skips a head already seen, its tail output has length at most the tail length and therefore strictly less than the original list length. Hence equality of input and output lengths forces every head to be retained and, recursively, absent from the later list. Conversely, a distinct list with no initially seen member is retained unchanged. Starting with an empty seen list gives

\[
 |L(X)|=|X|\iff\operatorname{Distinct}(X).
\]

Let D=map(second,T) and V=[f_T(s):s∈S]. A value in D has a dictionary row; unique keys make lookup return that row's value, and coverage puts its key in S, so the value occurs in V. Conversely, lookup of any admitted s yields a retained dictionary row and thus a value of D. Therefore D and V have identical value membership. Their first-occurrence lists are distinct and mutually contained; finite distinct-list length bounds in both directions give |L(D)|=|L(V)|. Since |V|=|S|,

\[
 |L(D)|=|S|\iff|L(V)|=|V|\iff\operatorname{Distinct}(V).
\]

On distinct S, injectivity of f_T makes V distinct: a repeated head value would identify its source with a later source, contradicting distinctness, and the tail follows by induction. Conversely, if V is distinct, equal mapped values cannot occur at two different source positions; splitting source membership into head and tail proves injectivity. Thus the original count test is equivalent to injectivity on S.

Each observed fibre is nonempty and distinct. Under injectivity, choose one of its members s; every other member has the same image and must equal s, so the fibre is [s]. Conversely, two sources with equal images lie in the same observed fibre, and singleton fibres make those sources equal. Combining the equivalences proves

\[
 \operatorname{isReversible}(S,T)=\operatorname{ok}(\mathrm{true})
 \iff f_T\text{ is injective on }S
 \iff\forall a\in L_T,\ \exists s,\ F_T(a)=[s].
\]

The argument uses membership and distinct counts, so arbitrary admitted dictionary-row order is preserved. Recovery follows from the existing reverse records, without postulating an inverse function.

117. Source succession and conservation of pair accounting

The singleton transformation has one source, one held image, one singleton predecessor fibre and empty retained and closed pair ledgers. Native evaluation proves the complete original record. Adding a fresh source and one image row preserves the admitted transformation conditions. Every image fibre retains its old members and appends the new source exactly when its label matches the added image.

The complete pair list after extension retains the original source traversal order, adding one pair between each prior source and the fresh source. A retained successor pair is exactly a previously retained pair or a new old/fresh pair with unequal images. A closed successor pair is exactly a previously closed pair or a new old/fresh pair with equal images. These native equivalences establish exhaustive successor accounting for arbitrary finite support.

All five original operational witnesses pass native proof: identity conservation, exact prefix loss, the identity/prefix reversibility boundary, complete held predecessor records and downstream erasure. \[
 F_{T'}(a)=F_T(a)\mathbin{++}\begin{cases}[x],&v=a,\\\lbrack\rbrack,&v\ne a.\end{cases}
\]

The pair list retains its nested source order. Explicitly, E_x([])=[] and E_x(y::R)=([(y,z):z∈R]++[(y,x)])++E_x(R), and P(S++[x])=E_x(S). Membership is exactly old pair membership or a new pair (s,x) with s∈S. Substituting the old and fresh image equations into the two filters yields

 p\in C_{T'}\iff p\in C_T\lor\exists s\in S,\ p=(s,x)\land f_T(s)=v.
\]

Both directions follow from the pair split: old endpoints keep their images; a new pair compares exactly its old image with v. The formulas classify the complete ordered successor list, without replacing it by a differently ordered concatenation of pair classes.

Composing prefix projection with a↦one,b↦one closes all six pairs and leaves no retained pair, establishing the downstream-erasure witness.

118. Complete conservation and transformation program correspondence

Fresh native execution matches all 1,024 original candidate lookups, registration, census, closure, controls, hashes and unknown-identifier rejection. Together with exhaustive pair accounting, exact composition, downstream retention, reversibility equivalence, predecessor recovery and arbitrary finite source succession, this completes the entry on its original deterministic finite domain. \[
 |\mathcal G|=2^{10}=1{,}024.
\]

Choosing the appropriate member of each axis list and applying nested product membership proves that every typed candidate is enumerated. Exhausting the ten constructor choices establishes equality between the source identifier decision and the conjunction of the ten admitted-field tests. Hence

\[
 \operatorname{accept}(c)\iff\bigwedge_{i=1}^{10}c_i=\mathrm{admitted}
 \iff c=(\mathrm{admitted},\ldots,\mathrm{admitted}).
\]

Projecting this equality onto any rejected field gives a contradiction, proving rejection for each failed criterion. This complete finite classification accompanies the source-pair, composition, fibre, recovery and successor derivations above.

The original program constructs each candidate from the ordered Cartesian product of its declared choice lists, joins its coordinate names to form the identifier, and retains the coordinate/form record. The reason scan stops at the first rejected coordinate in declared order. Census hashes retain the complete candidate record; closure hashes retain the closure record and ordered decisions; each control retains its own observed result and receipt hash. 119. Classical state, observation classes and deterministic realization

A classical information state retains one member of the complete nonempty duplicate-free support together with that support as provenance. A total observation partitions the same support by its labels in first-occurrence order. Each probability row retains its entire ordered microstate class and the reduced positive fraction of complete support occupied by that class. Native proofs identify the exact class membership, retained order and fraction count equation. Deterministic pushforward constructs corresponding image rows with complete predecessor classes and exact parts.

Observation first requires exactly one row for its observed label. A singleton member class returns its held classical state; every other retained class returns all its members. The native singleton equivalence and unresolved-member identity preserve this boundary. Deterministic realization visits the probability rows in order, pairing every original microstate with the deterministic-member tag while retaining the class label and its exact support part. Source-expression comparisons cover 6,296 support, ledger, resolution and realization outputs and error cases, including empty labels and original validation order. Exact-whole closure and the source microstate-successor construction are established below.


Canonical support admission is S≠[] and Distinct(S). A classical-state request succeeds exactly when this holds and h∈S, returning (heldState=h,supportProvenance=S). For observation O, probability validation checks the support first, then distinct keys and complete key coverage. Pushforward validation has the same successful domain but checks duplicate map keys before support validation, retaining the original short-circuit errors.

For each first-occurrence label a, let F_a=[s∈S:f_O(s)=a], m_a=|F_a| and N=|S|. The probability row is (a,F_a,(u_a,v_a)), with the positive reduced part satisfying

\[
 m_a v_a=u_aN,\qquad u_a>0,\quad v_a>0,\quad\gcd(u_a,v_a)=1.
\]

The row maps from the entropy ledger preserve its label, members and part exactly. Induction on those maps proves that projecting label/member pairs returns the original ordered partition. Pushforward uses the same record with image/predecessor field names, so its source provenance and fraction equation are identical.

Resolution first forms H=[r in rows:r.label=a]. It returns the outside-observation error unless H=[r] is exactly a singleton. For that sole row,

\[
 \operatorname{resolveMembers}(M)=\operatorname{classicalState}(s)\iff M=[s].
\]

The empty and longer-list cases return unresolvedClass(M) with M unchanged. Deterministic realization maps each row to (a,[(s,"deterministic-member"):s∈F_a],(u_a,v_a)). Projecting first coordinates recovers F_a by list induction, while the label and fraction are unchanged by construction. The realization therefore exposes every original member in order.

120. Complete observation-class cardinality

For every total observation of a finite support, the sum of the full fibre cardinalities over the first-occurrence observed labels equals the support cardinality. The proof counts each source occurrence against distinct observed labels: exactly its own image contributes once. Induction over the support then reconstructs the complete count. No equal-class-size assumption is used.

The raw exact-whole helper retains its Fraction input domain, including signed and zero fractions. Integer cross-multiplication accumulates the exact numerator and denominator; the nonempty ledger is whole precisely when those values are equal. Generated probability and pushforward rows supply their original positive reduced fractions to this calculation. 3,614 independent source-expression comparisons pass, including 2,801 raw fraction lists and 813 generated-ledger or original-error cases. The universal reduced-fraction bridge and exact-whole result are established below.


Let L be the distinct list of observed labels, and define

\[
 H_L(a)=\sum_{b\in L}\mathbf1_{b=a},\qquad
 K(S,O,L)=\sum_{a\in L}|F_O(a)|.
\]

If a∉L, every summand in H_L(a) is zero. If a∈L and L is distinct, its unique matching position contributes one and every other position contributes zero, so H_L(a)=1. For f_O(s)=a, expanding each fibre filter at the head gives

\[
 K(s::S,O,L)=H_L(a)+K(S,O,L).
\]

Total observation coverage supplies such an a∈L for each source. Induction over S, starting from K([],O,L)=0, therefore yields K(S,O,L)=|S|. This counts every source occurrence exactly once without assuming equal fibre sizes.

The raw exact-sum helper begins with (n,d)=(0,1) and, for each rational p/q, updates

\[
 (n,d)\longmapsto(nq+pd,dq).
\]

Here n,p are integers and d,q are natural denominators; zero and negative input fractions remain admitted. Cross-multiplication gives (nq+pd)/(dq)=n/d+p/q, so induction represents the exact rational sum. The executable whole test is false on an empty input list; on a nonempty list it tests n=d after all updates. Generated positive reduced parts enter this same helper through their exact numerator and denominator, without changing its broader raw domain.

121. Exact-whole closure and microstate succession

Every generated probability ledger and deterministic pushforward ledger reconstructs the exact whole. The proof tracks the numerator and denominator of the original exact sum through each retained class fraction. Its invariant relates the accumulated numerator to the count of represented microstates over the fixed support count. Reduced class fractions satisfy this relation by their native count equations. Complete class coverage gives the full support count, and cancellation of that positive count establishes equality of the accumulated numerator and denominator. Thus the executable exact-whole test returns true for every admitted ledger.

The singleton base retains its sole classical state with complete provenance, one observation class and one exact whole part. Extending admitted support by one fresh microstate preserves admission. Its assigned class gains exactly that state in source order, every other class retains its members, and each reduced fraction satisfies the updated membership-to-support ratio. The successor ledger again reconstructs the exact whole. These statements apply at arbitrary finite depth and preserve deterministic membership throughout. Full candidate enumeration and complete program correspondence are verified below.


For generated rows, let N>0 be the support size, m_i each row's microstate count and a_i/b_i its reduced part. The native row equation is a_iN=m_i b_i. At an intermediate sum with numerator n, denominator d and represented count u, use the invariant nN=ud. Adding one row gives

\[
 (nb_i+a_id)N
 =(nN)b_i+(a_iN)d
 =u d b_i+m_i b_i d
 =(u+m_i)(db_i).
\]

Thus the same invariant holds after each exact update. Starting from (0,1,0), induction over all rows gives n_final N=(Σ_i m_i)d_final. The class-count theorem supplies Σ_i m_i=N; cancellation of positive N yields n_final=d_final. The rows cannot be empty because their member count is N>0. Hence the executable exact-whole predicate returns true.

The natural-number accumulator for these positive rows agrees with the signed raw helper after embedding its numerator into the integers: their recurrences have identical multiplication and addition updates. Probability and pushforward row maps preserve the part list exactly. Consequently the preceding argument proves exact-whole closure for both generated ledger types, not only for unreduced count fractions.

For fresh x∉S with assigned label v, validation remains admitted after S'=S++[x], O'=O++[(x,v)]. Old lookup values persist, and the assigned fibre gains x:

\[
 F'_a=F_a\mathbin{++}\begin{cases}[x],&a=v,\\\lbrack\rbrack,&a\ne v.\end{cases}
\]

Every successor row with part a'_i/b'_i therefore satisfies

\[
 (|F_i|+\mathbf1_{i=v})b'_i=a'_i(N+1).
\]

Applying the universal closure result to the newly admitted ledger proves that it again reconstructs the whole. At the singleton base S=[s], O=[(s,a)], the state is (s,[s]), the projected ledger is [(a,[s])], and its part is 1/1. The same base and successor construction preserves deterministic-member provenance at every finite stage.

124. Quantum-information branch support and provenance

The support correspondence generates every held-label word across a nonempty canonical position trace. Its original validator requires at least two distinct labels and distinct positions. Native correspondence with the information-quantity construction preserves the full Cartesian order and proves exhaustive word membership and duplicate freedom. Empty string labels remain allowed.

The superposition-equivalent record retains the complete branch family and pairs each word with its full position-label trace. Projecting these records recovers the original branch family in order; projecting each trace recovers both its original word and every canonical position. The amplitude field retains the original not-admitted-at-support-boundary marker. 3,200 independent comparisons cover full support/provenance outputs and original errors. Information-unit traces, basis records, joint support and observation/reconstruction are established below; the canonical basis-name correspondence is established below.


Write L for the ordered label list and P for the ordered position list, with n=|P|. Admission is precisely |L|≥2, Distinct(L), n>0 and Distinct(P). The recursive complete support is

\[
 W_0(L)=[[]],\qquad W_{n+1}(L)=\mathop{\mathrm{concat}}_{\ell\in L}[\ell::w:w\in W_n(L)].
\]

Induction on n proves w∈W_n(L) if and only if |w|=n and every label of w belongs to L: the successor case removes the first label and applies the induction hypothesis to the tail. Distinct labels and distinct tails make each block duplicate-free, and different first labels separate different blocks. This establishes duplicate freedom of the complete support.

For each admitted w, define T_P(w)=zip(P,w). The returned branch record is (W_n,[(w,T_P(w)):w∈W_n],not-admitted-at-support-boundary). Equal lengths permit simultaneous induction on P and w, giving

\[
 \pi_1(T_P(w))=P,\qquad\pi_2(T_P(w))=w.
\]

Projecting the word field of the outer record likewise returns W_n in its original order. Thus the complete alternative family and each branch's full origin are retained by the construction itself.

125. Basis records and joint support

The basis correspondence retains each original word together with its source colon-delimited basis name. Projecting the retained words reconstructs complete input support exactly, and distinct words yield distinct word/name records. The name field alone is not injective over the original unrestricted string-label domain: labels a and a:a at two canonical positions generate the distinct words (a,a:a) and (a:a,a), both named basis:a:a:a. The accepted support, distinct words and identical names are established by native proofs. Consequently, retained-record correspondence and name-only uniqueness are separate propositions; the latter does not hold over the complete executable domain.

Joint support requires two nonempty duplicate-free word carriers and enumerates every left/right pair in source order, retaining both coordinates and their concatenation. Native membership equivalence establishes complete pair coverage; coordinate recovery preserves both source words even when concatenated values coincide. 993 independent output comparisons cover exact basis and joint records, errors, empty words and delimiter-containing labels.


For a word w=[w_1,…,w_n], the executable name is B(w)=“basis:”++intercalate(“:”,w), and the basis record list is [(w,B(w)):w∈S]. Projection onto its first component gives S. Equality of two records immediately gives equality of their words, establishing injectivity of the retained-record map without any condition on delimiters inside labels. The raw example satisfies

\[
 B([\text{a},\text{a:a}])=\text{basis:a:a:a}=B([\text{a:a},\text{a}]),
\]

while the two first coordinates differ. The fixed inherited Fold labels used in the registered derivation have the separate name-injectivity proof below.

For admitted left and right carriers A and C, the joint construction is

\[
 J(A,C)=\mathop{\mathrm{concat}}_{a\in A}[(a,c,a\mathbin{++}c):c\in C].
\]

Expanding the nested list maps proves (a,c,z)∈J(A,C) exactly when a∈A, c∈C and z=a++c. Equality of two emitted triples forces equality of both first and second coordinates by projection. Hence the joint correspondence retains the original pair even if concatenation alone would erase its split.

126. Independently realized information-unit traces

Each canonical position retains a four-field record: its position name, the one-Fold-information-distinction tag, the all-first-label baseline word and the word differing only at that position by the second held label. Let a and b be the first two distinct admitted labels. For zero-based position i<n, the baseline and its independently changed alternative are

\[
 u_i=a^i\mathbin{++}[a]\mathbin{++}a^{n-i-1}=a^n,\qquad
 v_i=a^i\mathbin{++}[b]\mathbin{++}a^{n-i-1}.
\]

Here a^k means the list of k copies of a. Both words have length n and every component belongs to L, so complete-support membership puts both in W_n(L). If u_i=v_i, cancelling the common prefix of i copies gives equal heads a=b, contradicting distinctness. The four-field row is (P_i,one-Fold-information-distinction,u_i,v_i).

The recursive implementation emits the head-position row and increments i before processing the remaining positions. Its invariant is i+|remaining positions|=n. Induction preserves this invariant, proves membership of both words in every row, and gives exactly n rows whose position projection is P. Thus the construction establishes an independent distinction at every position for arbitrary finite depth.

Let O have distinct word keys whose set equals the support set, and write f_O(w) for lookup of the image of w. For selected image y the emitted lists are

\[
 R_y=[w\in S:f_O(w)=y],\qquad C_y=[w\in S:w\notin R_y],\qquad
 E=[(w,f_O(w)):w\in S].
\]

Observation rejects an empty R_y. Otherwise it returns y, R_y, the presented C_y (using the empty-One marker when empty), and E. These equivalences prove disjointness and exhaustive accounting of S while preserving each filtered order.

List induction gives π₁(E)=S. Reconstruction first requires E nonempty and Distinct(π₁(E)), then returns π₁(E). Consequently canonical nonempty duplicate-free S is recovered exactly. The raw observation guard checks distinct observation keys and coverage in both directions; it does not require distinct S. Repeated support occurrences therefore remain present in E, and the separate reconstruction guard rejects them exactly as specified by the source.

130. Canonical Fold basis bijection

The registered Fold Assembly generator supplies precisely held-a and held-b. Quantum support with these inherited labels contains exactly the words in Fold Assembly at the same finite depth. The original colon-joined basis names uniquely identify these words: the native proof establishes exact character decoding, cancels the basis prefix and recovers the held-label sequence. Hence all emitted names are distinct and every emitted name has one and only one source word. This result holds at arbitrary finite depth and preserves the original executable functions on their broader raw input domains. Together with the unit, provenance, pair-support, observation, reconstruction and succession proofs and the complete 1,024-candidate program correspondence, it completes the registered quantum-information support entry.


Put H=[held-a,held-b]. Complete-support membership and the inherited Fold generator give the same condition,

\[
 w\in W_n(H)\iff |w|=n\ \land\ (\forall x\in w,\ x=\text{held-a}\ \lor\ x=\text{held-b}).
\]

To prove name injectivity, decode the name's bytes into characters. Each character of the fixed prefix, delimiter and held labels belongs to the explicit finite alphabet {h,e,l,d,-,a,b,:,s,i}; character-list induction proves exact decoding on that alphabet. Equality B(u)=B(v) therefore yields equality of their character lists. Cancelling the fixed “basis:” prefix leaves equality of the colon-joined label sequences.

For nonempty sequences, prefixing a colon produces blocks “:held-a” or “:held-b”, each of length seven. Their seventh characters distinguish the alternatives. Equality forces the same first label; cancelling the common seven-character block reduces to equality of the remaining blocks. Induction recovers the entire label sequence. The empty case is separated by the presence or absence of a first block. Hence

\[

131. Exact generated transition systems

A transition system retains the ordered generated state carrier, held action labels and source/action/target rows. Construction first checks state uniqueness, then action uniqueness and nonempty carriers; it then checks each row in order for carrier membership and repeated source/action coordinates. The relation may be partial. A requested step succeeds exactly when its matching target list is a singleton, preserving the original missing-transition boundary.

Execution first checks that the initial state belongs to the carrier, then retains that initial state and every successive generated target, propagating the first failed step. Native proofs identify successful execution exactly with an inductive chain of the original step results. Every admitted trace begins at its registered initial state, has one position for every action plus the initial position, and remains entirely within the state carrier. Constructor admission is equivalent to the exact original carrier and ordered-row conditions. 3,397 independent comparisons cover complete outputs and original errors, including duplicate states/actions, empty strings, missing transitions, repeated coordinates, escaped rows and failure order.


Write a system as (S,A,R), where each retained row is (s,a,t). Row admission requires s,t∈S and a∈A. Scanning the relation maintains the list K of previously seen (source,action) coordinates: an empty remainder succeeds; a head row succeeds only if it is carrier-bound and (s,a)∉K, after which validation continues with (s,a)::K. Together with distinct, nonempty S and A, this is exactly constructor admission, including its ordered failure behavior.

Define T_R(s,a)=[t:(s,a,t) occurs in R]. The executable step satisfies

\[
 \operatorname{step}(s,a)=\operatorname{ok}(t)\iff T_R(s,a)=[t].
\]

The retained execution relation has the two clauses

\[
 E(s,[],[s]),\qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{step}(s,a)=\operatorname{ok}(t)\quad E(t,u,\tau)}
 {E(s,a::u,s::\tau)}.
\]

Induction on the requested action list proves runFrom(s,u)=ok(τ) iff E(s,u,τ), by matching each successful step and recursive result; either error branch propagates unchanged. The outer run additionally requires s∈S. Induction on E gives head(τ)=s and |τ|=|u|+1. Each successful step selects a retained row, whose validation gives its target in S. Starting with s∈S, the same induction therefore puts every trace state in S.

Every successful execution admits an exact decomposition into its retained predecessor positions and terminal state.  E(s,u,\tau)\iff\exists b,t,\ \tau=b\mathbin{++}[t]\ \land\ P(s,u,b,t).

134. Finite language derivation certificates

The language formation rules retain the empty construction frontier and append a held alphabet symbol at each finite successor. Native derivation trees are sound and complete for the exact generated word layer: a word belongs to that layer if and only if it has the corresponding finite derivation certificate. The certificate fixes its depth, admits only symbols in the generated alphabet and retains a recoverable predecessor at each successor. For the complete cumulative language output, membership is exactly the original empty-One marker or a positive-depth derivation bounded by the registered position trace. The marker and the empty host frontier remain distinct, and literal marker-valued alphabet symbols retain their original behavior. The shared native operation proofs and all three claim-specific witnesses combine with full 256-candidate program/output/hash agreement to complete the registered Fold Formal-Language and Grammar Law. The native finite certificate \(D_A(n,w)\) has precisely the source's seed and append clauses:

\[
 D_A(0,[]),\qquad
 \frac{D_A(n,w)\quad a\in A}{D_A(n+1,w\mathbin{++}[a])}.
\]

\[
 w\in W_n(A)\iff D_A(n,w),\qquad
 D_A(n,w)\Longrightarrow |w|=n\ \land\ \forall a\in w,\ a\in A.
\]

Every successor certificate therefore has a recoverable predecessor and final held symbol. Substituting this equivalence into cumulative-output membership gives w∈\(G_N\) iff w=[empty-One] or there exists 0<n≤N with \(D_A(n,w)\). This disjunction preserves literal marker-valued symbols in ordinary generated words as well as the distinguished initial marker.

For \(D_A(m,u)\) and \(D_A(n,v)\), induction on the second certificate proves \(D_A\)(m+n,u++v). The seed uses u++[]=u. Its append case applies one append to the induction hypothesis and reassociates (u++v)++[a]=u++(v++[a]). Thus concatenation retains the complete finite construction certificate at the summed depth.

137. Registered rewrite boundaries and trace classes

The finite relation of registered rewrite applications retains complete records, including rule identity, source word, selected position, replacement and successor. Admitted applications belong to this retained relation, have both endpoints in the generated carrier and replay the original exact rewrite operation. Every admitted application has an exact source-symbol occurrence at its held position, a source-word decomposition around that occurrence and the replacement at that same coordinate. Missing registrations and endpoints outside the generated carrier are excluded by the declared boundary; the raw executable helper keeps its original guards.

A terminal word has no admitted outgoing application. Consequently its retained traces are empty and it cannot begin a cyclic or branching trace. A cyclic trace retains a nonempty return path, which can be repeated by exact composition. A branching trace retains two admitted applications from the same word with distinct successors; each yields its own complete one-step trace. Identity, serial composition and one-record succession preserve the retained relation. Extending the registered application relation and generated carrier preserves all previous traces. These predicates formalise the declared finite trace classes; no claim of universal termination or confluence is introduced. Full 256-candidate native program agreement and the original three operational witnesses complete the registered Rewriting entry.


For registered records Q and carrier C, define A(r) by r∈Q, source(r)∈C, successor(r)∈C and exact replay. A retained trace additionally requires its initial word in C and A(r) for each record. \[
 P(s,u\mathbin{++}v,b,t)\iff\exists m,c,d,\ b=c\mathbin{++}d\ \land P(s,u,c,m)\ \land P(m,v,d,t).

If D_n⊆E_n for each n, completeness of E restricts to completeness of D by membership inclusion. These equations preserve the exact scope of the finite samples, declared domains and supplied induction certificates.

 P(s,u,b,t)\Longrightarrow\exists R,\ Inverse(t,R,s)\land |R|=|u|.
\]

The undo operation checks \(current=row.target\) and that the original source step reaches row.target, then recurses from row.source. Its resource trace is t::map(source,R), so map-length preservation gives \(timeCount=|R|+1\) while the original ledger retains occupied support unchanged.

The quantifiers range over an arbitrary system, initial state and action list. The empty path gives an empty inverse. For a successor, first reverse the remaining path, then append its original head transition as a predecessor row. Consequently an execution with action list \(A\) constructs an executable inverse with exactly \(|A|\) rows, independently of the lengths used in the source-comparison census. 164. Independent and causally layered work

The native ready-set construction retains exactly the declared tasks not yet completed whose incoming predecessors are all completed. This condition proves that simultaneous ready tasks have no dependency edge between them. The original ordered-selection generator exhausts every layer choice over that ready set. Readiness is the exact predicate

\[
 Ready(D,x)\iff x\in nodes\land x\notin D\land
 \forall p,\ (p,x)\in edges\Longrightarrow p\in D.
\]

Boolean conjunction and edge-list membership establish equivalence with the executable ready test; filtering the node carrier therefore gives exactly Ready. If x and y are ready and (x,y) is an edge, readiness of y forces \(x∈D\), contradicting readiness of x. Ordered selections of this complete ready set enumerate every declared layer choice. Synchronization filtering retains exactly original edges whose target lies in the layer, so each predecessor belongs to D.

A layer schedule has identity result D and successor state \(D++layer\). Induction gives \(result=D++flatten(layers)\). The same induction proves serial schedule composition, and list concatenation gives \(flatten(L++K)=flatten(L)++flatten(K)\). A new admitted layer appends its complete work without changing previous rows. Starting from \(D=[]\), declared result coverage transfers directly to the flattened work trace, without requiring execution order to equal node-carrier order. \]

a contradiction. A lower certificate supplies such a pair for each declared model whose measured cost is below B. For stage records R, define \(trace([])=[]\), \(trace(r::R)=r.observed\mathbin{++}trace(R)\), \(cost([])=0\) and \(cost(r::R)=r.timeCount+cost(R)\). Induction substitutes each verified \(r.timeCount=|r.observed|\) and obtains

\[
 cost(R)=|trace(R)|,\quad
 trace(L\mathbin{++}R)=trace(L)\mathbin{++}trace(R),\quad

\]

A reduction chain is identity or a verified first reduction followed by another chain. Membership in fresh::I splits the obligation into Chain(fresh,t) and Hard(I,t). Identity therefore supplies completeness for the singleton inventory.

For any registry \(\mathcal R\), resource predicate \(L\), problem inventory \(I\) and target \(t\), the precise completeness judgment is
\[
 \operatorname{Complete}_{\mathcal R,L}(I,t)
 \iff t\in I\land\forall p\in I,\ \operatorname{Chain}_{\mathcal R,L}(p,t).
\]
A chain is generated by identity and by a verified reduction followed by a chain. Induction on the first chain proves composition. Enlarging the inventory has the exact obligation
\[
 \operatorname{Hard}_{\mathcal R,L}(p::I,t)
 \iff\operatorname{Chain}_{\mathcal R,L}(p,t)
       \land\operatorname{Hard}_{\mathcal R,L}(I,t).
\]
Hence arbitrary finite inventories are supported, while each added problem contributes its own retained reduction chain under the same resource predicate. 180. Causally independent algorithm layers

Every task in an admitted ready layer reads the same prior retained result table. The dependency graph places each prerequisite before the layer and excludes dependencies between simultaneous tasks. Let \(B\) be the retained result table and \(L=[(k_i,d_i)]_{i=1}^m\) a layer of task identities and dependency lists. The source execution reads every dependency list against the same \(B\):
\[
 \operatorname{layerRun}(R,B,[]) = \operatorname{some}[],
 \qquad
 \operatorname{layerRun}(R,B,(k,d)::L)
 =\operatorname{some}((k,v)::W)
\]
precisely when \(\operatorname{inputs}(B,d)=\operatorname{some}u\), the selected recurrence gives \(\operatorname{result}(R,k,u)=\operatorname{some}v\), and \(\operatorname{layerRun}(R,B,L)=\operatorname{some}W\). A failed read or recurrence produces failure. Thus earlier rows in the same layer never become inputs to its later tasks. The native reconstruction and identity statements are
\[
 \operatorname{layerRun}(R,B,L)=\operatorname{some}W
 \iff \operatorname{LayerExecution}(R,B,L,W),\qquad
 \operatorname{ids}(W)=\operatorname{ids}(L),\quad |W|=|L|.
\]
For an admitted ready layer, every graph prerequisite belongs to \(\operatorname{ids}(B)\), and no edge joins two tasks in that layer. Under the retained local-rule hypothesis, validated dependency values imply a validated recurrence result; induction over the layer then validates every row of \(W\). Instantiating this implication with the source derivation property reconstructs each result's derivation.

Writing \(E(B,\mathcal L)\) for execution of successive layers, its equations are
\[
 E(B,[])=\operatorname{some}B,\qquad
 E(B,L::\mathcal L)=E(B\mathbin{+\!\!+}W,\mathcal L)
 \quad\text{when }\operatorname{layerRun}(R,B,L)=\operatorname{some}W.
\]
The scheduled trace retains readiness at each intermediate table. Induction gives
\[
 \operatorname{ids}(B_{\rm final})
 =\operatorname{ids}(B_{\rm initial})
   \mathbin{+\!\!+}\operatorname{flatten}([\operatorname{ids}(L):L\in\mathcal L]).
\]
With an empty initial table, coverage of final node identities therefore yields coverage by the flattened work trace. The same layer induction propagates complete derivations, while concatenation of executions uses their shared retained table.

181. Global replay of retained local process events

A retained event identifies its process, prior local state, action and resulting local state. The replay checker resolves the registered process kernel and verifies the unchanged local transition before updating that process in the global state table. Native certificates and successful replay imply one another for every finite event trace. Process identities are preserved, and every process absent from the trace retains its original local state. Serial composition and successor extension reconstruct through the shared intermediate state. These results establish the local-state replay component; the message and causal/fault certificates below complete its connection to distributed communication.


Write an event as \(e=(\iota,p,b,a,c)\), with identity \(\iota\), process \(p\), prior state \(b\), action \(a\), and resulting state \(c\). For registry \(K\) and store \(S\), the exact successful replay condition is
\[
\begin{gathered}
 \operatorname{replayEvent}(K,S,e)=\operatorname{some}S'
 \iff \exists M:\\
 \begin{aligned}
 &\operatorname{lookupFirst}(K,p)=\operatorname{some}M\\
 &\land\operatorname{lookupFirst}(S,p)=\operatorname{some}b\\
 &\land\operatorname{step}(M,b,a)=\operatorname{ok}c\\
 &\land S'=\operatorname{update}(S,p,c).
 \end{aligned}
\end{gathered}
\]
Here update preserves the store's list structure and replaces the value of every row whose process identity equals \(p\); lookup retains the original first-match convention. A missing process, wrong prior state, transition error, or mismatched resulting state rejects the event.

The full trace is generated by identity and successor rules:
\[
 \operatorname{GlobalTrace}(K,S,[],S),\qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{LocalStep}(K,S,e)\quad
       \operatorname{GlobalTrace}(K,\operatorname{update}(S,p,c),T,F)}
      {\operatorname{GlobalTrace}(K,S,e::T,F)}.
\]
Induction in both directions establishes
\[
 \operatorname{replay}(K,S,T)=\operatorname{some}F
 \iff\operatorname{GlobalTrace}(K,S,T,F),\qquad
 \operatorname{ids}(F)=\operatorname{ids}(S).
\]
If \(q\ne e.p\) for every event \(e\in T\), each update preserves its lookup, hence
\[
 \operatorname{lookupFirst}(F,q)=\operatorname{lookupFirst}(S,q).
\]
Two traces from \(S\) to \(M\) and from \(M\) to \(F\) compose into their concatenation from \(S\) to \(F\); the successor case is the corresponding one-event extension.

Source, proof and provenance: [V3 DISTRIBUTED](https://github.com/MettaMazza/ernos-labs-sft-platform/blob/76f1b34e9e9682989adcbb088797b4ae4ce4fcf1/sft/computation/spec_data.py#L105); [V3 structural_recursion](https://github.com/MettaMazza/ernos-labs-sft-platform/blob/76f1b34e9e9682989adcbb088797b4ae4ce4fcf1/sft/computation/operations.py#L85-L92); [V3 run](https://github.com/MettaMazza/ernos-labs-sft-platform/blob/76f1b34e9e9682989adcbb088797b4ae4ce4fcf1/sft/computation/operations.py#L51-L59); [SFT.Computation.DistributedReplay.globalReplay](https://github.com/MettaMazza/SFT-v4-LEAN-VERIFIED/blob/59172eee89576735796ec396f85e8527f0744130/SFT/Computation/DistributedReplay.lean#L133-L139); [SFT.Computation.DistributedReplay.globalDerivation](https://github.com/MettaMazza/SFT-v4-LEAN-VERIFIED/blob/59172eee89576735796ec396f85e8527f0744130/SFT/Computation/DistributedReplay.lean#L140-L153); [Timeline: Turn 235, line 2440](https://github.com/MettaMazza/SFT-v4-LEAN-VERIFIED/blob/59172eee89576735796ec396f85e8527f0744130/TIMELINE.txt#L2440-L2445).

182. Exact distributed messages and causal reconstruction

Separate send and receive ledgers retain each message identity, payload, process and event identity. Every record binds to the registered alphabet and an actual process event. Every declared receipt has a retained send with the same message identity and payload at an earlier event position. Sends without a declared receipt remain visible; delivery is not assumed. Canonical event identities and exact positions make the causal relation transitive and irreflexive, excluding causal return cycles.

An original local transition error prevents global replay from continuing to a result. A completed certificate combines the full local-state trace, canonical event identities and verified message ledger, reconstructing the terminal global state while preserving all process identities. Trace extension retains prior port bindings and causal decisions; ledger composition retains both complete record collections. System implementation and physical network claims remain outside the formal theorem. All 256 original candidates, witnesses and complete native program fields and hashes agree with pinned V3, completing the Fold Distributed-Algorithm Law.


For a port \(r=(m,\iota,p,v)\), let \(A\) be the payload alphabet and \(T\) the event list. The binding and causal predicates have the exact meanings
\[
 \operatorname{bound}(A,T,r)
 \iff v\in A\land\exists e\in T,\ e.\iota=\iota\land e.p=p,
\]
\[
 \operatorname{before}_T(x,y)
 \iff \exists i,j,\ 
 \operatorname{scan}(x,\operatorname{ids}(T))=\operatorname{some}i
 \land\operatorname{scan}(y,\operatorname{ids}(T))=\operatorname{some}j
 \land i<j.
\]
Scan uses the source's first matching position. For send ledger \(S\) and receipt ledger \(R\), validity is exactly
\[
 \bigl(\forall s\in S,\operatorname{bound}(A,T,s)\bigr)
 \land\bigl(\forall r\in R,\operatorname{bound}(A,T,r)\bigr)
 \land\bigl(\forall r\in R,\exists s\in S,\
 s.m=r.m\land s.v=r.v\land\operatorname{before}_T(s.\iota,r.\iota)\bigr).
\]
This quantifies over every receipt without requiring every send to have a receipt. An unpaired receipt contradicts the final conjunct. Determinacy of scan identifies the middle index in two causal comparisons, so \(i<j\) and \(j<k\) give \(i<k\); \(i<i\) is impossible. These establish transitivity, absence of self-cause, and absence of causal return.

The complete certificate conjoins distinct event identities, the global local-state trace, and this message-ledger validity:
\[
 C=\operatorname{Distinct}(\operatorname{ids}(T))
 \land\operatorname{GlobalTrace}(K,I,T,F)
 \land\operatorname{valid}(A,T,S,R).
\]
Consequently \(C\) implies \(\operatorname{replay}(K,I,T)=\operatorname{some}F\) and \(\operatorname{ids}(F)=\operatorname{ids}(I)\). Under the registered-machine and current-state premises, a local transition error yields a failed event replay, which yields failed replay for the trace beginning with that event. Appending events preserves existing bindings and successful scan positions; therefore it preserves this ledger's validity. Two valid send/receipt ledgers over the same event list compose by list concatenation, retaining witnesses from their respective original ledgers.

Source, proof and provenance: [V3 DISTRIBUTED](https://github.com/MettaMazza/ernos-labs-sft-platform/blob/76f1b34e9e9682989adcbb088797b4ae4ce4fcf1/sft/computation/spec_data.py#L105); [V3 structural_recursion](https://github.com/MettaMazza/ernos-labs-sft-platform/blob/76f1b34e9e9682989adcbb088797b4ae4ce4fcf1/sft/computation/operations.py#L85-L92); [V3 run](https://github.com/MettaMazza/ernos-labs-sft-platform/blob/76f1b34e9e9682989adcbb088797b4ae4ce4fcf1/sft/computation/operations.py#L51-L59); [SFT.Computation.DistributedMessages.completeReceiptProvenance](https://github.com/MettaMazza/SFT-v4-LEAN-VERIFIED/blob/59172eee89576735796ec396f85e8527f0744130/SFT/Computation/DistributedMessages.lean#L76-L85); [SFT.Computation.DistributedMessages.noCausalReturn](https://github.com/MettaMazza/SFT-v4-LEAN-VERIFIED/blob/59172eee89576735796ec396f85e8527f0744130/SFT/Computation/DistributedMessages.lean#L118-L121); [Timeline: Turn 235, line 2440](https://github.com/MettaMazza/SFT-v4-LEAN-VERIFIED/blob/59172eee89576735796ec396f85e8527f0744130/TIMELINE.txt#L2440-L2445).

183. Finite-prefix streaming and retained distinctions

Every generated input has a complete ordered prefix family, including its identity prefix. Native proofs establish both directions between prefix membership and exact input decomposition, giving one result record per prefix and a total of input length plus one records. Each successful result reconstructs its complete original execution path and terminal state summary. The original transition relation determines the next summary, and serial continuation uses the retained intermediate state.

The full ordered pair ledger retains exactly distinct supported inputs whose state summaries coincide. Inputs with different summaries are excluded from that loss ledger. Input extension preserves every earlier prefix, output and lost-distinction record. Each resource certificate retains the complete observation trace and supplied occupied support with their exact counts. The prefix and output theorems quantify over every finite input and every finite appended segment. All 256 original candidates, witnesses and complete native program fields and hashes agree with pinned V3, completing the Fold Online and Streaming Algorithm Law.


For a finite input \(x\), the complete ordered prefix list is defined recursively:
\[
 P([])=[[]],\qquad P(a::x)=[]::[a::p:p\in P(x)].
\]
Induction proves both its exact boundary and its count:
\[
 p\in P(x)\iff\exists s,\ x=p\mathbin{+\!\!+}s,\qquad |P(x)|=|x|+1.
\]
The output ledger is \(O(x)=[(p,\operatorname{run}(M,i,p)):p\in P(x)]\), so it retains exactly the original run for each prefix and has \(|x|+1\) rows. Its summary is
\[
 \sigma(p)=
 \begin{cases}
 \operatorname{failed}(r),&\operatorname{run}(M,i,p)=\operatorname{error}r,\\
 \operatorname{returned}(\operatorname{endLabel}(t)),
       &\operatorname{run}(M,i,p)=\operatorname{ok}t.
 \end{cases}
\]
For every successful prefix, native path reconstruction gives \(x=p\mathbin{+\!\!+}s\), \(t=b\mathbin{+\!\!+}[q]\), the original path from \(i\) through \(p\) to \(q\), and \(\sigma(p)=\operatorname{returned}(\operatorname{some}q)\). If that path extends by \(\operatorname{step}(M,q,a)=\operatorname{ok}q'\), with the original initial-state admissibility, then
\[
 \sigma(p\mathbin{+\!\!+}[a])=\operatorname{returned}(\operatorname{some}q').
\]
Serial path composition gives the corresponding statement for an arbitrary admitted continuation.

For supplied finite support \(U\), form the full ordered product list \(U\times U\), retaining its source ordering and multiplicities, then filter it:
\[
 L(U)=\operatorname{filter}_{u\ne v\ \land\ \sigma(u)=\sigma(v)}(U\times U).
\]
The exact membership theorem is
\[
 (u,v)\in L(U)\iff
 u\in U\land v\in U\land u\ne v\land\sigma(u)=\sigma(v).
\]
Different summaries therefore exclude a pair. Since every old prefix remains a prefix after appending input, old output rows and pairs in \(L(P(x))\) remain in the extended ledgers. Finally, for a successful run and its accepted resource record with supplied occupied support \(H\),
\[
 \operatorname{map}(\operatorname{snd},\ell.\operatorname{timeTrace})=t,\quad
 \ell.\operatorname{spaceSupport}=H,\quad
 \ell.\operatorname{timeCount}=|p|+1,\quad
 \ell.\operatorname{spaceCount}=|H|.
\]
These equations retain the full finite observation trace as well as the exact support supplied to the recorder.

For arbitrary finite lists \(x,z\), a previous prefix decomposition \(x=p{+\!\!+}s\) gives
\[
 x{+\!\!+}z=p{+\!\!+}(s{+\!\!+}z).
\]
The complete prefix-membership theorem therefore retains \(p\), and the output-membership theorem retains exactly \((p,\operatorname{run}(M,i,p))\). This proves extension for any segment length; each execution still computes the finite prefix list supplied to it. 184. Exact oriented numerical-error records

For equal nonempty finite supports of exact positive fractions, the numerical error ledger retains one ordered cell record per paired input. Equal values carry the structural One marker and the equal orientation; unequal values carry their exact positive difference and the held-below or held-above orientation. Native arithmetic proofs identify each normalized difference by its cross-multiplied rational value. Nonpositive values and unequal or empty supports retain the original rejection behavior. These results establish the error-ledger component of the numerical formalisation.


For reference \(x=n_x/d_x>0\) and approximation \(y=n_y/d_y>0\), define the exact cross-products
\[
 A=n_y d_x,\qquad E=n_x d_y,\qquad D=d_xd_y>0.
\]
The source error operation is the following oriented positive-part record:
\[
 \operatorname{err}(x,y)=
 \begin{cases}
 (1,\text{equal}),&A=E,\\
 (\operatorname{normalizePositive}(E-A,D),\text{held-below}),&A<E,\\
 (\operatorname{normalizePositive}(A-E,D),\text{held-above}),&E<A.
 \end{cases}
\]
The equal case deliberately retains the structural One marker. For either unequal branch, with positive difference numerator \(\Delta\) and normalized result \(n/d\), preservation of exact value is proved by
\[
 \Delta d=nD,\qquad n>0.
\]
Thus normalization retains the exact rational difference and the orientation separately. The ordered row operation starts at index \(1\), emits \((\text{cell-}i,\operatorname{err}(x_i,y_i))\), and recurses at \(i+1\). Its outer admission guard is
\[
 |X|=|Y|\ \land\ X\ne[],
\]
while each paired element must have the positive constructor. A zero or negative constructor rejects the scientific value; a length mismatch or empty reference rejects the support. These are distinct original error branches, not numerical tolerances.

185. Complete numerical error-ledger reconstruction

Successful numerical error-ledger execution is equivalent to a complete ordered certificate pairing each reference value with its approximation and exact oriented row. The certificate proves positivity of both input supports and every error value, equal support lengths, and one row per pair without omission. Conversely, every equal-length nonempty pair of positive supports constructs a successful ledger. Serial composition and successor extension preserve earlier rows while advancing the original cell labels. Independent finite expression comparisons exercise all 1,849 pairs of supports of widths up to two over six exact signed/zero/positive test values; their output and rejection records agree with native Lean execution.


Let \(\mathcal R_i(X,Y,L)\) denote the retained ordered row certificate. Its constructors are
\[
 \mathcal R_i([],[],[]),\qquad
 \frac{\mathcal R_{i+1}(X,Y,L)}
 {\mathcal R_i(x::X,y::Y,(\text{cell-}i,\operatorname{err}(x,y))::L)}
 \quad(x,y\text{ positive}).
\]
Structural induction on these constructors reproduces the executable row operation. Conversely, inspection of each successful executable branch constructs the corresponding certificate. Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{rowsFrom}(i,X,Y)=\operatorname{ok}L
 \iff\mathcal R_i(X,Y,L),
\]
\[
 \operatorname{exactErrorLedger}(X,Y)=\operatorname{ok}L
 \iff X\ne[]\land\mathcal R_1(X,Y,L).
\]
Induction gives positivity of both supports and every error numerator, together with
\[
 |L|=|X|=|Y|.
\]
Each row retains its paired positive values, index label, and exact error operation. Conversely, the recursively generated positive-row list provides a certificate for any two equal-length positive supports; nonemptiness then gives outer ledger admission.

For concatenated supports, the second certificate begins at the advanced cell index:
\[
 \mathcal R_i(X,Y,L)\land
 \mathcal R_{i+|X|}(X',Y',L')
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 \mathcal R_i(X\mathbin{+\!\!+}X',Y\mathbin{+\!\!+}Y',L\mathbin{+\!\!+}L').
\]
Taking the second pair of supports to be singletons proves successor extension with label \(\text{cell-}(i+|X|)\). The finite comparison family uses \(1+6+6^2=43\) supports, including the empty support, so its complete ordered pair family has \(43^2=1,849\) cases. Rejected supports and signed or zero elements remain part of that comparison.

186. Retained numerical update observations

Every state in a generated update trace resolves to its registered numerical carrier and a complete exact error ledger. The observation checker and the retained certificate imply one another; the ordered projection reproduces the entire state trace, and every numerical value is traced to its registered carrier row. Connecting these records to the original transition execution gives exactly one observation for each action plus the initial state. Composition retains all intermediate records. An admitted successor step appends its exact observation while preserving the earlier trace. Missing carrier values or rejected error ledgers cannot produce an accepted observation trace.


Let \(T\) be the registered state-to-value table and \(X\) the fixed reference support. The numerical observation recursion is
\[
 N(T,X,[])=\operatorname{some}[],
\]
\[
 N(T,X,s::S)=\operatorname{some}((s,Y,L)::Q)
\]
exactly when
\[
 \operatorname{lookupFirst}(T,s)=\operatorname{some}Y,\qquad
 \operatorname{exactErrorLedger}(X,Y)=\operatorname{ok}L,\qquad
 N(T,X,S)=\operatorname{some}Q.
\]
Missing lookups, rejected ledgers, and failed suffix observations propagate failure. The corresponding inductive certificate retains these three witnesses at every row. Reconstruction and replay prove
\[
 N(T,X,S)=\operatorname{some}Q
 \iff\operatorname{Records}(T,X,S,Q).
\]
Induction then yields
\[
 \operatorname{map}(\operatorname{fst},Q)=S,\qquad |Q|=|S|,
\]
and for every \((s,Y,L)\in Q\), the registered row \((s,Y)\in T\), nonempty reference, and full certificate \(\mathcal R_1(X,Y,L)\).

If the original state execution satisfies \(\operatorname{run}(M,i,a)=\operatorname{ok}S\), its path theorem gives \(|S|=|a|+1\). Combining this equality with the observation count gives
\[
 |Q|=|a|+1.
\]
An admitted transition from the retained terminal state to \(s'\), its registered value \(Y'\), and accepted error ledger \(L'\) extend both executions:
\[
 S'=S\mathbin{+\!\!+}[s'],\qquad
 Q'=Q\mathbin{+\!\!+}[(s',Y',L')].
\]
The earlier records remain intact. Concatenation of observation certificates follows directly by induction over the first certificate.
