The complete binary part support contains \(1/2\) and One. Self-pairing to One selects only \(1/2\), and the general positive-part theorem strengthens this to
\[
 \operatorname{selfJunction}(p)=\mathrm{One}\iff p=\tfrac12.
\]
The same part is its own complement and folds to One. For positive depth \(k\), let \(N=2^k\). The complete spectrum is
\[
 p_i=\frac{2i+1}{2N},\qquad 0\le i<N.
\]
Normalization retains the cross-product identity with this raw fraction. Since \(0<2i+1<2N\), every level is in the positive unit domain. Equal normalized levels imply equal raw numerators and hence equal indices, proving injectivity.

The successor doubles support and denominator. Writing \(n_i=2i+1\), its paired numerators satisfy
\[
 n_{2i}=2n_i-1,\qquad n_{2i+1}=2n_i+1,
\]
so the two successor values are
\[
 p'_{2i}=p_i-\frac1{4N},\qquad
 p'_{2i+1}=p_i+\frac1{4N}.
\]
Adjacent raw numerators differ by two, and complete cardinality is \(2^k\) at every generated depth.

The source grammar tests carrier, dependency, relation, enumeration, minimality, measurement, record and extension. Its ordered coordinate product has \(2^{8}=256\) forms. The half-One uniqueness and successor spectrum identities above supply the relation coordinate; the remaining coordinates retain its dependency trace, full enumeration, omission controls, seal and source records. Write \(D_i\) for each ordered source coordinate list and \(c_i^*\) for its admitted value. The nested product construction and acceptance predicate give
\[
G=\prod_{i=1}^{8}D_i,\qquad
c\in G\iff\bigwedge_{i=1}^{8}(c_i\in D_i),\qquad
|G|=\prod_{i=1}^{8}|D_i|=2^8,
\]
\[
A(c)\iff\bigwedge_{i=1}^{8}(c_i=c_i^*)\iff c=c^*.
\]

323. Exact Fold return and binary multiplicative order

For q>0, let h_q(x) be the held representative of x modulo q: h_q(x)=x mod q when that remainder is nonzero, and h_q(x)=q otherwise. The executed recurrence is
\[
r_0=p,  r_{k+1}=h_q(2r_k)
\]
Induction gives r_k ≡ p·2^k (mod q): the initial step is p≡p·1, and doubling the induction identity gives r_(k+1)≡2p·2^k=p·2^(k+1). For a reduced input, gcd(p,q)=1. Because held representatives are unique in {1,…,q},
\[
r_k=p \iff  p\cdot 2^k\equiv p \pmod{q}
\]
\[
\iff  q\text{ divides }p(2^k-1)
\]
\[
\iff  q\text{ divides }2^k-1
\]
\[
\iff  2^k\equiv 1 \pmod{q}
\]
The cancellation uses gcd(p,q)=1. Taking the least positive k on both sides identifies first Fold return with first binary multiplicative order whenever that return exists. For odd q>1, existence follows from the finite-carrier argument below; the even-denominator transient is treated separately.

For every supplied positive reduced part p/q through the One, native repeated double-and-cast execution satisfies rank_k modulo q = p times 2^k modulo q. The complete-denominator representative is retained when a remainder vanishes. Reducedness permits cancellation of p: an exact return to the original held rank occurs if and only if 2^k modulo q equals 1 modulo q. The first-positive-return and first-positive-order predicates therefore have the same least index. These identities hold at arbitrary supplied finite depth; they do not use a bounded prime list. All 25 definitions and supporting theorems have zero Lean axiom dependencies.

Successful finite witness replays preserve the original order-loop and orbit-loop guard, update and stopping branches. The native correspondence proofs connect returned replay records to those source loop relations. An unfinished replay cannot pass a witness; its internal execution budget supplies no scientific value or survivor selector.

324. Counted binary transient and complete orbit support

Let the supplied reduced denominator be 2^a times an odd positive core m. Native execution has reduced denominator m at depth a and at every later depth. Before that depth, at depth k with a=k+r and positive r, its denominator is exactly 2^r times m and is even. Thus a is exactly the first depth with an odd denominator. Write D_k for the denominator of the actual normalized executed state, with q=2^a m and gcd(p,q)=1. Remainder preservation and normalization give
\[
 D_k=\frac{q}{\gcd(p2^k,q)}
 =\begin{cases}
  2^{a-k}m,&k<a,\\
  m,&k\ge a.
 \end{cases}
\]
For k<a, removing the shared binary power leaves gcd(p,2^(a−k)m)=1, so the removed common divisor is exactly 2^k. At k=a+j, oddness of m makes gcd(2^j,m)=1, so the removed divisor remains exactly 2^a. The first case is even and the second odd. This proves the exact first odd-denominator depth a for the executed states, including the complete-denominator representative.

If ℓ is the first positive binary return, an equality r_i=r_j at 0≤i<j<ℓ cancels the reduced starting rank and the invertible power 2^i modulo the odd denominator, giving 2^(j−i)≡1. This contradicts minimality of ℓ. Consequently the full list [r_0,…,r_(ℓ−1)] has ℓ distinct positions and r_(k+ℓ)=r_k for every finite k.

325. Complete cyclotomic counting and source-loop termination

For odd q>1, gcd(2,q)=1. If two powers at indices i<j have the same residue, cancellation of 2^i gives 2^(j−i)≡1 (mod q). The q+1 residues at indices 0,…,q cannot all be distinct in a carrier of q residues, so a positive return exists. Let ℓ be the least such index. For a reduced starting rank p, an equality r_i=r_j with 0≤i<j<ℓ would imply 2^(j−i)≡1, contradicting minimality. Hence its complete cycle C(p) has exactly ℓ members.

For any cycles C(p), C(s), suppose r_i(p)=r_j(s). Each cycle has period ℓ, so advancing within the cycle by the complementary index ℓ−j expresses s as an iterate of p. The same reasoning expresses p as an iterate of s. Thus C(p)=C(s). Every reduced rank lies in its own cycle, and distinct cycles are disjoint. If R_q={r:1≤r<q, gcd(r,q)=1} and C is the number of cycles, successive removal of complete cycles therefore gives
\[
|R_q| = \ell  C
\]
For prime q, each 1≤r<q is coprime to q, so |R_q|=q−1 and
  q−1 = ℓ C, hence ℓ divides q−1.
This is a finite partition derivation for each admitted denominator, independent of the finite witness table.

For every admitted odd denominator above the One, the finite carrier forces a first binary return. If no return occurred through the carrier bound, one more executed position than there are held ranks would have to remain distinct, contradicting the exact finite count. The original order loop therefore terminates, and its returned count is the first binary multiplicative order. For every reduced numerator, the original orbit loop returns a complete ordered trace of exactly this length.

The executed cycles preserve reducedness. Two cycles that share a rank have identical members; every reduced rank belongs to its own cycle. Removing complete cycles successively from the full reduced-residue support proves that the residue count equals orbit length times orbit count. For a prime denominator, every positive rank below the prime is reduced, so the period divides one less than the prime. These are arbitrary supplied finite-denominator results, not conclusions extrapolated from the witness census.

The orbit loop also terminates for positive held parts with even denominators: each fresh step adds a distinct held rank, and the finite carrier bounds the number of additions before repetition. Combined with the counted binary-depth result, this retains the transient prefix before the odd recurrent core. 327. Exact positive-ratio composition

Let N(a,b) denote division of a positive numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor. Its normalized pair (u,v) satisfies av=ub. For an arbitrary reduced positive ratio x=(n,d), define its reciprocal y=N(d,n) and composition x·y=N(ny_n,dy_d). Value preservation for y gives dy_d=y_n n=ny_n. The composite therefore has equal positive raw numerator and denominator, and normalization gives (1,1). Every admitted positive ratio composed with its reciprocal returns the One, including ratios above the One.

For positive counts a,b,c, the raw product of the views a/b and b/c is N(ab,bc)=(u,v). Value preservation gives abv=ubc. Associativity and commutativity place the common positive factor b on the same side; applying finite division by b and the identity (bk)/b=k gives av=uc. Thus this composite represents a/c exactly. For any positive m, the raw product of m/1 and 1/m is (m·1,1·m); commutativity makes the sides equal, and normalization yields (1,1). This reconstructs the One from m corresponding equal parts.

These native component results have thirteen audited definitions and theorems with zero axiom dependencies. The full source entry additionally includes shorter separation, complement, local transport and finite-family cycle composition.

The same telescoping law holds for actual composition after normalizing both input views. Let x=N(a,b), y=N(c,d), and z=compose(x,y). Value preservation gives ax_d=x_n b, cy_d=y_n d, and (x_n y_n)z_d=z_n(x_d y_d). Put e=x_d y_d>0. Multiplying and rearranging the first two identities gives (ac)e=(x_n y_n)(bd). Multiplication by z_d and substitution of the third identity therefore yield e(ac z_d)=e(z_n bd). Exact positive cancellation gives ac z_d=z_n bd. Specializing the second view to N(b,c) gives ab z_d=z_n bc; cancellation of b gives a z_d=z_n c. Thus normalization of either input and the composite preserves the telescoping relation itself.

328. Unique positive holding complement

For a generated count m>1, write m=k+2 and define h=N(k+1,k+2), the exact (m−1)-of-m part. A positive ratio x=n/d is the holding complement of the equal part 1/m precisely when x+1/m=1. Clearing the positive denominator dm gives the entirely positive-side equation
\[
nm+d=dm
\]
Expanding dm=d(k+1)+d and removing the same terminal d from both sides forces nm=(k+1)d. Normalization of h gives h_n m=(k+1)h_d, so h satisfies the holding equation. If any other positive ratio x satisfies it, multiply its forced equality by h_d and the equality for h by d. Rearranging gives m(nh_d)=m(h_n d). Cancellation by positive m yields nh_d=h_n d, establishing uniqueness of the exact rational value. At m=2, h=N(1,2)=(1,2), the half-One witness. The condition m>1 is precisely the positive-complement domain: at m=1 the holding equation would require n+d=d, which admits no positive numerator. These seven native definitions and theorems have zero axiom dependencies; the source entry's other relation and cycle requirements remain separate.

330. Positive local separation before casting

After a common finite refinement, let the held ordered positions be l/d and u/d, where 0<l<u≤d. Their positive directed gap is N(u−l,d). \]
Normalizing the two equal positive numerators against the same denominator gives identical positive Fraction objects. For the resulting transported pair (t_n,t_d),
\[
2(u-l)t_d=t_n d
\]
Thus the uncast local gap transports by the generated binary factor. This statement concerns the local gap before whole-turn casting; it does not identify every directed gap with the shorter circular separation or omit a change of cast branch. The component's seven audited declarations have no axiom dependencies.

If d<2l, then d<2u and both doubled numerators are at most 2d. Casting therefore removes exactly d from each. The retained difference is (2u−d)−(2l−d)=2u−2l=2(u−l). The shared-removal identity follows by restoring d to both retained numerators and cancelling the common added term. 331. Least common return of every positive finite cycle family

For supplied positive periods a,b, let g=gcd(a,b). The actual native least-common-multiple operation is L=ab/g. Since g divides both a and b, exact division yields L=a(b/g)=b(a/g). Thus a divides L, b divides L, and L>0. Also gL=ab.

To prove minimality, let c>0 be any shared return, so a divides c and b divides c. Then ab divides both ac and bc. The constructive greatest-common-divisor property gives ab dividing gcd(ac,bc). Positive scaling gives gcd(ac,bc)=c·gcd(a,b)=cg. Therefore cg=abk=gLk for a finite count k. Cancelling the positive g gives c=Lk, so L divides every positive shared return and L≤c. This establishes the first common return, not merely one common multiple.

For a nonempty supplied finite family, retain its first period p and the remaining finite list P. Define J(p,[])=p and J(p,q::P)=J(lcm(p,q),P). Induction proves positivity and the exact characterization, for every positive n,
  J(p,P) divides n ⇔ p divides n and every period in P divides n.
The empty-tail case is the single cycle. At a successor, divisibility by lcm(p,q) is equivalent to simultaneous divisibility by p and q, by the two-period result; the induction hypothesis handles the remaining list. Applying the characterization to n=J(p,P) shows that every supplied period returns there. Applying it to any other positive shared return n shows J(p,P) divides n and hence J(p,P)≤n. The original witness is J(2,[3,4])=12. All sixteen native definitions and theorems in this derivation have zero axiom dependencies; the construction uses no completed infinite family or fixed period table.

335. Exact finite-difference identities

Put q=2^k and h=1/q at a positive generated depth k. For the centered quadratic construction, clearing the denominator q² gives
\[
(q+1)^{2}+(q-1)^{2}=2q^{2}+2
\]
Thus (1+h)²+(1−h)²=2+2h², and the centered second difference divided by h² is exactly 2. The native proof establishes the denominator identity for q=m+1 by distributivity and exact addition; it is not inferred from the finite witness list.

For the forward cubic construction, clearing q³ gives
\[
(q+2)^{3}+q^{3}=2(q+1)^{3}+6q+6
\]
Equivalently (1+2h)³+1=2(1+h)³+6h²+6h³. Its forward second difference divided by h² is therefore 6+6h, with exact positive error E_k=6/2^k. The native error carrier is the normalized positive fraction N(6,2^k); its numerator and denominator satisfy 6E_d=E_n2^k. The denominator successor is 2^(k+1)=2^k+2^k. These seven audited component declarations have zero axiom dependencies.

For normalized E_k=(a_n,a_d) and E_(k+1)=(b_n,b_d), value preservation gives 6a_d=a_n2^k and 6b_d=b_n(2^k+2^k). Multiplying these identities by the opposite denominators and cancelling the positive 2^k yields (b_n+b_n)a_d=a_n b_d. Therefore 2E_(k+1)=E_k exactly. Since b_n a_d>0, it follows that b_n a_d<a_n b_d, proving strict decrease in the actual normalized representation.

338. Complete finite traces and the typed object boundary

344. General odd-denominator vacuum recurrence

For any supplied denominator q > 1 with q mod 2 = 1, let r_k be the held rank obtained after k executions of the original binary Fold from unit rank r_0 = 1. The existing exact rank calculation gives

\[
 0<r_k\le q,\qquad r_k\equiv 2^k\pmod q,\qquad
 \gcd(r_k,q)=1.
\]

The first inequality follows from the positive held-rank transition. Reducedness follows from gcd(1,q) = 1 and coprimality of every binary power with odd q. Exact held-rank recovery identifies return with the binary order condition:

\[
 r_k=1\iff 2^k\bmod q=1\bmod q.
\]

If no positive return occurred through q steps, cancellation of the common binary factor would make all q+1 positions r_0,…,r_q distinct. They lie in the complete q-member positive rank carrier, contradicting its finite cardinality. Ascending search therefore supplies a first period p with

\[
 0<p\le q,\qquad r_p=1,\qquad
 \forall j,\ 0<j<p\Longrightarrow r_j\ne1.
\]

The executed transition then gives r_(p+k) = r_k. Repeated removal of a complete period yields

\[
 r_k=r_{k\bmod p}\qquad(k\ge0).
\]

Thus positivity and exact recurrence persist at every finite continuation, without a cutoff on denominators or Fold depth. Each generated odd successor q = 2n+3 satisfies q > 1 and q mod 2 = 1 by the exact remainder identity (3+2n) mod 2 = 3 mod 2 = 1, so the same first-return theorem applies for every supplied n. Five native theorems establish these statements with no axiom dependencies. The executable odd-denominator wrapper and its complete registered entry checks are separate from these general recurrence theorems.

346. Exact Fraction and held-rank recurrence correspondence

Let c_q(n) denote the original positive cast: repeatedly subtract q while the retained numerator is greater than q. Each subtraction preserves the remainder, so induction on the actual removal trace proves

\[
 c_q(n)\bmod q=n\bmod q.
\]

For positive n and q, the cast lies in 1,…,q. The held-rank Fold is

\[
 F_q(n)=\begin{cases}q,&2n\bmod q=0,\\2n\bmod q,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}
\]

It lies in the same held-rank interval and has remainder 2n mod q. Two ranks in 1,…,q with equal remainders are equal: a nonzero remainder names the rank itself, while zero names the retained whole q. Hence

\[
 c_q(n+n)=F_q(n).
\]

Write N(n,q) for the original normalized positive Fraction n/q. The already derived normalization and Fold-cast identity now yields the exact state equation

\[
 \operatorname{Fold}(N(n,q))=N(c_q(n+n),q)=N(F_q(n),q).
\]

For the unit orbit define x_k = N(r_k,q), where r_k is the actual held-rank iteration from section 344. Then Fold(x_k) = x_(k+1). The rank return r_p = 1 supplied for every odd q > 1 therefore gives x_p = x_0. This is equality of the actual normalized Fraction states, including their positive-cast convention, rather than only equality of modular residues. Eight native declarations establish this correspondence and Fraction-return existence with no axiom dependencies. The original loop's first-return branch and successful output for arbitrary odd q follow from the visited-state argument below.

347. General success of the original odd-denominator first-return loop

For odd q, reducedness gives gcd(r_k,q) = 1. Normalization therefore leaves the numerator unchanged:

\[
 \operatorname{numerator}(x_k)=r_k/\gcd(r_k,q)=r_k.
\]

Equality of Fraction states implies equality of their held ranks. Before the first binary period p, the rank-cancellation proof excludes every collision at distinct positions, hence

\[
 0\le i<j<p\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_i\ne x_j.
\]

At loop position k < p, retain the invariant that the current state is x_k and every stored visited key is the key of some x_i with i ≤ k. The actual next Fold is x_(k+1). If k+1 = p, this state is x_0, so the original return-to-source branch succeeds before testing visited keys. If it differs from the source, k+1 < p. A visited-key match would then give x_(k+1) = x_i with i ≤ k, contradicting the displayed collision exclusion. Thus the non-source-repeat error branch is impossible. Advancing adds exactly the next key and preserves the invariant. Induction over the terminating original Run proves successful output.

The retained first-return theorem supplies the complete trace structure

\[
 \operatorname{firstReturn}(x_0)=\operatorname{ok}(T),\qquad
 T=B\mathbin{+\!+}[x_0],\qquad
 \operatorname{Steps}(x_0,T),\qquad
 \forall x\in B,\ x\ne x_0.
\]

This also proves T is nonempty. For odd q, the even-denominator guard cannot hold: if floor(q/2)·2 = q, taking remainders gives q mod 2 = 0, contradicting q mod 2 = 1. The wrapper therefore reaches the original loop, and its final positive-domain guard preserves T by section 345. For every supplied n with (n+2) mod 2 = 1,

\[
 \exists T,\quad
 \operatorname{oddDenominatorOrbit}(n+2)=\operatorname{ok}(T)
 \land\operatorname{FirstReturn}(1/(n+2),T).
\]

Nine native theorems establish the Fraction-state collision exclusion, actual loop success, guard passage and complete wrapper result with no axiom dependencies. The theorem is quantified over the full admitted odd-denominator domain.

350. Complete reference-equivalence classes and retained records

Let R be the generated kind-preserving reference equivalence of the physical quantity construction, and write Q_a(o) for R(a,o.carrier). The equivalence properties and the separate observation record are those of the quantity carrier itself. Every observation belongs to the class anchored at its own carrier, since R(o.carrier,o.carrier).

If an observation o lies in both Q_a and Q_b, symmetry gives R(o.carrier,b), and transitivity with R(a,o.carrier) gives R(a,b). For any observation x, transitivity in both directions then yields
\[
 Q_a(o)\land Q_b(o)\Longrightarrow R(a,b),\qquad
 R(a,b)\Longrightarrow\bigl(Q_a(x)\iff Q_b(x)\bigr).
\]
Conversely, suppose membership agrees for all observations. Apply the membership equivalence to the observation with carrier b and any held record. Reflexivity gives membership in Q_b, hence R(a,b). Therefore
\[
 \bigl(\forall o,\ Q_a(o)\iff Q_b(o)\bigr)\iff R(a,b).
\]
Disconnected anchors consequently have no common member. The classes cover all admitted observations and are either disjoint or have identical membership, without constructing a quotient that erases records. If x and y belong to Q_a, kind preservation gives kind(x.carrier)=kind(a)=kind(y.carrier). Replacing only an observation's record leaves its membership unchanged; distinct records remain separately held by the underlying observation constructor. Eight native theorems establish these class consequences with zero axiom dependencies. They operate on the source's reference-equivalence carrier; they do not replace it with a numerical-value classifier.

351. Exact same-dimension reference transport

A reference retains its name and canonical dimension form. An admitted comparison from reference a to reference b carries both the equality D(a)=D(b) and a positive normalized ratio x. The dimension form is a held form, independent of the ratio's numerical value. If D(a)≠D(b), an admitted comparison would supply the contradictory equality, so no such comparison can be constructed.

For x=n/d with n,d positive, reversing the comparison exchanges the reference endpoints, reverses their dimension equality and uses the already derived normalized reciprocal. Writing N for exact normalization,
\[
 x^{-1}=N(d,n),\qquad
 x\,x^{-1}=N(1,1).
\]
For comparisons a→b with ratio x and b→c with ratio y, transitivity gives D(a)=D(c), and the composite ratio is
\[
 z=N(n_xn_y,d_xd_y),\qquad
 (n_xn_y)d_z=n_z(d_xd_y).
\]
The cross-product identity is the normalization-preserving composition theorem, valid at arbitrary admitted positive counts. For views N(n,m) and N(m,k), its existing exact cancellation theorem gives
\[
 n_z\,k=n\,d_z,
\]
so the intermediate reference cancels in value while both input comparisons remain available in the finite chain.

A chain begins with one comparison and extends by appending a comparison whose starting reference is the current endpoint. Its evaluated comparison is defined by
\[
 C([a\to b])=C_{ab},\qquad
 C(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=C(P)\circ C_{bc}.
\]
The constructor retains the prior chain and the appended comparison. Each collapse uses the positive ratio product and transitive dimension identity; hence every supplied finite chain has a positive ratio and preserves the dimension of its endpoints. Thirteen native theorems establish exclusion of unlike dimensions, positive ratios, reciprocal return, exact composition, telescoping and the finite-chain base and successor equations, with zero axiom dependencies. This component formalizes transport on admitted references. Canonical dimension generation is derived in Sections 352–353; the complete source-program and empirical comparisons are reported in Section 355.

352. Finite canonical dimension composition

The registered dimension statement describes canonical finite products and exact quotients of independent quantity kinds. Represent a generated description by a kind label, a product of two descriptions, or an exact quotient of two descriptions. Its support is the finite list of kind labels appearing in that description, retaining both operands at every composition. No measured value enters this construction.

For a held kind k, retain a numerator count n and denominator count d. A matching kind contributes (1,0), and an absent kind contributes (0,0). Products add like-side counts; quotients exchange the second operand's sides:
\[
 C_k(ab)=(n_a+n_b,d_a+d_b),\qquad
 C_k(a/b)=(n_a+d_b,d_a+n_b).
\]
These are counts of occurrences in the finite description. Their zero denotes absence of a factor, not a physical zero magnitude. Cancellation gives the canonical residual pair
\[
 R(n,d)=(n-d,d-n).
\]
At least one residual side is absent: if n≤d, n−d=0; otherwise d≤n and d−n=0. Induction on the common appended count c proves
\[
 R(n+c,d+c)=R(n,d).
\]
Thus a common numerator/denominator factor cancels exactly without choosing a numerical scale or using a signed physical magnitude.

Write F_k(p)=R(C_k(p)) for the held form of description p at kind k. Descriptions share a dimension precisely when their forms agree at every kind. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from equality of the residual pairs. Distinct primitive labels cannot be identified: at label k, the description k has pair (1,0), whereas a different primitive q has pair (0,0). This retains the independence of the kind carriers.

Finite count addition proves product commutation and association. Exchanging denominator orientation proves
\[
 (a/b)/c \sim a/(bc),\qquad a/(b/c)\sim(ac)/b.
\]
Here ∼ means equality of all held kind forms. For (ab)/b, the counts at each kind are n_a+n_b+d_b and d_a+d_b+n_b. Reordering the same appended support and applying common-factor cancellation gives
\[
 (ab)/b\sim a,\qquad a/a\sim 1.
\]
The final notation denotes absence of every residual factor, not an extra primitive quantity. Likewise, the counts of (a/b)(b/c) contain the common addition n_b+d_b on both sides. Removing that addition proves
\[
 (a/b)(b/c)\sim a/c.
\]
These identities hold for every supplied finite description, including composite denominator descriptions.

353. Complete finite decision of held dimension identity

Let S(p) be the complete generated support of a description p. Induction on its construction proves that k∉S(p) implies C_k(p)=(0,0), hence F_k(p)=(0,0). For products and quotients, absence from the appended support implies absence from both operand supports, and the count equations preserve the absent pair.

The executable comparison checks every label in S(a)++S(b):
\[
 B(a,b)=\bigwedge_{k\in S(a)\mathbin{+\!+}S(b)}
             [F_k(a)=F_k(b)].
\]
If B is true, finite-list induction supplies equality at each listed kind. Any unlisted kind is absent from both supports and has pair (0,0) on both sides. Therefore the finite comparison establishes equality at every kind. Conversely, equality at every kind supplies every conjunction member, so finite-list induction makes B true:
\[
 B(a,b)=\mathrm{true}\iff
       \forall k,\ F_k(a)=F_k(b).
\]
Duplicate occurrences and support order do not omit a kind: the comparison retains the complete operand supports, and repeated equality checks preserve the result. Distinct primitive kind labels are rejected by the finite comparison because its soundness would otherwise contradict primitive independence. 356. Operational realization with a complete retained trace

A realization step from reference a to reference b contains the admitted same-dimension comparison, its exact positive ratio x, source identity σ and observation record ρ. A finite process begins with one step and extends only by a step whose starting reference is the current endpoint. For a process P and appended step s, define its resulting comparison and trace by
\[
 R([s])=s.\mathrm{comparison},\qquad
 R(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s])=R(P)\circ s.\mathrm{comparison},
\]
\[
 T([s])=[\mathrm{row}(s,x)],\qquad
 T(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s])=
 T(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[\mathrm{row}(s,R(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s]).\mathrm{ratio})].
\]
Each row holds the from-reference, to-reference, source identity, observation record, local factor and cumulative ratio. The row constructor preserves both endpoints and both source fields exactly. The composition operation is the normalized positive ratio composition of Section 351; hence, writing x=n_x/d_x and y=n_y/d_y,
\[
 \mathrm{ratio}(R(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s]))
 =N(n_xn_y,d_xd_y),
\]
where x is the prior cumulative ratio and y the appended comparison ratio.

Let H(P) be the ordered list of source-identity/record pairs and let L(P) count steps. The first-step equations are H([s])=[(σ_s,ρ_s)] and L([s])=1; extension appends that pair and increases the count by one. The finite-list identities
\[
 \mathrm{map}(f,X\mathbin{+\!+}[x])
 =\mathrm{map}(f,X)\mathbin{+\!+}[f(x)],\qquad
 |X\mathbin{+\!+}[x]|=|X|+1
\]
follow by induction on X. Applying them at each process extension proves
\[
 \mathrm{map}((σ,ρ),T(P))=H(P),\qquad |T(P)|=L(P)>0.
\]
Thus the trace is nonempty, retains every comparison record in order and preserves its entire prior prefix on extension. The resulting comparison carries D(a)∼D(b), and its normalized ratio has positive numerator. Twelve native theorems establish these statements with zero axiom dependencies. Source identity here is the retained identity field; the trace theorem preserves supplied records and does not manufacture empirical observations.

357. Measured values as separate records

The source measured-value record is the ordered triple
\[
 V=(r,s,p),
\]
with held reference identity r, textual numerical inscription s and observation provenance p. Replacing the inscription by t gives
\[
 \mathrm{replace}(V,t)=(r,t,p).
\]
Projection therefore proves reference retention, exact replacement of the inscription and provenance retention. These three facts do not depend on the text being parsed as a proof-domain scalar.

Each coordinate remains distinguishable. If two records V and W were equal, applying any coordinate projection would give equality of that coordinate. Taking the contrapositive separately yields
\[
 r_V\ne r_W\Rightarrow V\ne W,\qquad
 s_V\ne s_W\Rightarrow V\ne W,\qquad
 p_V\ne p_W\Rightarrow V\ne W.
\]
Conversely, rebuilding a record from its three held projections reproduces it exactly:
\[
 (V.r,V.s,V.p)=V.
\]
The seven native proofs retain the source distinction between a quantity's structural carrier and its externally reported numerical inscription, with zero axiom dependencies.

358. Complete retention of measurement uncertainty

A source-bound alternative consists of its relation, source identity and the recorded verdict of whether it remains admissible. Let a(x) denote that verdict. The uncertainty support is the complete ordered retention operation
\[
 U([])=[],\qquad
 U(x::X)=
 \begin{cases}
 x::U(X),&a(x)=\mathrm{true},\\
 U(X),&a(x)=\mathrm{false}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The admissibility verdict is part of the supplied measurement record. It is not a fitted choice made by this retention operation.

Define a valid retention derivation by three rules: the empty input retains the empty output; an admitted head must be retained; a rejected head must be removed. Induction on X constructs such a derivation for U(X). Induction on any valid derivation proves its output equals U(X). Therefore two valid retention derivations for the same input cannot select different supports.

List induction also proves both directions of the exact support statement:
\[
 x\in U(X)\iff x\in X\ \land\ a(x)=\mathrm{true}.
\]
The forward direction establishes source membership and admissibility; the reverse establishes that no admitted source alternative is omitted. A rejected alternative cannot belong to U(X), since membership would make its Boolean verdict both true and false. Finally, induction on X proves
\[
 U(X\mathbin{+\!+}Y)=U(X)\mathbin{+\!+}U(Y).
\]
Thus the construction preserves all admissible alternatives in source order, including their retained identities. Eight native theorems establish construction, exactness, unique selection, complete membership and concatenation with zero axiom dependencies.

 \mathrm{get}(\mathrm{drop}(B,o),j)=\mathrm{get}(B,o+j).

 A([])=\mathrm{true},\qquad
 A((p,q)::P)=B(p,q)\land A(P),

 \mathcal L(P)\iff

 A(P)=\mathrm{true}\iff\mathcal L(P).

363. Complete observed events and retained change

The mechanics source follows the completed measurement chain. A physical event retains the complete observed source state; a change retains both endpoint observations and the source-bound action connecting them. The construction below is uniform in the held state carrier and uses the already defined observation record. It does not replace that carrier with a finite answer classifier or a reported numerical inscription.

Write an observed event as E=(s,ρ), where s is the complete supplied carrier state and ρ is its held observation record. A transition from a to b holds source identity σ and action record A. Its retained row is
\[
 R(a\to b)=(a,b,σ,A).
\]
Both complete events remain present, including both observation records. Projecting a row recovers each of these coordinates. If either endpoint, source identity or action record differs, equality of the two rows would imply equality of that coordinate by projection, a contradiction. Reconstructing the row from its four projections returns the exact original row.

An event path begins at one observed event and extends by one transition from its current endpoint. Its event sequence E(P), transition rows T(P) and source/action ledger H(P) satisfy
\[
 E([a])=[a],\quad T([a])=[],\quad H([a])=[],
\]
\[
 E(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=E(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[c],
\]
\[
 T(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=T(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[R(b\to c)],
\]
\[
 H(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=H(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[(σ_{bc},A_{bc})].
\]
The endpoint indices ensure that the appended transition starts at the previous endpoint. Let n(P)=|T(P)|. The append-one length identity proves n(P+[b→c])=n(P)+1. Induction on the path then proves
\[
 |E(P)|=n(P)+1,\qquad E(P)\ne[],\qquad
 \mathrm{map}((σ,A),T(P))=H(P).
\]
Thus every extension preserves all earlier events and transitions, appends exactly one generated change, and retains every source/action record in order. Fifteen native theorems establish these base, successor, retention and distinguishability properties without axiom dependencies.

364. Duration from generated recurrence

A held reference recurrence contains its starting observation, returning observation and complete event path C. It retains the equality of the returning and starting carrier states, while the observation records remain separately held. Its generated transition count m=n(C) is positive. No absolute background time coordinate enters the construction.

For a measured event path P, let n=n(P). The source distinction between absent change and positive duration is represented by separate constructors:
\[
 \Delta(P;C)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathrm{EmptyOne},&n=0,\\
 \mathrm{Positive}(N(n,m)),&n>0,
 \end{cases}
\]
where N is the previously derived exact positive fraction normalization. The zero in the branch condition counts the absence of transitions; it is not a numerical physical duration. The positive constructor carries a fraction whose numerator is proved positive and whose denominator is nonzero.

For one observed event there is no transition, so Δ([a];C)=EmptyOne. Conversely, if Δ(P;C)=EmptyOne, a positive transition count would put the result in the distinct positive constructor. Therefore
\[
 \Delta(P;C)=\mathrm{EmptyOne}\iff n(P)=0.
\]
Appending a transition gives n+1 and excludes the Empty One case. For n>0, writing N(n,m)=u/v, exact normalization proves
\[
 nv=um,\qquad u>0.
\]
The reference recurrence compared with itself gives N(m,m)=1/1: both normalized numerator and denominator are exactly 1.

Changing the held reference from a recurrence of m transitions to one of k transitions composes the generated ratios. If z=N(n,m)\circ N(m,k), the exact telescoping theorem gives
\[
 z_{\mathrm{num}}\,k=n\,z_{\mathrm{den}}.
\]
The intermediate recurrence cancels in value while both source paths remain available. The event-count identity |E(P)|=n(P)+1 connects duration to the retained ordered path. Eleven native theorems establish absence, positive duration, exact normalization, reference return, reference-unit One and reference-change telescoping with zero axiom dependencies.

365. Reference-relative location and held displacement orientation

A location retains its reference identity, complete supplied support and observation record:
\[
 L=(r,S,ρ).
\]
Changing either the reference identity or the support distinguishes the location, because equality would preserve each projection. Rebuilding L from its three projections returns L exactly. This is a reference-relative record; no unobserved absolute position is added.

A displacement holds two such locations, their admitted exact positive separation x and which endpoint holds the orientation:
\[
 d=(L_1,L_2,x,h),\qquad h\in\{\mathrm{first},\mathrm{second}\}.
\]
The separation is the supplied exact quantity relation, not a fitted coefficient. Both endpoint reference identities and both observation records remain held. Define opposite(first)=second and opposite(second)=first. The two finite cases establish opposite(opposite(h))=h and opposite(h)≠h.

Reversing the comparison orientation is
\[
 \mathrm{reverse}(d)=(L_1,L_2,x,\mathrm{opposite}(h)).
\]
It preserves the positive magnitude and the entire source pair, changes the held orientation, and returns d when applied twice. Orientation reversal introduces no negative physical length.

Relabelling the written endpoint order is a separate description operation:
\[
 \mathrm{swap}(d)=(L_2,L_1,x,\mathrm{opposite}(h)).
\]
Checking the two held-endpoint cases proves that this operation preserves the actual held location. It also preserves x and is involutive. The distinction between reversing a comparison and exchanging the written endpoint order keeps orientation and description identity explicit. Fourteen native theorems establish the record, positivity, retention and orientation properties without axiom dependencies.

366. Exact speed and oriented velocity

The source speed relation divides the retained exact separation by a positive generated duration. Velocity retains that rate together with the displacement orientation. For separation x=n_x/d_x and duration t=n_t/d_t, define
\[
 q=N(n_xd_t,d_xn_t).
\]
Both products are positive because x and t are admitted positive fractions. Normalization supplies the exact cross-product identity
\[
 (n_xd_t)q_{\mathrm{den}}=q_{\mathrm{num}}(d_xn_t),
 \qquad q_{\mathrm{num}}>0.
\]
This constructs the quotient from the two retained quantity relations without an added numerical scale.

The native velocity record retains the displacement, both endpoint events, the complete event path, the reference recurrence and the proof that the path contains a transition. Its speed is the quotient above with t=N(n(P),n(C)); its orientation is the held displacement endpoint. Reversing that orientation leaves the displacement magnitude, event path and reference recurrence unchanged. Hence
\[
 \mathrm{speed}(\mathrm{reverse}(v))=\mathrm{speed}(v),
\]
\[
 \mathrm{orientation}(\mathrm{reverse}(v))
 =\mathrm{opposite}(\mathrm{orientation}(v)),\qquad
 \mathrm{reverse}(\mathrm{reverse}(v))=v.
\]
The duration trace and reference are retained by equality of the complete corresponding fields, rather than by equality of a reported number alone.

The dimension description is the generated quotient of the separation and duration descriptions. For each kind k, if their numerator/denominator occurrence counts are (a,b) and (c,d), its counts are

 C_k(D_{\mathrm{speed}})=(a+d,b+c).

This is the exact quotient construction of Section 352, retaining both dimension carriers. 370. Source-bound inertial continuation

The inertia construction retains the complete velocity carrier v, including displacement, orientation, generated path and reference recurrence. A transfer record is a triple t=(source identity, action record, resulting carrier). The V3 provenance rule has two admitted continuation forms: retain v when no transfer is present, or retain the result of the supplied source-bound transfer. With the absence marker denoted by none,
\[
 S(v,\mathrm{none})=v,\qquad
 S(v,\mathrm{some}(t))=t.\mathrm{result}.
\]
The inductive admissibility relation has exactly these retained and transferred constructors. Elimination of its constructors proves that every admitted continuation w satisfies \(w=S(v,s)\). Consequently, if an admitted w differs from v, then there exists a retained transfer t with \(s=\mathrm{some}(t)\) and \(w=t.\mathrm{result}\). The absence marker is a structural alternative; it is not a zero-valued motion carrier.

For a finite ordered transfer-option list L, define the complete succession and source ledger recursively:
\[
 F(v,[])=v,\qquad F(v,s::L)=F(S(v,s),L),
\]
\[
 Q([])=[],\quad Q(\mathrm{none}::L)=Q(L),\quad
 Q(\mathrm{some}(t)::L)=t::Q(L).
\]
Induction on L establishes \(Q(L)=[]\Rightarrow F(v,L)=v\). The empty list is reflexive. An absent-transfer successor reduces to the induction hypothesis; a present-transfer successor gives a nonempty ledger and cannot satisfy the premise. This proves preservation of the complete velocity, and hence preservation of its exact speed and held orientation. The same recursion proves
\[
 F(v,L\mathbin{+\!+}R)=F(F(v,L),R),\qquad
 Q(L\mathbin{+\!+}R)=Q(L)\mathbin{+\!+}Q(R).
\]
Ten native component theorems establish these statements with zero axiom dependencies. The original 256-form program, complete blind empirical method and four independent-validator cases also agree with V3. The inertia entry is complete following its acceleration dependency.

372. Exact oriented scalar changes

 A=ps,\qquad B=rq,\qquad D=qs>0.

 A>B:\quad(o_x,\operatorname{normalizePositive}(A-B,D)),

 B>A:\quad(o_y,\operatorname{normalizePositive}(B-A,D)),

 (A-B)d_z=n_zD,

while exact removal reconstructs the original common support:

 Bd_z+n_zD=Ad_z.

The right-held branch gives the symmetric identities. The result is Empty One exactly when the cross-products coincide. Equality, left dominance and right dominance therefore exhaust the original positive-rational domain. Empty One is an additive identity, and the source subtraction is
\[
 x\mathbin{\ominus}y=x\mathbin{\oplus}\operatorname{reverse}(y).
\]
In particular, x⊖x is Empty One for every admitted scalar, including Empty One itself. Both the operation and its result retain the original held-orientation convention.

For an admitted positive forward duration t=a/b, the original division first constructs the exact reciprocal b/a and then multiplies. If the numerator magnitude is m=n/d, the resulting reduced magnitude z satisfies

 (nb)d_z=n_z(da),\qquad n_z>0.

Division preserves the numerator's held orientation; an Empty One numerator remains Empty One. The positive-duration type excludes division by structural absence, matching the source boundary. 373. Acceleration from the complete velocity comparison

An acceleration record has two complete observed velocity endpoints E_before and E_after, a source-bound generated path between those very endpoints, and a held reference recurrence. The endpoint velocities retain the displacement support, exact separation, original motion interval, reference recurrence, observation and held orientation defined in Sections 363–366. The comparison does not replace them with an answer-only rate.

The two displacement orientation labels are renamed bijectively as forward-held and counter-held for the original scalar operations. Both round-trip identities are proved. Reversing the displacement orientation corresponds exactly to scalar reversal, with the speed unchanged.

Let N>0 be the generated comparison-path transition count and K>0 the held reference recurrence count. The duration τ=n_τ/d_τ is obtained by the original exact normalization:
\[
 \tau=\operatorname{normalizePositive}(N,K),\qquad
 Nd_\tau=n_\tau K.
\]
The acceleration value is then computed, rather than supplied as an independent field:
\[
 \Delta v=v_{\mathrm{after}}\mathbin{\ominus}v_{\mathrm{before}},\qquad
 a=\Delta v\mathbin{/}\tau.
\]

The held-orientation rule is the original multiply_scalar rule: matching orientations give forward-held, and differing orientations give counter-held. Its four cases are exhaustive. For every generated kind, the numerator and denominator occurrence counts of D_W and D_E agree. The positive-side calculation reduces to

377. Angular motion: exact phase in a retained closed recurrence

Let C be a finite observed recurrence with N > 0 source-bound transitions, returning to the same complete carrier. Its traversal retains a held orientation h. A position is an observed event together with an initial path P and remaining path Q satisfying P joined to Q = C. Consequently,

\[
\operatorname{changes}(P) ++ \operatorname{changes}(Q) = \operatorname{changes}(C)
\]
k + r = N,    k = count(P),    r = count(Q),    k ≤ N.

This decomposition retains every transition and its order. The phase magnitude at a present position is the normalized exact part k/N; its orientation is h. An initial path with no transition has structural Empty One. The terminal position has phase magnitude N/N = 1, while its observed carrier equals the starting carrier. Thus returning to the same carrier does not discard the completed traversal.

If normalize(k,N) = (u,v), Lean proves k v = u N and u ≤ v. No irrational angular unit enters this construction. For two ordered positions, the connecting observed interval I must satisfy P_before joined to I = P_after. The full interval ledger is retained, and k_before + count(I) = k_after. With a held clock recurrence of M transitions,

tau = count(I)/M,
\[
\Delta\phi = \phi_{\mathrm{after}}\mathbin{\ominus}\phi_{\mathrm{before}}
\]
\[
\omega = \operatorname{dividePositive}(\Delta\phi,\tau)
\]

The subtraction and division are the previously derived exact held-orientation scalar operations. For a present phase change of magnitude a/b and positive duration c/d, the normalized rate p/q satisfies (a d) q = p (b c); its held change orientation is preserved. The mathematical construction covers every finite admitted path decomposition, independently of the finite candidate grammar.

Here \(x\mathbin{\ominus}y=x\mathbin{\oplus}\operatorname{reverse}(y)\) is the oriented FoldScalar operation of §372; equality yields EmptyOne, and division retains that case.

for every aggregate F on the complete retained carriers. This establishes conservation of the complete support, not merely equality of a selected scalar total. 383. Geometric dilution and the unique conserved share

Let the positive source support be s = a/b, and let its complete equivalent boundary contain N > 0 generated cells. The response assigned to every cell is the reduced exact ratio

\[
u = \operatorname{normalize}(a, bN)
\]

If u = p/q, normalization proves

\[
a q = p b N
\]

The complete response ledger pairs each boundary cell with u. Projecting the cell coordinates recovers the entire boundary, and the response count is N. Every retained response has the same share; choosing a different profile cannot satisfy that complete equal-cell assignment.

Uniqueness follows from conservation. If a second positive reduced share v = r/t satisfies a t = r b N, combining that identity with a q = p b N gives

\[
(bN) r q = (bN) p t
\]

Since bN is positive, cancellation gives r q = p t. Reduced positive-fraction identity then yields v = u. The gcd and positive-cancellation steps are proved constructively. No fitted boundary profile enters this result.

For every positive generated count k, common replication also preserves the reduced relation:

\[
\operatorname{normalize}(ka, kb) = \operatorname{normalize}(a,b)

392. Generated adjacency and completed causal accessibility

Let A(a,b) be the generated adjacency relation on observed events. Source-bound propagation is constructed by the following rules:

one(a) : a reaches a,
append(p,c,A(b,d)) : a reaches d,

where p reaches b from a and c is the complete recorded change from b to d. Erasing only the adjacency certificates yields the existing full mechanical event path. Structural induction proves that every retained change row has adjacent before and after events. For a noninitial destination, case analysis on the final propagation constructor supplies its actual adjacent predecessor. A remote change cannot be admitted through an unrecorded predecessor in this representation.

Composition joins two compatible paths, and its erased trace equals the complete mechanical join. Thus composition retains the ordered source/action records of both pieces. For a finite list of completed arrivals C, accessibility at that event is

accessible(C) = [destination(r) : r in C].

Membership yields an actual arrival occurrence in C with that destination and its retained adjacent propagation proof. Conversely, a destination outside this complete list has no arrival occurrence in C. Appending one completed arrival gives

\[
\operatorname{accessible}(C ++ [r]) = \operatorname{accessible}(C) ++ [\operatorname{destination}(r)]
\]

This is the completed-path boundary of the source claim. It does not replace completed accessibility by all paths that might be generated at a later event.

The radiative carrier retains the full source identity, energy and momentum records, recurrence and held polarization while local source contact is absent. For an observation sequence R, its detached ledger is [(carrier, none, r) : r in R]. Projection recovers R exactly, the complete carrier remains at every occurrence, and appending an observation preserves all prior records. 396. Exact interior change and boundary flow

Let I(x) record whether a generated support node lies inside the held region. Every original transfer t retains its named source s(t), destination d(t), complete carrier, source identity and action record. The complete outward and inward ledgers are selected by

O = [t : I(s(t)) = true and I(d(t)) = false],
J = [t : I(s(t)) = false and I(d(t)) = true].

The membership theorems are biconditionals: a transfer occurs in O precisely when it occurs in the original network and satisfies the outward conditions; the corresponding statement holds for J. Thus no crossing is omitted or invented. Inward selection is outward selection for the complementary region, with both endpoints retained.

Let D be the number of transfers departing from an interior node and A the number arriving at an interior node. Complete finite-network induction gives

\[
D + |J| = A + |O|
\]

The proof checks all four endpoint-membership cases. An interior-to-interior transfer adds one to both D and A. An interior-to-exterior transfer adds one to D and |O|. An exterior-to-interior transfer adds one to A and |J|. An exterior-to-exterior transfer changes none of the four counts. This equality expresses continuity without introducing a negative proof magnitude.

The result retains complete carriers as well as counts. Interior losses are source-side records of O, and boundary outflow is the recipient-side record of the same O. Projection onto carriers gives exactly equal ordered lists. Interior gains and boundary inflow similarly project to the same complete carrier list from J. Source identities, actions and distinct transfer occurrences remain available throughout; equal-valued transfers are not silently merged.

398. Period and frequency from complete recurrence counts

A wave retains a closed, oriented recurrence and a complete held-reference recurrence. Let N > 0 be the wave recurrence's transition count and M > 0 the reference count. The exact period is

\[
T = \operatorname{normalize}(N,M)
\]

and frequency is its positive reciprocal f. If T has reduced numerator p and denominator q, then N q = p M. If f has reduced numerator a and denominator b, reciprocal normalization gives q b = a p. Combining the two identities and cancelling the positive p yields

\[
M b = a N
\]
\[
f = \operatorname{normalize}(M,N)
\]

Consequently the exact normalized product T f is One: its numerator and denominator are both 1. The proof holds for every positive generated recurrence/reference pair. Both period and frequency remain positive; no floating or irrational cycle value is introduced.

The recurrence's last carrier equals its first carrier. A held phase position retains an initial and remaining path whose concatenation is the complete original recurrence. Therefore the phase record preserves the full source/action history as well as the count ratio.

401. Complete labelled wave superposition

The source composition retains every independently generated wave trace on shared support. Write L=[l_1,...,l_m] and R=[r_1,...,r_n], where each record may carry its complete source, frequency, phase and support. The disjoint junction is

402. Common-cell phase-labelled predecessor merging

Each predecessor retains its observation cell, full incoming trace, held orientation and positive exact support. Merging is defined at a shared observation cell and retains the ordered pair of complete predecessors alongside the resulting support. The support operation is the previously established exact held-scalar addition.

For positive fractions x=a/b and y=c/d, matching held labels produce

\[
x+y = (ad+cb)/(bd)
\]

reduced by the exact normalization operation. The normalized numerator N and denominator D satisfy (ad+cb)D=Nbd. For opposed labels the comparison is between the positive cross-products ad and cb. Equality closes the support distinction to EmptyOne; ad>cb retains the first held orientation with positive remainder (ad-cb)/(bd); ad<cb retains the opposite orientation with positive remainder (cb-ad)/(bd). These subtractions denote the corresponding admitted positive remainder branches, not negative scientific quantities.

Thus exact opposed closure is equivalent to ad=cb. In either unequal branch, recomposing the remainder with the smaller support reconstructs the larger support. Closure of the observed distinction does not erase either predecessor: projecting the merged observation recovers both original records and their common cell. Distinct source traces remain distinct records even when the merged support is equal.

403. Aperture selection and complete reachable-support regeneration

Let P be the complete finite list of incident propagation paths, A(p) the registered aperture decision and S(p) the generated successor list for path p. The retained paths and regenerated output are

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_A(P)&=[p\in P\mid A(p)=\mathrm{true}],\\
G_A(P)&=\operatorname{concat}_{p\in R_A(P)}[(p,q)\mid q\in S(p)].
\end{aligned}
\]

Induction on P establishes exact aperture membership:

p in R_A(P) iff p in P and A(p)=true.

The full flattened successor generation then gives both directions of

(p,q) in G_A(P) iff p in P, A(p)=true and q in S(p).

404. Held transverse polarization

A polarized recurrence retains the complete radiation carrier, including its joint electromagnetic response, energy, momentum, recurrence and held polarization label. Reversal changes the held polarization label and retains the other fields. With the two held orientations denoted h_1 and h_2,

\]

\]

E(R(p))=E(p),     M(R(p))=M(p),     C(R(p))=C(p)
\]

Because frequency is derived from that same recurrence and reference clock, f(R(p))=f(p). The transverse role extracted from the joint magnetic response is likewise unchanged. 406. Exact recurrence matching and resonance

Retain the full driver and supported recurrence paths on their common generated refinement, with positive counts a and b and their held phase labels phi_d and phi_s. The least common return is

\[
L = \operatorname{lcm} (a,b) = a (b/\gcd (a,b)) = b (a/\gcd (a,b))
\]

Both a and b divide L and L is positive. Exact phase-aligned matching at a generated return n is

Matched(n) iff n>0, a divides n, b divides n and phi_d=phi_s.

If the phases agree, L is a matched return. Every matched n is divisible by L, hence L≤n. Any positive matched return that is least among all matched returns must equal L, by the two inequalities. This proves uniqueness of the least exact refinement without a tolerance band.

If phi_d≠phi_s, Matched(n) is false for every n under that retained phase pairing. This is an exclusion of unmatched phases from coherent transfer, not erasure of the driver or supported traces. For a list N of matched returns the transfer ledger is

T(N) = [(n,driver,supported,phi_d,phi_s) | n in N].

Its length equals |N|, every row has equal held phase labels, and appending a matched return appends exactly one complete transfer record while preserving all prior records. The original recurrence paths remain in every row, so repeated aligned transfer carries its full source correspondence.

412. Record-preserving joint refinement and incompatibility

Let S be the complete generated source support, A(s) and B(s) the two complete observation records, including their held phase/action information, and F the original generated family of candidate joint refinements. A refinement r supplies a generated joint record J_r(s) and its two record projections L_r and R_r.

Its exact preservation condition is

P(r,s) iff L_r(J_r(s))=A(s) and R_r(J_r(s))=B(s),
Preserves(r) iff for every s in S, P(r,s).

The finite Boolean preservation computation is proved equivalent to this full row-wise condition. A failed computation constructs an actual source occurrence s for which at least one of the two complete records differs; failure is not merely an indirect candidate-count test.

The incompatibility boundary is then established exactly over the registered family:

Incompatible(A,B;S,F)
iff every r in F fails Preserves(r)
iff there is no r in F preserving both complete records on every source occurrence.

Suppose a candidate resolution r in F preserves A on all of S. The constructive failed-row theorem supplies an occurrence whose A or B record differs. The first alternative contradicts preservation of A, so a required B record must differ. Interchanging A and B proves the symmetric statement. Resolving either side therefore closes a distinction required to preserve the other whenever the registered common-refinement condition fails.

The ledger [(s,J_r(s),L_r(J_r(s)),R_r(J_r(s))) | s in S] projects back to S exactly. Thus the exclusion retains complete source provenance. It introduces neither an irrational uncertainty bound nor a replacement family of admissible refinements.

414. Indistinguishability through complete exchange traces

Physical identity in the V3 construction is exchange equivalence of the complete observable transition and composition record. Let p=(a,b) be a pair of constituents and E(p)=(b,a) its exchange. The operation retains both constituents and satisfies

\[
E(E(p))=p
\]

For the complete registered observation family O=[o_1,...,o_n], retain the ordered ledger

\[
L_O(p)=[o_1(p),...,o_n(p)]
\]

The physical indistinguishability condition is

I_O(p) iff for every o in O, o(E(p))=o(p).

Induction on the complete observation list gives the exact equivalence

\[
I_O(p)\iff L_O(E(p))=L_O(p)
\]

The forward induction rewrites each head observation and retains the induction hypothesis for the remaining ledger. In the reverse direction, equality of the two lists gives equality of their heads and tails, recovering every registered observation. No constituent or observation is discarded by this quotient.

Exchange is an involution, so I_O(p) implies I_O(E(p)). Conversely, a held observation o in O with o(E(p))≠o(p) distinguishes the constituents. Extending the registered family preserves the exact condition:

I_(o::O)(p) iff o(E(p))=o(p) and I_O(p).

Thus indistinguishability does not erase a physical distinction that appears in the complete transition or composition trace. The original empirical identity classifications remain separately sealed and compared after the derivation.

415. Exclusion in the alternating exchange class

The alternating composition class carries one of two opposite held orientations. Write J for orientation reversal. These are distinct labels in the positive exact representation, with

J(h)≠h.

For an orientation record H on constituent pairs, alternating exchange means

\[
H(E(p))=J(H(p))
\]

If exchange fixes a pair, E(p)=p, substitution would require H(p)=J(H(p)), contradicting the distinction of the two held orientations. Hence

E(p)=p implies that p is excluded from the alternating class.

A constituent occupant retains its complete word w and its one-constituent observation cell c. For a=(w_a,c_a) and b=(w_b,c_b), equality of both fields gives

w_a=w_b and c_a=c_b implies a=b,
\[
E(a,b)=(a,b)
\]

Combining these identities with the alternating-orientation condition gives the same-cell exclusion derivation:

w_a=w_b and c_a=c_b implies not alternating(a,b).

Equivalently, any admitted alternating pair with identical constituent words must satisfy c_a≠c_b. The contradiction uses the actual exchanged record and the retained orientation distinction. It introduces no signed proof magnitude, occupation fit or additional exclusion rule. The statement applies to the original alternating exchange class, and its external occupation classifications retain their original empirical boundary.

416. Tunnelling from complete generated support

Let S be an admitted prepared physical Fold state. A successful reversible gate sequence G generates terminal state S', retains every predecessor state, and supplies an exact branch trace from each source branch to its terminal branch. The existing evolution construction establishes

b in branches(S') iff there exists a in branches(S) with BranchTrace(G,a,b),

and the inverse gate sequence reconstructs S exactly.

Let K(b) be the held phase-compatibility test for the generated barrier record, and C(b) the corresponding coarse classical observation. The complete traversal support is the ordered filter

T=[b in branches(S') : K(b)=true and C(b)=false].

The filter membership proof gives both directions of this equation for every generated branch. Consequently every observed b in T has an original source a and its exact successful gate trace. The branch was generated by the complete reversible evolution; it was not added to compensate for the coarse observation.

The coarse support is P=[b in branches(S') : C(b)=true]. If b belongs to both T and P, the retained coarse record would satisfy C(b)=false and C(b)=true. Therefore

b in T implies b not in P.

Conversely, every generated branch with the held compatible phase record and a closed coarse record belongs to T. This establishes the V3 distinction: complete support retains the lawful path that the coarse observation closes. The full preparation, gate sequence, predecessor ledger and terminal state remain beside the traversal observation. The underlying evolution stays exactly reversible after the traversal subset has been recorded.

417. Discrete spectra from exact boundary recurrence

For an admitted prepared state S and a generated boundary trace t, let A(S,t) be the original finite cyclic phase action. Successful action preserves the complete branch support and original phase cycle. A boundary class is closed precisely when the resulting state equals the initial state:

\[
closed_S(t)\iff A(S,t)=S
\]

The executable closure test compares both complete state fields, branches and phase cycle, after successful action. Equality of the two fields reconstructs equality of the state; conversely equality of the states makes both comparisons true. Failure of the original action is rejected.

For the complete finite family B of generated boundary traces, the bound-state spectrum is

Sigma(S,B)=[t in B : closed_S(t)].

The native membership proof establishes

t in Sigma(S,B) iff t in B and A(S,t)=S.

Every generated boundary trace is tested, and every retained class closes exactly. If the held cycle has length m and a generated trace has length m, the cyclic-action derivation gives A(S,t)=S, so that trace is retained in the spectrum. The original empty-action guard excludes the empty trace; the full-cycle result uses the admitted nontrivial phase cycle.

A transition record retains two distinct generated closed trace classes u and v. Its obligations give

u in Sigma(S,B), v in Sigma(S,B), u≠v,
A(S,u)=S and A(S,v)=S.

The transition retains the complete preparation, boundary family and both trace records. Discreteness follows from the finite generated recurrence classes and their exact closure test. No continuum eigenvalue equation is imported to select the classes.

418. Entanglement as nonfactorable complete joint support

Retain the common preparation and the full original branch beside its two constituent observations. For projections l and r on the complete prepared support, the joint ledger contains

(b,l(b),r(b)) for every b in branches(S).

Projecting each ledger row back to b reconstructs branches(S) in its original order. The joint support J consists of the corresponding pairs (l(b),r(b)); the preparation and source identity remain held separately from the projections.

Independent constituent supports L and R factor the joint support exactly when

(x,y) in J iff x in L and y in R.

Such a factorization forces cross-word closure: if (x,y) and (x',y') belong to J, then (x,y') also belongs to J. The proof takes x from the first pair's left membership and y' from the second pair's right membership and applies the reverse direction of the product condition.

The converse follows from the complete marginals. If J is cross-closed, any x in the left marginal and y in the right marginal have source rows (x,a) and (b,y) in J. Cross closure supplies (x,y). Hence

J has an independent-support factorization iff J is cross-closed.

Entanglement is the failure of this factorization while common preparation remains retained. In particular,

(x,y) in J, (x',y') in J, (x,y') not in J

excludes every independent product L×R, not only one proposed product. Each individual constituent reading occurs, but their missing cross word prevents a reconstruction from independent marginals. The original successful Fold composition separately establishes its complete product-support relation through jointWord(l,r); that existing construction supplies the independent-composition side of the distinction. Neither the correlation proof nor the composition projection drops the full source branch or common preparation.

419. Bell correlations and the omitted-dependence boundary

A complete generated event retains common preparation p, both measurement settings s_L and s_R, and both output records a and b. Its deterministic input is

\[
I(e)=(p(e),s_L(e),s_R(e))
\]

The full ledger stores each event beside this input and its two outputs. Projecting the ledger back to its source events recovers the entire census in order. The physical ledger additionally retains the admitted Fold preparation and every original branch beside its event interpretation.

The local factorized record considered by V3 retains a record h(e) and proposes functions f and g satisfying, for every generated event,

\[
f(h(e),s_L(e))=a(e)
\]
\[
g(h(e),s_R(e))=b(e)
\]

Suppose the complete census contains e and e' for which

\[
h(e)=h(e'), s_L(e)=s_L(e'),\quad\text{but }a(e)\ne a(e')
\]

Function congruence forces

\[
f(h(e),s_L(e))=f(h(e'),s_L(e'))
\]

whereas faithful reproduction would identify these equal values with the two distinct held outputs. This contradiction excludes every such factorized reproduction. The same derivation applies to the right side when its retained record and local setting agree but its generated output differs.

The excluded factorization is therefore specified by the exact generated dependence it omits. The complete preparation-and-settings record remains part of the deterministic state throughout. Applying the contradiction to events obtained from two actual held physical branches connects the boundary directly to the complete Fold support. This preserves V3's setting-inclusive correlation statement and its original independent causal boundary; no additional numerical Bell bound or replacement hidden-record premise is introduced.

420. Contextuality and complete observation provenance

\operatorname{map}(first,R)=\operatorname{branches}(S)
\]

|R|=|\operatorname{branches}(S)|

Selection does not erase the other original branches. The observation record retains (S,C,q,R), so distinct complete contexts remain distinct recorded observations.

r(i,C_1)≠r(i,C_2),

no context-erasing assignment a(i) can reproduce both. Such an assignment would require

a(i)=r(i,C_1), a(i)=r(i,C_2)

421. Decoherence through reversible environmental records

Let an admitted preparation S evolve reversibly to S'. A complete terminal branch is b=(w,phi), with physical word w and held phase label phi. Environmental distribution retains an environmental word e(b) and a phase reading d satisfying, for every original terminal branch,

\[
d(e(b))=phi
\]

The global record and its recovery map are

\[
G(b)=(w,e(b))
\]
\[
U(w,e)=(w,d(e))
\]

Substitution gives U(G(b))=b for every held branch. Therefore equal global records imply equal original branches. The global encoding cannot merge two distinct held branches or erase their phase distinction.

In particular, if phi_a≠phi_b, then e(a)≠e(b): equality of the environmental words would give equality of their decoded phases. Applying recovery to every row of the complete global ledger reconstructs branches(S') in its original order.

The reduced observation omits the inaccessible environmental component. Its projection is exactly

map(first,map(G,branches(S')))=support(S').

Branches with the same system word consequently have the same reduced observation even when their distinct phases remain recoverable from distinct environmental words. The original successful reverse gate trace still reconstructs S from S'. The local closure of phase distinctions is thus a projection of retained global records, with no stochastic deletion of the source support.

422. The environment-distinguished classical quotient

On the declared macroscopic boundary, let k(b) identify the relevant predecessor class and e(b) its environmental record. The classical-limit condition is that environmental records distinguish these classes:

e(a)=e(b) implies k(a)=k(b)

for all branches in the complete terminal support. Equivalently for a held distinction, k(a)≠k(b) forces e(a)≠e(b).

For a macroscopic reading M, retain the joint observation

\[
J(b)=(M(b),e(b))
\]

If two different predecessor classes had the same joint observation, projecting to the environmental component would identify their environmental records and hence their classes. Therefore

k(a)≠k(b) implies J(a)≠J(b).

Each nonempty environmental fibre consequently contains exactly one represented predecessor class: choose a member to establish existence, and apply the class-equality implication to any two members for uniqueness. Different interfering predecessor classes cannot merge within that fibre, even when their retained macroscopic readings coincide. The complete ledger still contains (b,J(b)) for every source branch, and projecting to b reconstructs the entire original support. Equal environmental records also give equal decoded phase labels through the environmental reconstruction law. These identities establish the original record-stabilized classical observation quotient on its declared scale without deleting the underlying reversible branch process.

423. Complete remote fibres and no-signalling

Represent the complete joint observation support as an ordered list of pairs (l,r). A generated change of remote partition is a bijective relabelling f with inverse g, satisfying g(f(r))=r and f(g(r'))=r'. Apply it to every joint row:

\[
T_f(l,r)=(l,f(r))
\]

The complete relabelling is reversible row by row, and its local projection is unchanged:

\[
\operatorname{map}((l,r') -> (l,g(r')),\operatorname{map}(T_f,J))=J
\]
\[
\operatorname{map}(first,\operatorname{map}(T_f,J))=\operatorname{map}(first,J)
\]

For any registered local observation test P, the exact local support count is

\[
N_P(J)=|\operatorname{filter}(P,\operatorname{map}(first,J))|
\]

Applying the same filter to the equal local projections proves

\[
N_P(\operatorname{map}(T_f,J))=N_P(J)
\]

The total support count is unchanged as well, so both the numerator and denominator of the exact local observation weight remain identical. Every remote-fibre row is retained; a remote partition change cannot alter that local count by omitting a branch.

The independent causal boundary remains the original generated-support rule. A noninitial admitted arrival has a generated adjacent predecessor. A destination outside the completed causal support has no completed arrival record. The count-preservation result and this source-bound causal condition give the V3 no-signalling boundary: remote relabelling preserves the complete local observation, while a changed causal response requires its generated transfer trace.

424. Mass-energy from two propagation transfers

A retained inertial preparation carries exact positive content m. Its held limiting propagation carrier has exact speed c and retains its complete spatial, temporal and source records. The original conversion composes that inertial content with two copies of the same propagation-speed carrier:

\[
E=m(c c)=mc^2
\]

The number of transfers is forced by the already derived energy dimension. Starting with the mass kind, let D_n be the dimension after n speed transfers:

\[
D_0=M
\]
\[
D_{n+1}=D_n(L/T)
\]

Induction gives the length-kind exponent of D_n as n, with no length-kind denominator. The transferred-work energy dimension is ML^2/T^2. Equality of the dimension forms therefore requires n=2. Conversely, expanding the products and quotients for D_2 gives exactly the energy dimension for every kind. Thus two transfers are both necessary and sufficient within the original generated conversion construction.

Write the exact positive carriers as m=m_n/m_d and c=c_n/c_d. Normalized Fold composition yields a positive reduced energy carrier E_n/E_d satisfying

\[
(m_n c_n^2) E_d = E_n (m_d c_d^2)
\]

The reduced-positive-fraction identity theorem proves uniqueness: any admitted positive reduced carrier satisfying this cross-product equation equals E. No further conversion coefficient is present. The full record retains the original inertial preparation, source trace and both complete propagation transfers.

The original numerical validation separately supplies the CODATA electron-mass interval and exact vacuum-speed carrier. The ten-instruction prediction computes the lower and upper speed squares and then the corresponding mass products:

\[
E_{\mathrm{lower}}=m_{\mathrm{lower}}c_{\mathrm{lower}}^2
\]
\[
E_{\mathrm{upper}}=m_{\mathrm{upper}}c_{\mathrm{upper}}^2
\]

For the pinned source, the exact prediction interval is

[2046776446362983920916785951/25000000000000000000000000000000000000000,
 2046776447621241171148330647/25000000000000000000000000000000000000000].

The separately committed mass-energy target interval is

[40935528927/500000000000000000000000,
 40935528953/500000000000000000000000].

The prediction is sealed before the target is released. Their exact rational intervals overlap, while the deliberately displaced unfavorable interval is rejected. These observed input and target records retain the source's empirical role; they do not select the structural two-transfer law.

425. Particle-antiparticle reversal of held labels

A complete constituent retains its physical Fold word and preparation, positive inertial support, finite spin action, complete transition grammar and ordered conserved-label record. For a held orientation h, let J(h) be its opposite. The existing held-label construction gives

\[
J(J(h))=h
\]
J(h)≠h.

Charge conjugation reverses every oriented label while retaining its identity:

(name,h) -> (name,J(h)).

Applying this map to the complete ordered label list defines the reversed constituent. Induction on the list and the orientation involution give

\[
\operatorname{reverseLabels}(\operatorname{reverseLabels}(L))=L
\]
\[
\operatorname{reverse}(\operatorname{reverse}(p))=p
\]

Every original label has its reversed row in the new record. Projecting the reversed list onto label names gives the original name list, and its length is unchanged. Thus no conserved label is added, omitted or replaced by an unrecorded label.

The reversal leaves the complete physical word, inertial carrier, spin action and transition grammar unchanged. In particular, the reversed constituent retains the same strictly positive inertial magnitude. The distinguishing operation acts on held orientations, not on a negative mass or signed proof magnitude. The original particle/antiparticle property and charge-conjugate decay records remain separate empirical comparisons at the registered boundary.

426. Spin action and exchange-composition classes

The finite spin action retains the prepared physical word, its complete phase cycle and the generated orientation trace. Let s be the prepared state, A its admitted orientation action, and r a held-orientation reading of its generated result. For the two held orientations h and J(h), the exchange alternatives are exhaustive and exclusive:

\[
r(A(s))=r(s)\text{ or }r(A(s))=J(r(s))
\]
J(h)≠h.

The first equation defines the preserving class and the second the alternating class. The construction classifies the actual generated spin result; it does not assign the class by an external particle name. When an exchange observation identifies its initial and final held readings with those of the generated action, its exchange class equals this spin-action class. A full phase-cycle trace returns the original state,

\[
A_{\mathrm{period}}(s)=s
\]

and therefore has preserving held reading. These statements retain the full action trace and the original finite cycle rather than replacing either with a continuously adjustable spin value.

For two identical words occupying the same cell, exchanging the pair leaves the complete pair unchanged. Every held reading of that pair must consequently agree before and after exchange. Alternation would require h=J(h), which the two held constructors exclude. Thus an alternating composition cannot contain that duplicate one-cell pair, while the preserving composition admits it. Both classifications are derived from the same exchange operation, whose square returns the original pair.

427. Complete transitionwise conservation of physical labels

A complete transition ledger pairs each input label occurrence with either an output carrier or a named boundary carrier. Labels are counted as occurrences, so equal inscriptions do not erase distinct transfers. For any exact label test T and a complete ledger L, define I_T(L), O_T(L) and B_T(L) as its input, output and named-boundary counts. The empty ledger satisfies

\[
I_T([])=O_T([])=B_T([])=0
\]

Appending an accepted output row increases I_T and O_T by one; appending an accepted boundary row increases I_T and B_T by one. Rejected rows change none of these counts. Induction on every row therefore gives

\[
I_T(L)=O_T(L)+B_T(L)
\]

The stronger ordered statement is also retained: projection of the complete input ledger onto its labels equals projection of the destination ledger onto its labels. Every destination occurrence has its original input, and every original occurrence has a destination. These results apply to each complete generated transition and to any exact label selection; neither a missing channel nor an unnamed boundary can be inserted into the pairing silently.
