428. Minimal recurrent trace classes and the observed particle spectrum

Let R be any finite list of recurrent constituent descriptions, and let the observable-trace type have decidable equality. The classification theorem quantifies over every such R and trace type; the registered measurement census is one application. Each description retains the complete constituent, a generated full-period return, its observable transition signature τ, and the source's list D of proper recurrent constituent decompositions. Particle names are descriptive fields. They do not enter τ or the minimality test.

Within this complete generated domain, a description is minimal exactly when its proper-decomposition list is empty:

\[
\operatorname{minimal}(d) \iff  D(d)=∅
\]

Let E(R) select the minimal descriptions from the finite source census R. The selection theorem proves both directions:

d∈E(R) ⇔ d∈R and D(d)=∅.

Any recorded proper recurrent decomposition therefore excludes its parent from E(R). The trace-class criterion is

\[
d_{1}∼d_{2} \iff  \tau (d_{1})=\tau (d_{2})
\]

Changing only a particle name preserves the class; changing the complete observable trace distinguishes it. Applying constructive duplicate removal to the complete selected signature list gives the spectrum

\[
S(R)=\operatorname{unique}([\tau (d) : d\in E(R)])
\]

The resulting list has no repeated signature, and its exact membership theorem is

τ∈S(R) ⇔ there exists d∈R with D(d)=∅ and τ(d)=τ.

Thus no minimal source class is omitted and no class lacking a minimal source representative is introduced. The source census supplies the generated decompositions and complete transition signatures; an external particle-table inscription cannot replace those structures or choose the equivalence law. The registered PDG rows remain the separate empirical membership boundary. Each retained constituent also preserves its original generated recurrence: an orientation trace of the complete phase-cycle length returns its prepared state exactly.

The proof proceeds through three exact list operations. Structural induction on R proves that filtering retains a description precisely when it occurs in R and has no recorded proper decomposition. Mapping the retained descriptions to their signatures therefore has exactly those signature preimages. Duplicate removal proceeds recursively: if a head signature occurs in the retained tail, discard that head; otherwise retain it. In either branch membership is unchanged, and induction proves distinctness. Combining these two membership equivalences yields the displayed spectrum equivalence for every R. Appending descriptions changes the source list supplied to the same theorem; there is no cardinality cutoff in its proof. 429. Boundary-closed composite hadrons

A joint hadron record retains its recurrent whole word, at least two complete constituents, its internal transfer ledger, and the observable total carriers and positive inertial support. If the constituent list is

\[
C=[c_{1},c_{2}] ++ R
\]

then |C|=|R|+2. Every internal transfer has both endpoints in the finite constituent index type Fin(|C|); the internal ledger therefore contains no endpoint outside the joint boundary.

Write departures(N) and arrivals(N) for the complete carrier projections of the internal network N. The original transfer pairing gives the ordered identity

\[
\operatorname{departures}(N)=\operatorname{arrivals}(N)
\]

Consequently, for every aggregate F of those complete carriers,

\[
F(\operatorname{departures}(N))=F(\operatorname{arrivals}(N))
\]

The external observation retains the total-carrier record and the whole word's strictly positive inertial carrier:

\[
\operatorname{external}(j)=(\operatorname{totalCarriers}(j),\operatorname{inertia}(j))
\]

Changing internal transfer arrangements while holding those external carriers fixed leaves this observation unchanged. More generally, every external reading f obeys

\[
\operatorname{external}(j_{1})=\operatorname{external}(j_{2}) \implies  f(\operatorname{external}(j_{1}))=f(\operatorname{external}(j_{2}))
\]

An internal label therefore cannot be distinguished separately by a reading of the same external totals. The generated proper decomposition [C] is retained in the joint description, so the composite-exclusion theorem removes that description from the elementary census. The whole joint word still has its complete generated phase recurrence. This distinguishes boundary-closed composition from an elementary trace class without importing an external hadron taxonomy.

430. Complete scattering channels and exact cross-section measure

A scattering channel retains its incoming and outgoing constituent words, preparation record, detector conditions, source identity and observed success flag. Let L be the complete registered channel ledger and H(L) its exact successful-channel selection. The native selection theorem is

c∈H(L) ⇔ c∈L and successful(c)=true.

Induction on L gives |H(L)|≤|L|. In the source's positive observed-support domain, k=|H(L)|>0, hence n=|L|>0. The exact normalized support ratio w=w_n/w_d satisfies

k w_d=w_n n

For the registered positive geometry carrier g=g_n/g_d, the cross section is the existing exact composition

\[
σ=w\cdot g
\]

Its reduced positive representation satisfies the full source-normalized equation

\[
(k g_n) σ_d=σ_n (n g_d)
\]

The uniqueness theorem for positive reduced fractions proves that any admitted positive carrier satisfying this equation equals σ. No fitted multiplier is introduced. The geometry's recorded inscription does not select or alter the mathematical carrier used in that composition.

The complete incoming-to-outgoing map retains one row per original channel and preserves every preparation, detector and source field. Its length is n, and every original channel occurs in it. The empirical collision-event and reconstructed-outgoing-object records are checked separately against the sealed relation. 431. Conserved particle decay transitions

A decay record retains the recurrent input constituent, the lower-recurrence joint output, a nonempty list of product words, and the complete pairing of conserved labels and mechanical carriers. The mechanical-carrier type retains the original energy-transfer and momentum records; these are not replaced by untyped particle-name tokens. Each carrier is assigned to a generated product index or a named boundary carrier, together with its source trace.

[(carrier,trace) : \operatorname{released}(L)]=[(carrier,trace) : \operatorname{received}(L)]

Every aggregate F of the full label and mechanical-carrier records consequently satisfies

\[
F(\operatorname{released}(L))=F(\operatorname{received}(L))
\]

The occurrence-level statements hold in both directions: every received carrier has its source occurrence, and every source occurrence has its recorded destination. This is the exact closure that excludes an unrecorded source or an unpaired disappearance.

The generated product list has the form [p₁] ++ P, so its length is strictly positive. The retained finite recurrence comparison is

period(outputJoint)<period(input),

A_{\text{input-period}}(\mathrm{input})=\mathrm{input}
\]
\[
A_{\text{output-period}}(\mathrm{outputJoint})=\mathrm{outputJoint}
\]

The structural transition therefore retains both recurrent words, their ordered product support and every carrier crossing the boundary. The registered lifetime, decay-mode and branching records remain empirical comparisons to this sealed transition structure.

432. State mixing as cyclic overlap of observation refinements

The common support is the complete prepared Fold state, including every word and held phase label. Let P(b) and I(b) be the exact preparation and interaction selections on a branch b. Their joint observed support in state s is

O(P,I;s)=[b∈branches(s) : P(b) and I(b)],
\[
N(P,I;s)=|O(P,I;s)|
\]

Selection is proved in both directions: a branch belongs to O exactly when it belongs to the complete original support and both selections accept it. Thus

0≤N(P,I;s)≤|branches(s)|.

The two selections retain their separate roles. A branch on which P and I disagree witnesses that they are different refinements, rather than two names for the same selection.

An admitted finite spin action advances held phases through the original phase cycle. For a generated action A with orientation trace a and cycle length m, the complete resulting branch sequence is determined by the original shift with residue |a| mod m. Two admitted actions with equal residues therefore give the same overlap support and exact count for the fixed observation refinements. The original word support is preserved:

support(A(s))=support(s).

A complete cycle returns the state and both observation quantities:

\[
A_m(s)=s
\]
\[
O(P,I;A_m(s))=O(P,I;s)
\]
\[
N(P,I;A_m(s))=N(P,I;s)
\]

A difference between overlap counts at intermediate generated actions necessarily distinguishes their observed supports. The mixing readout is this exact cyclic overlap, with the constituent support retained throughout. No additional constituent or stochastic source is introduced by a changed observed label. The separate registered mixing and oscillation records are evaluated against the sealed structural relation.

433. Nuclear binding and the positive released carrier

Let the separated inertial carrier be u=u_n/u_d and the bound joint-word carrier be b=b_n/b_d. The source's binding domain has strictly greater separated support,

\[
L=u_n b_d > R=b_n u_d
\]

The positive reduction Δ is the existing normalized Fold remainder of these carriers. Its exact reduced representation satisfies

\[
(L-R) \Delta _d=\Delta _n u_d b_d
\]
Δ_n>0.

This is an oriented positive remainder, not a negative mass. Constructive remainder reconstruction proves the complete balance

\[
L \Delta _d=\Delta _n u_d b_d+R \Delta _d
\]

The positive reduced representation of Δ is unique: any admitted carrier satisfying the same exact cross-product equation equals this normalized reduction.

The bound joint record retains the full recurrent word, its complete constituents, source trace and named destination for the released carrier. Applying the already derived two-propagation conversion to Δ gives the released energy E=Δc². With c=c_n/c_d, the native equation is

\[
(\Delta _n c_n^{2}) E_d=E_n (\Delta _d c_d^{2})
\]

The release therefore pairs the exact observed separation of inertial support with the corresponding positive energy carrier. The destination and complete source trace remain in the released record. The bound word retains its generated full-cycle return, and the registered nuclear mass, level and binding records retain their separate empirical role.

434. Finite nuclear recurrence classes and carrier transitions

A nuclear level retains its boundary-closed joint word, complete recurrence trace and observed class signature τ. Names do not select the class. For the complete finite source list L, the level census is

C(L)=\operatorname{unique}([\tau (l) : l\in L])
\]

The constructive census has no duplicate signature and satisfies

\[
\tau \in C(L) \iff  \text{there exists }l\in L\text{ with }\tau (l)=\tau 
\]

\[

\]

\]

\[

\]

443. Self-similar support and exact finite-tail convergence

Let m denote the retained label count. The empty host accumulator has support C₀=1, and each appended label position multiplies the support by m:

\[
C_0=1,\qquad C_{d+1}=m C_d,\qquad C_d=m^d
\]

The induction is exact at every finite depth: m·m^d=m^(d+1). For three labels the first three supports are 3, 9 and 27. Appending either held binary label increases word length by exactly one. The appended words are distinct and both return to the original word under the Fold return. The transported local separation doubles; the source witness is 2·(2/35)=4/35. Within the original exponent grammar {1,2,3,4}, the equation 2^e=2 retains exactly e=1.

At binary depth d the source's adjacent-carrier gap is

\[
a_d = (2+2^d)/(3+2^d) - (1+2^d)/(2+2^d)
\]
\[
= 1/[(2+2^d)(3+2^d)]
\]

Writing D_d=(2+2^d)(3+2^d), one has a_d=1/D_d. Both factors strictly increase with d because 2^(d+1)=2·2^d>2^d. Therefore D_(d+1)>D_d. Also D_d≥2^d, giving the exact majorant a_d≤2^(−d).

For the actual finite partial sum S(d,n)=Σ_(j=0)^(n−1) a_(d+j), retain an integer numerator and positive denominator, S(d,n)=N_(d,n)/Q_(d,n). Their recurrence is

\[
N_{d,0}=0,   Q_{d,0}=1
\]
\[
N_{d,n+1}=N_{d,n}D_{d+n}+Q_{d,n}
\]
\[
Q_{d,n+1}=Q_{d,n}D_{d+n}
\]

The zero numerator here denotes the empty host accumulator. Every nonempty term is positive. Induction using D_(d+n)≥2^(d+n) proves

\[N_{d,n}2^{d+n}+2Q_{d,n}\leq2^{n+1}Q_{d,n}.\]

or, equivalently,

\[S(d,n)+\frac{2}{2^{d+n}}\leq\frac{2}{2^d}.\]

The base is equality at n=0. For the successor, multiply the preceding inequality by the new positive denominator, insert the recurrence, and use 2^(d+n)≤D_(d+n) to bound the newly added numerator. This proves the bound for the actual summed gap ledger at every depth and count. The explicit positive remainder 2/2^(d+n) halves with every successor, so every finite tail satisfies S(d,n)<2/2^d. No measured tail or imported limiting value selects the bound.

The original fourteen successive denominator comparisons and eleven-term rational bracket are retained, including Σ_(d=0)^10 1/[(2+2^d)(3+2^d)]<11/60. The complete 256-form source grammar, closure and controls agree with fresh native execution, and all exported declarations have empty Lean axiom dependencies.

444. Source-bound relational spacetime events

An event relation retains the original source observation s, the adjacent transition e→e′, its source identity and action record, one generated recurrence clock C, one oriented spatial relation x, and the complete causal predecessor path P:s→e. The complete source-to-event path is the append

\[
P′ = P \cdot  (e\to e′)
\]

Every edge of P′ belongs to the held adjacency relation. Its event ledger and transition ledger are exactly

\[
\operatorname{Events}(P′)=\operatorname{Events}(P) ++ [e′]
\]
\[
\operatorname{Changes}(P′)=\operatorname{Changes}(P) ++ [\operatorname{record}(e\to e′)]
\]
\[
n(P′)=n(P)+1
\]

Thus the new event retains every predecessor and introduces exactly its generated transition. Mapping the complete transition ledger to source/action pairs reproduces the full original source trace. No causal predecessor is replaced by a numerical summary.

The recurrence clock has a positive closed transition count c=n(C). The complete path also has positive count n=n(P)+1. Its exact temporal relation is the reduced positive fraction t=n/c. Writing t=N/D, the normalization theorem gives

\[
nD=Nc,   N>0,   D>0
\]

The clock's recurrence closes on its original carrier. The spatial relation separately retains both observed supports, their reference identities, the positive exact separation and its held orientation. Numerical duration and separation do not replace the source observations or causal records.

Appending a further adjacent event retains the source and clock and extends both complete ledgers by exactly one record. A change in the held clock, spatial relation or source observation remains a distinguishable event relation. Reconstructing the relation from all of its retained fields gives the original relation exactly. These results formalize the source's operational event construction without an external background coordinate manifold.

445. Canonical interval under reference relabeling

The interval construction retains an exact temporal relation t, positive spatial separation x, held orientation o and complete causal record c. Write their joint separation as s=(t,x,o,c). A reference description is d=(s,L), where L contains the description labels. Relabeling replaces only L:

\[
R_{L′}(s,L)=(s,L′),   κ(s,L)=s
\]

The original equivalence is d∼e exactly when κ(d)=κ(e). Equality of the canonical record is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. More precisely,

\[
d\sim e\iff R_{\operatorname{labels}(e)}(d)=e
\]

The forward direction substitutes the equal separation record and retains e's labels. The reverse direction projects the separation record from the relabeling equality. Thus equivalence changes reference labels only. Temporal relation, spatial separation, held orientation and causal records are individually preserved, and equality of all four fields suffices for equivalence.

Every separation has the representative rep(s)=(s,[]), with κ(rep(s))=s. For any result f that is invariant under every reference relabeling, define its induced interval result by g(s)=f(rep(s)). Then

\[
g(\kappa(d))=f(R_{[]}(d))=f(d)
\]

If another function h satisfies h(κ(d))=f(d) for every description, substitution of d=rep(s) gives h(s)=f(rep(s))=g(s). This is pointwise uniqueness of the induced result. It establishes the canonical interval's universal property without a quotient axiom or a chosen preferred reference label.

For a generated event relation r, the separation is constructed from its exact elapsed recurrence ratio, its retained positive spatial separation and orientation, and its complete causal transition ledger. 446. Causal accessibility on finite recurrence support

\]

The retained event has no transition and witnesses a≼_R a. For paths P:a→b and Q:b→c, concatenation preserves their complete ordered ledgers and satisfies

\[
n(P\cdot Q)=n(P)+n(Q)
\]

Consequently a≼_R b and b≼_S c imply a≼_(R+S) c. Increasing the available support preserves any existing witness. Appending one admitted adjacent transition extends accessibility from R to R+1 and adds exactly that transition to the record.

The original antisymmetry statement concerns irreversible records. Such records retain a finite history H(a), and each irreversible adjacent extension strictly increases its length. |H(a)|<|H(b)|≤|H(a)|,

which is impossible. The forward path must be the retained event, giving a=b. The structural boundary-growth law is derived and sealed before the experiment. The observed compatible family cannot supply or alter that law. The boundary-growth method receives an exact distance ratio r>1 and a complete ordered response interval 1<L≤U after the prediction method is sealed. It starts with exponent one and predicted ratio r. Each successor multiplies the current prediction by the same held ratio. Every exponent whose prediction belongs to [L,U] is retained; the method stops at the first strict excess above U.

Write r=a/b with a>b>0 and U=u/v with v>0. These are representations of the held observations, not adjustable scientific constants. The positive-power recurrence is r^(n+1)=r^n·r. A constructive lower bound valid for every finite n is

b·a^n ≥ b^n(b+n).

The base n=0 is equality. For the successor, a≥b+1 and

\[
(b+n)(b+1)=b(b+n+1)+n\ge b(b+n+1)
\]

Multiplying the induction hypothesis by b+1 and then using b+1≤a establishes the bound at n+1. Thus the stopping depth can be derived from the actual input. Set N=bu+1. Since ub<b+N, the bound gives

u·b^N<a^N≤v·a^N,

so r^N>U. Every later power remains above U: multiplying a strict excess by b and using a>b preserves strict excess at the successor. Consequently every compatible positive exponent lies strictly below N. This is a proved termination bound derived from the observed rational inputs; it is not a fixed search cutoff.

The numerical selection is performed by exact whole cross-products:

\[
L\le r^n \iff  l\cdot b^n\le l_d\cdot a^n
\]
\[
r^n\le U \iff  v\cdot a^n\le u\cdot b^n
\]

where L=l/l_d. The source stop-scan is proved equal to the complete finite interval census: after the first strict excess, every remaining candidate in that census is rejected by the successor theorem. The first-excess index itself has a proved above-endpoint certificate, and its next power is strictly larger. No logarithm, fitted exponent, regression or imported physical dimension enters the method.

The original synthetic calls retain exponent three for r=3 and L=U=27, and for r=2 with [L,U]=[7,9]. For r=5/2 and U=40, the first strict-excess exponent is five, and the original monotonic-stop certificate is true. The public exact-fraction, distance-above-One and complete ordered response-interval guards are retained. The full ten-axis grammar contains 1,024 forms and retains the original source-bound, post-seal measurement boundary.

The source grammar tests source, distance, response, scale, candidates, selection, stopping, target, record and extension. Its ordered coordinate product has \(2^{10}=1024\) forms. The positive ratio recurrence, interval test and first strict excess prove the admitted candidate, selection and stopping coordinates for each supplied interval; a fixed search depth or first-match selector fails those criteria. 449. Generated common support and finite convergence witnesses

The common running coordinate starts at One and applies binary succession. At positive level n, write k=n−1. Induction on the exact succession loop gives

\[
R_n=2^{n-1},     R_{n+1}=2R_n
\]

The complete sector ladder P=(2,3,5,7) is held at every level. For p∈P and R>0, the inventory construction gives g_p(R)=(p+R−1)/(p+R). Its positive shortfall and binary-successor gain are

\[
1-g_p(R)=1/(p+R)
\]
\[
g_p(2R)-g_p(R)=R/[(p+R)(p+2R)]>0
\]

For the latter identity, the common numerator is

\[
(p+2R-1)(p+R)-(p+R-1)(p+2R)=R
\]

For p<q, the exact pair gap is Δ_(p,q)(R)=(q−p)/[(p+R)(q+R)]. Both denominator factors strictly increase under R↦2R, while the positive numerator remains q−p. Hence

0<Δ_(p,q)(2R)<Δ_(p,q)(R).

Let the finite positive tolerance be 1/d. Starting at support One, the original binary-cover procedure stops at a generated support R≥(q−p)d. Its retained succession record identifies R=2^k and level k+1. Because p,q are positive,

(q−p)d≤R<(p+R)(q+R),

and therefore Δ_(p,q)(R)<1/d. This is a finite witness for each positive whole denominator, with no completed-infinite proof value. The source certificate retains all six ordered sector pairs and all six denominators (1,2,3,5,7,11), giving 36 witnesses; each satisfies both the binary-support bound and the strict gap comparison. The initial six levels retain supports (1,2,4,8,16,32). For example, required support 55 is covered at level seven with support 64.

450. Inertial-frame correspondence from complete invariant records

An inertial reference assigns a name to each complete generated record and recovers that same record from its name. Write N_A:R→L_A and D_A:L_A→R for naming and recovery in reference A. Completeness and faithful labeling give

\[
D_A(N_A(r))=r,     N_A(D_A(x))=x
\]

For references A and B, the correspondence is therefore

\[
T_{AB}(x)=N_B(D_A(x))
\]

Recovery in B gives D_B(T_AB(x))=D_A(x). The inverse follows directly:

\[
T_{BA}(T_{AB}(x))=N_A(D_B(N_B(D_A(x))))=N_A(D_A(x))=x
\]

Thus T_AB is injective, and each y in L_B has preimage T_BA(y), proving surjectivity. Identity and composition are forced by the same recovery equations:

\[
T_{AA}(x)=x,     T_{BC}(T_{AB}(x))=T_{AC}(x)
\]

The complete invariant record retains the event-coincidence identity, canonical interval class and limiting causal-path record. Equality of those three fields gives equality of the whole record. If a proposed relabeling F preserves all three fields, then D_B(F(x))=D_A(x), and applying N_B forces F(x)=T_AB(x). This is pointwise uniqueness of the source correspondence. A different coordinate assignment at any held record therefore fails at least one retained invariant.

Uniform recurrence and translation are retained through their generated successor S:R→R. The reference description of that successor is S_A=N_A∘S∘D_A. Substitution gives

\[
T_{AB}(S_A(x))=S_B(T_{AB}(x))
\]

Induction on the finite recurrence count yields T_AB(S_A^n(x))=S_B^n(T_AB(x)) for every generated n. Event coincidence, interval class and causal accessibility are preserved throughout the complete successor record. The original 256-form grammar, two CODATA reference rows, source custody and adverse control remain attached to this correspondence.

452. Elementary causal support and the invariant limiting ratio

An elementary source-bound event retains its adjacent causal transition, spatial support and recurrence clock. \[
v_*=l/t,   n_l d_t d_v=n_v d_l n_t
\]

No speed is assigned to an absent recurrence: the EmptyOne temporal case has no quotient. Equality of the complete interval record preserves both spatial separation and positive duration, and therefore preserves their quotient. An inertial correspondence reads back the same elementary record, so v_*(b.read(b.name(a.read(x))))=v_*(a.read(x)). This is the boundary invariance inherited from the already derived exact frame correspondence.

For an accessible path making n elementary support advances during R retained recurrence units, causal accessibility supplies n≤R. Writing one elementary support-to-recurrence ratio as A/B, positivity gives

\[
(nA)B \le  (RA)B = A(RB)
\]

Thus nA/(RB)≤A/B. One elementary advance in one recurrence attains equality. This bound uses the complete retained causal path and its recurrence budget; it introduces no independent propagation coefficient.

453. Relative clock accumulation on complete causal paths

Let P and Q be complete causal paths between the same first and last events. Their positive retained recurrence counts are n=N(P) and m=N(Q). The source clock-rate correspondence is the normalized positive ratio

\[
r=n/m,    n d_r=n_r m,    n_r>0
\]

Reversing the reference paths exchanges n and m; reversing twice returns the original complete path record. The correspondence therefore compares generated recurrence accumulations without introducing an absolute external time carrier.

The value is forced by the retained counts. If another positive reduced candidate q satisfies n d_q=n_q m, multiplication and cancellation give

\[
m(n_q d_r)=(n d_q)d_r=(n d_r)d_q=m(n_r d_q)
\]

Since m>0, n_q d_r=n_r d_q. Thus every count-preserving candidate has the same rational value as r; no independent clock-rate coefficient remains. For a third positive reference count k, exact normalized composition telescopes:

\[
(n/m)(m/k)=n/k
\]

An inertial naming correspondence reads back the same complete causal-path pair. Applying the recurrence-count ratio to the recovered pair therefore returns the original ratio. Common endpoints are retained in the path types, and the already established event, interval and limiting-boundary records remain unchanged under this naming correspondence. The empirical boundary remains the registered GWOSC timing and source-frame/detector-frame records.

454. Complete simultaneous support and relative spatial extent

Let U be the retained whole spatial support and let π assign each support observation its held clock label. The simultaneous slice at label τ retains exactly

\[
S_\tau=\{s\in U:\pi(s)=\tau\}
\]

Both directions of membership are retained: every member of S_τ belongs to U and has clock label τ; every member of U at τ belongs to S_τ. If τ≠σ, no support observation belongs to both slices, since that would give τ=π(s)=σ. The positive count of a slice is its complete list length. For two positive slice counts n and m, the relative extent is the normalized positive ratio a=n/m, satisfying n d_a=n_a m. A slice compared with itself has normalized numerator and denominator both One.

The paired change of extent and clock records is expressed in the original support-per-recurrence boundary. Let t and u be the respective positive recurrence counts. Preserving that boundary gives nu=mt. Put b=t/u. Normalization gives n d_a=n_a m and t d_b=n_b u. The retained pairing then forces

\[
(mu)(n_a d_b)=(n d_a)(u d_b)
\]
\[
=(nu)(d_a d_b)
\]
\[
=(mt)(d_a d_b)
\]
\[
=(m d_a)(t d_b)
\]
\[
=(mu)(n_b d_a)
\]

Since mu>0, n_a d_b=n_b d_a, so the extent and clock ratios have the paired exact value required by the preserved boundary. 455. Universal free response and local inertial–gravitational equivalence

456. Source-bound transport and relational curvature

T_p(o)≠T_q(o).

A path cannot witness nonclosure against itself. Any nonclosing comparison therefore distinguishes two paths. The forward implication follows because equal orientations have equal names; the reverse follows from injectivity. Let D and F be the declared finite direction and frequency supports. The complete observation support is their ordered product

\]
  x ∈ B(R) ↔ background(x) ∈ R.
The complete tagged sequence remains available, so foreground separation does not replace the original observation history.

\[
\forall  r \in  cells, \operatorname{class}(r) = θ
\]
The cell census is nonempty. If both θ and θ′ satisfy this equation, selecting any retained cell gives θ = class(r) = θ′. A discordant retained cell excludes consistency. Together with the full declared direction/frequency product, this distinguishes the source's background class from a favorable selection of cells. Every curving source therefore comes from the original causal trace. No additional interaction is inserted into the path construction.

The distance-support equivalence is exactly
\[
r ~ s \iff  \Sigma (r) = \Sigma (s)
\]
Equality supplies reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. Its exact class is retained as the predicate
\[

without introducing a quotient axiom. Both recurrence carriers and every causal change remain explicit components of Σ.

\[
\operatorname{kind}(p) = \operatorname{kind}(q) \land  \Sigma (\operatorname{record}(p)) = \Sigma (\operatorname{record}(q))
\]
Different kinds therefore cannot be conflated, even when they concern the same source and observer. Source/detector relabeling changes neither the support signature nor its equivalence class. 469. Exact partition closure and spatial flatness

Let an admitted partition be a nonempty finite list p_i=n_i/d_i of strictly positive exact fractions, with d_i>0. Its total is evaluated by the exact recurrence
\[
N_0=0, D_0=1
\]
\[
N_{k+1}=N_k d_{k+1}+n_{k+1} D_k
\]
\[
D_{k+1}=D_k d_{k+1}
\]
Induction gives N_k/D_k=sum_(i=1)^k p_i. Consequently the source condition sum_i p_i=One is exactly N_m=D_m. The closed_partition operation rejects an empty list, a non-Fraction input, a nonpositive part or a total unequal to One. An admitted closed partition returns EMPTY_ONE, the source's structural-absence scalar. The arithmetic accumulator is an exact representation of the sum; it does not replace that returned scalar by a physical numerical-zero object.

For a selected parent p=n/d, write its two proposed children as a=u/v and b=w/z, with a,b>0. The refinement is admitted exactly when the index identifies an existing part and
\[
a+b=p
\]
\[
d(uz+wv)=nvz
\]
The resulting list is prefix ++ [a,b] ++ suffix. All untouched parts and their order are retained. In particular, refine_partition imposes its positivity conditions on the two children; it does not add a new positivity guard on untouched parts. Its original Boolean-index interpretation is preserved.

Let (N,D) and (N',D') be the exact total pairs before and after this replacement. Distributing the common prefix and suffix factors through the accumulator gives
\[
d N'=vz N
\]
\[
d D'=vz D
\]
Since d>0, N=D implies N'=D'. Thus every admitted positive exact split of a closed positive partition preserves closure to EMPTY_ONE. For a finite refinement sequence P_0 -> P_1 -> ... -> P_k, the base is the initial closure and the successor is this same replacement identity; induction yields
\[
\operatorname{closed\_partition}(P_0)=\mathrm{EMPTY\_ONE}
\]
\[
\Longrightarrow \operatorname{closed\_partition}(P_k)=\mathrm{EMPTY\_ONE}
\]
for every finite k and every admitted sequence. No preferred split ratio or refinement depth is introduced. This is the source's depth-independent flatness derivation.

The external curvature comparison retains its empirical status. The registered Planck TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO record has central orientation positive, magnitude 0.0007 and complete 68-percent uncertainty 0.0019. In the registered signed observational coordinate its interval is
  [(7-19)/10000, (7+19)/10000]
\[
= [-0.0012, 0.0026]
\]
which contains the structural-absence prediction at the coordinate origin. The uncertainty, confidence region, data combination and equation-47b source locator remain part of the measured record. They are neither derived constants nor premises of partition closure.

The native representation retains all eleven original grammar axes and all 2,048 alternatives, with the original elimination decisions, three operational witnesses, controls and source-bound validation method.

470. Complete generated cosmic budget

The previously derived generator g=3 has spatial volume g^g=27. Its least complete binary cover has depth D=5 and support N=2^D=32. A complete boundary pair retains two states per depth. Writing P(D) for their count, P(0)=0 and P(D+1)=P(D)+2, so induction gives P(D)=2D. At the derived depth this yields
\[
P=2D=10, F=N-P=22
\]
\[
f_m=P/N=10/32=5/16
\]
\[
f_v=F/N=22/32=11/16
\]
The support partition P+F=N therefore gives f_m+f_v=1.

The independently generated within-matter split retains D states against g^g states:
\[
f_{b|m}=D/N=5/32
\]
\[
f_{cd|m}=g^g/N=27/32
\]
\[
f_{b|m}+f_{cd|m}=(5+27)/32=1
\]
Composition with the total matter share gives
\[
f_b=f_m f_{b|m}=(5/16)(5/32)=25/512
\]
\[
f_{\mathrm{cd}}=f_m f_{cd|m}=(5/16)(27/32)=135/512

473. Unified Constants: the foundation-order object

The Unified Constants Object assembles the admitted electromagnetic, lepton, quark, dark/baryon, Hubble, Planck-hierarchy and vacuum constructions through one rooted incidence graph. It is the distinct v3 Unified Constants entry; it does not rename or replace the Physics Grand Lock. Its physical construction uses the Fold-derived binary count b=2 and generator c=3, spatial rank s=3 and boundary rank t=2. No measured constant selects these quantities.

For the source's dependency probe, c is a whole count at least three. Define the positive least covers
\[
 d(c)=\min\{k\ge1:b^k\ge c^s\},\qquad
 u(c)=\min\{k\ge1:b^k\ge c^{s+1}\}.
\]
The implementation advances support by multiplication with its supplied binary argument until it first covers the carrier. Its constructive run proof establishes both coverage and strict failure at every earlier positive depth. Positive power is repeated multiplication, P(a,1)=a and P(a,n+1)=P(a,n)*a; the positive predecessor of n>1 is the unique p>=1 with p+1=n. These are operations on generated counts, not selectable scientific coefficients.

Write B_d=b^d, B_u=b^u and C=b*d^c. The full sixteen-field foundation vector is
\[
 F(c)=(b,c,s,t,d,u,A,L,Q_d,Q_u,R,f_D,H,P,V,1/b),
\]
where every component follows from the same generated counts:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A&=B_u+c^b\frac{C+1}{C},& L&=\frac1{bc^d-1},\\
 Q_d&=\frac1{cB_d-1},&Q_u&=\frac1{cB_u-1},\\
 R&=\frac{c^s}{d},&f_D&=\frac{c^s}{B_d},\\
 H&=1+\frac{c-1}{cb^s},&P&=\frac{B_u-1}{b},\\
 V&=\frac1{b^{4d}}.&&
 \end{aligned}
\]

At the admitted generator, 2^4<3^3<=2^5 and 2^6<3^4<=2^7 force d=5 and u=7. Consequently C=2*5^3=250 and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A&=128+9\frac{251}{250}=\frac{34259}{250},\\
 L&=\frac1{2\cdot3^5-1}=\frac1{485},\\
 Q_d&=\frac1{3\cdot32-1}=\frac1{95},\qquad Q_u=\frac1{3\cdot128-1}=\frac1{383},\\
 R&=\frac{27}{5},\quad f_D=\frac{27}{32},\quad H=1+\frac{2/3}{8}=\frac{13}{12},\\
 P&=\frac{127}{2},\quad V=\frac1{2^{20}},\quad \frac1b=\frac12.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is a complete ordered vector; no sector is omitted to select a favourable headline.

The source's successor probe replaces c=3 by c=4 while holding b,s,t fixed. It is a controlled dependency test, not an adjustable parameter in the physical model. The cover calculations become 2^5<4^3<=2^6 and 2^7<4^4<=2^8, hence d=6 and u=8. Recomputing every component gives the following complete comparison:

and the terminal product is the source's positive take

476. Microstate-to-macrostate observation

A thermal macrostate retains the complete observation fibre of a finite generated microstate support. Let S be the nonempty ordered support with distinct microstate labels, and let phi assign exactly one observed label to every member of S. The inherited entropy partition computes
\[
M_o=\operatorname{filter}_{\phi(s)=o}(S),\qquad
P(S,\phi)=[(o,M_o):o\text{ occurs in }\phi(S)].
\]
Observed labels occur in first-occurrence order; microstates retain their original support order. Thus the construction preserves predecessor identity as well as multiplicity. Its completeness and exclusivity are
\[
\forall s\in S\;\exists o\;(o,M_o)\in P(S,\phi)\land s\in M_o,
\qquad s\in M_o\cap M_p\Longrightarrow o=p.
\]
The first implication follows from total observation coverage. For the second, membership in either fibre gives the image of the same microstate; equality of those images forces equality of labels. The defining filter then forces the member lists to coincide. The native theorem eachMicrostateHasUniqueMacrostate combines the already established coverage, disjointness and exact-fibre theorems. Distinctness of S is inherited by every filtered class, so no predecessor is duplicated.

For each class, the inherited ledger retains its complete ordered member list, its unresolved pairs, and the normalized exact support part. If that part is n_o/d_o, normalization preserves
\[
|M_o|d_o=n_o|S|,\qquad
U_o=\{(s_i,s_j):s_i,s_j\in M_o,\ i<j\}.
\]
The native exactMultiplicity theorem binds the existing rational normalization proof to this thermal entry. unresolvedFibreRetained binds the ledger's uncertainty field to the complete predecessor-pair construction. A singleton class has structural empty-One uncertainty; the distinction ledger is not replaced by a fitted probability or an imported entropy score.

The One case is P([s],[(s,o)])=[(o,[s])]. For a fresh microstate x assigned label v, the exact successor is
\[
S'=S\mathbin{+\!+}[x],\quad \phi'=\phi\mathbin{+\!+}[(x,v)],\qquad
M'_o=M_o\mathbin{+\!+}
\begin{cases}[x],&v=o,\\[],&v\ne o.\end{cases}
\]
The induction preserves every earlier member and appends precisely the new member to its named class. 477. Temperature carrier and thermal ordering

The source defines temperature by comparing the exact change of energy support with the exact change of accessible-state multiplicity, relative to one held thermal reference. Each native transition retains its complete before and after macro-observation fibres and its original mechanical energy-transfer record. The inherited partition guard establishes a positive member count for each named macrostate. If those counts are m_before and m_after, their exact multiplicities are normalized m/1 and the accessible change is the source scalar subtraction
\[
\Delta M=\operatorname{subtract}(m_{\rm after}/1,m_{\rm before}/1).
\]
Subtraction retains a held orientation and a positive rational magnitude when a distinction remains; equality produces structural empty One. The energy change is the already derived MechanicalWorkEnergy.energyChange of the full retained interaction, not an independent fitted quantity. The thermal carrier and its reading relative to reference R are
\[
\Theta(t)=\operatorname{divide}(\Delta E(t),\Delta M(t)),\qquad
\Theta_R(t)=\operatorname{divide}(\Theta(t),\Theta(R)).
\]
Both divisions use the original calculator operation. For positive magnitudes x=a/b and y=c/d, the quotient is the reduced positive fraction representing ad/(bc). Its exact preservation equation is
\[
(ad)q_{\rm den}=q_{\rm num}(bc).
\]
The held orientation is the product of the two source orientations. Empty energy divided by a nonempty carrier remains structural empty One. A structural empty-One divisor produces the source's mandatory undefined-division halt. In particular, unchanged accessible multiplicity is detected before assigning a thermal quotient; the implementation does not insert a replacement value at that boundary.

The order compares the exact reference-relative readings. Positive magnitudes are compared by their cross products:
\[
\frac ab\preceq\frac cd\iff ad\le cb,\qquad
\frac ab=\frac cd\iff ad=cb.
\]
Reflexivity and totality follow from natural-number comparison. Antisymmetry forces equal cross products. To show transitivity for x, y and z, multiply the first comparison by z's positive denominator and the second by x's positive denominator, align their middle products, and cancel y's positive denominator. Thus
\[
x_ny_d\le y_nx_d,\quad y_nz_d\le z_ny_d
\Longrightarrow
 y_d(x_nz_d)\le y_d(z_nx_d)
\Longrightarrow x_nz_d\le z_nx_d.
\]
The native proof uses the existing constructive multiplication associativity theorem. The source's counter-held orientation reverses magnitude comparison; structural empty One and opposite orientations retain their original comparison branches. Once the held reference is fixed, every reading and comparison is determined by the retained source records.

478. Thermal equilibrium under reciprocal exchange

\[
C\sim D\iff V(C)=V(D)
\iff M_L(C)=M_L(D)\land M_R(C)=M_R(D)\land\theta(C)=\theta(D).
\]
Projection of the view equality yields each component condition. Conversely, the three equalities reconstruct the view equality. This establishes the source's separate-class and thermal-order criterion. A change in either class or the thermal reading excludes preservation. Because equality is reflexive, symmetric and transitive,
\[
C\sim C,\qquad C\sim D\Longrightarrow D\sim C,\qquad
C\sim D\land D\sim E\Longrightarrow C\sim E.
\]
These proofs apply to every admitted coupled state and preserve the same held reference through composition.

Both ledger entries retain the carrier c. The inherited closed-ledger theorem gives

\operatorname{outgoingSupport}(L(t))=
\operatorname{incomingSupport}(L(t)).
\]
The native Exchange object binds this complete reciprocal ledger to its before and after coupled states. sourceCriterion establishes that its equilibrium predicate is precisely the three preservation conditions above. 485. Thermodynamic state relation and removal of dependent coordinates

The source names four independently observed carrier roles: support content, boundary response, thermal order and energy. The native StateRow retains those four fields together. A RegisteredDomain supplies the complete finite state list D and its source-bound observation map O into those rows. The generated relation is
\[
R_D(r)\iff\exists x\in D,\ O(x)=r.
\]
Closure requires every registered state to have its observed row in the relation. completeClosure establishes this directly: for x in D, x itself witnesses R_D(O(x)). Conversely, if a proposed relation Q covers every registered state, each witness of R_D(r) supplies Q(O(x)), and O(x)=r gives Q(r). Thus
\[
\operatorname{Covers}(D,Q)\Longrightarrow R_D\subseteq Q.
\]
This is leastClosedRelation: the generated relation is the least relation containing all registered observations. If Q is itself complete and minimal among complete relations, then its minimality gives Q⊆R_D, while the preceding result gives R_D⊆Q. Therefore
\[
\forall r,\ Q(r)\iff R_D(r).
\]
uniqueMinimalRelation proves this pointwise equivalence constructively. It neither selects a relation by fitting measured values nor introduces an independent equation coefficient. Deleting a generated row breaks coverage of its witnessing state; adding an ungenerated row breaks exactness. The four-field equality theorem also makes preservation explicit: two retained rows are equal exactly when their content, boundary, thermal and energy carriers are all equal.

A redundant coordinate is one reconstructible from the retained row by its source derivation h. Its expanded relation is
\[
R_D^h(r,z)\iff\exists x\in D,\ O(x)=r\land h(O(x))=z.
\]
Transporting equality through h gives the exact characterization
\[
R_D^h(r,z)\iff R_D(r)\land z=h(r).
\]
Consequently projection removes that dependent description coordinate without losing a registered carrier:
\[
\exists z,\R_D^h(r,z)\iff R_D(r).
\]
For the reverse direction choose the explicitly computed h(r). No choice axiom is required. Two admitted readings z and z' at the same retained row must both equal h(r), hence z=z'. The source-bound reconstruction h determines the redundant reading; the formalisation does not treat it as an adjustable scientific parameter.

The singleton relation contains exactly its one observed row. Extending D by a generated state x gives
\[
R_{x::D}(r)\iff O(x)=r\lor R_D(r).
\]
successorRelation proves both directions by source-list membership. Every prior row remains present, and the only appended row is the new state's actual observation. These base and successor statements preserve the original finite-domain construction independently of the separate complete candidate grammar.

505. Exact carrier recurrence preserves readings and excludes predecessor merging

\operatorname{ok}(r)=A(s,w)=\operatorname{ok}(s)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad r=s.

\[
A(a,u)=\operatorname{ok}(a)=\operatorname{ok}(r),\qquad
A(b,v)=\operatorname{ok}(b)=\operatorname{ok}(r).
\]
Constructor injectivity gives a=r and b=r, hence a=b. Distinct returning complete carriers therefore cannot merge into one result. These are consequences of the retained recurrence equality, independent of path length and of any particular scalar observation.

H(s,[])=\operatorname{ok}(s),\qquad

\operatorname{error}(e)&A(s,w)=\operatorname{error}(e).
\end{cases}
\]

At the successor, bandExactly gives A(s,w)=ok(s); substitution reduces the execution to H(s,W), and the induction hypothesis closes the step. Consequently a successful resulting carrier r satisfies r=s and R(r)=R(s) for every reading R. This is induction over arbitrary finite recurrence histories, with the existing phase action executed at every step. 506. Complete motion-distinction loss ledger

\[

\]

\[
D=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\forall(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pairs}(S),\quad
C(a)=C(b)\land O(a)=O(b)\Longrightarrow M(a)=M(b).
\]
For the forward direction, an unequal motion pair satisfying the antecedent would be a member of the empty list. Conversely, any first member of a nonempty list contradicts the stated motion equality. This condition concerns loss of a held distinction at the receiving observation; it does not require equality of scalar momentum readings at adjacent endpoints.

A closed pair cannot have both original motion labels reconstructed by one decoder of its receiving observation. If d(O(a))=M(a) and d(O(b))=M(b), the equality O(a)=O(b) gives M(a)=M(b), contradicting membership in D. For the one-carrier identity boundary with no transfers, Pairs(S) is empty and therefore D is empty; no transfer is required merely to retain the initial carrier.

\[

This establishes complete class invariance, not only endpoint agreement. If t is outside [p], the reverse implication proves it remains outside [q]. The construction retains the graph, incidence support and boundary ledger throughout the trace.

The complete source member/reference trace remains available; the total is computed from that trace. Membership elimination proves the same-kind condition over the complete successor list. A new member of a different kind contradicts admission rather than silently changing the meaning of the count.

The generated-count construction consists of the singleton base and these same-kind successors. To establish that this determines the measure, let v be any proposed measure satisfying the source base and successor equations. At the base, v=1=N. If v(M)=N(M), then
\[
v(M\mathbin{+\!+}[m])=v(M)+1=N(M)+1=N(M\mathbin{+\!+}[m]).
\]
Induction therefore gives v=N on every generated amount carrier. The count is fixed by the original construction rather than by an added scale factor. In particular, a proposed multiplier f preserving the one-member base obeys f\cdot1=1 and hence f=1.

Every admitted member list is nonempty, so its count is positive. Finite-history induction preserves the reference and every earlier member. The unit-comparison record is unchanged by member extension, and replacing that separate unit record leaves N unchanged. Reidentifying carrier data while retaining the member positions and held kinds also preserves list length. Thus the count does not depend on isotope-dependent mass data or a conventional unit scale; these cannot select the amount law.

514. Molecular formula: exact composition, retained structure and complete decoding

A molecular formula retains the composition of a discrete molecule. Write each coordinate as c_i=(e_i,n_i), where e_i is its held chemical-entity identity and n_i is its generated positive multiplicity. Let C=[c_1,...,c_k] and let H be the held sequence of structural coordinates required to distinguish the molecule. Admission requires
\[
k>0,\qquad \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\ n_i>0.
\]
The entity identity is the previously derived constitution/isotope/context record, so the label is not an anonymous symbol. The structure record H remains separate from the multiplicities: equal counts need not imply equal molecular structure.

The source base is one entity/count coordinate. The successor adjoins a coordinate and any further held structural coordinates J:
\[
(C,H)\longmapsto(C\mathbin{+\!+}[c],H\mathbin{+\!+}J).
\]
The new count must be positive. Complete append-membership elimination proves admission for every old coordinate and for the new coordinate. Removing the final composition coordinate returns exactly C; every previous structural coordinate also remains present. A zero multiplicity fails admission at the appended coordinate itself.

Define the ordered code and its decoder by
\[
E(C,H)=([(e_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^{k},H),\qquad
D([(e_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^{k},H)=([c_i]_{i=1}^{k},H).
\]
Induction over the coordinate list gives D(E(C,H))=(C,H). Consequently E(a)=E(b) implies a=D(E(a))=D(E(b))=b. This proves retention of every entity, count, position and structure coordinate. In particular, different structure records remain distinct even when the composition lists agree.

Minimality concerns the required distinctions, rather than the spelling of a conventional formula. For any other exact code E' with decoder D', the equation D'(E'(x))=x implies that E'(a)=E'(b) forces a=b and hence E(a)=E(b). Conversely, equal composition and structural records give equal E codes. The representation therefore adds no further identity distinction.

The comparison-boundary mass reconstruction reads the retained composition. Writing that source-bound reading as R(C), decoding yields
\[
R(\pi_C D(E(C,H)))=R(C).
\]
Equal composition records give the same reading; changing a separate structural record cannot select a different composition reading. R denotes the retained comparison-boundary reconstruction, not an adjustable coefficient or a numerical mass prediction introduced by this entry.

The generated domain is exactly the admitted domain. A singleton positive coordinate is generated. For any generated prefix, induction over a positive suffix constructs the corresponding append sequence. Every nonempty positive list splits into its first coordinate and such a suffix, so it is generated. Together with successor preservation this gives Generated(f) if and only if Admitted(f), at every positive finite length. The original eight binary decision axes then enumerate all 256 alternatives. The native grammar proves complete enumeration, the exact elimination decisions and the sole admitted form, preserving all original controls and closure fields.

515. Systematic nomenclature: ordered construction and exact identity decoding

A registered name part is a syllable together with an optional generated positive count prefix. For syllable register R and part p=(s,q), the source admission rule is
\[
s\in R,\qquad q=\mathrm{absent}\quad\text{or}\quad q=\mathrm{present}(n),\ n>0.
\]
The complete name retains a nonempty ordered list P of admitted parts and its admitted molecular-formula record F. A singleton supplies the first complete name. Appending an admitted part gives (P++[p],F): the prior ordered list is recovered by deleting the last part, and formula binding remains exactly F. An unregistered syllable or a present zero count is rejected. Induction over suffixes proves that every admitted positive-finite name is generated by the singleton and append constructors; induction over those constructors proves the converse.

The source does not infer reversibility from typography. Its registered decoding boundary for a retained table T is
\[
\forall a,b\in T,\quad P(a)=P(b)\Longrightarrow F(a)=F(b).
\]
The native lookup traverses T in order and returns the formula of the first matching complete word. To prove exactness for a retained name n, consider the table head a. If P(a)=P(n), the registered boundary forces F(a)=F(n), so lookup returns the required formula. Otherwise n belongs to the tail, where the boundary is inherited and the induction hypothesis applies. Thus
\[
n\in T\ \land\ \operatorname{InjectiveBoundary}(T)
\Longrightarrow\operatorname{lookup}(P(n),T)=\mathrm{some}(F(n)).
\]
Two retained rows with the same word but different formula records contradict the boundary directly. A singleton table satisfies it. Adding a new row preserves it precisely under the source compatibility requirement: every old row sharing the new word has the same formula. The proof checks new/new, new/old, old/new and old/old cases; exact decoding then applies to the extended table. This carries the original qualification through construction instead of assuming that every conventional name is reversible.

The eight original binary axes cover carrier, parts, prefix, order, binding, decoding, record and extension. Their 256 alternatives, decisions, source registration, controls and closure are retained in the native entry. Registered syllables and comparison records are explicit source data; the derivation introduces no fitted naming rule.

516. Chemical measurement uncertainty: complete alternatives and the fixed use boundary

A chemical uncertainty record retains a registered boundary B and the complete decision record D. B contains source identity, method identity, intended use, exact result identity and the exact positive upper-limit record U. Each decision carries its alternative, source identity and the registered resolution verdict. The compatible-alternative class is obtained by the existing measurement-uncertainty construction:
\[
\mathcal A(D)=\{d\text{ in the retained order of }D:\operatorname{compatible}(d)=\mathrm{true}\}.
\]
The native membership theorem establishes both directions:
\[
d\in\mathcal A(D)\iff d\in D\ \land\ \operatorname{compatible}(d)=\mathrm{true}.
\]
It therefore retains every compatible alternative and admits none without a source row. The complete decision record remains available, including rejected and adverse rows. The inductive retention relation has only empty, keep-compatible and remove-incompatible constructors. Its existing uniqueness theorem shows that any two executions of these constructors produce the same retained class.

For the source successor, append a registered decision d while retaining B:
\[
(B,D)\longmapsto(B,D\mathbin{+\!+}[d]).
\]
The existing complete-append theorem gives
\[
\mathcal A(D\mathbin{+\!+}[d])=\mathcal A(D)\mathbin{+\!+}\mathcal A([d]).
\]
When d is compatible, the final term is [d]. Every previous decision and every previous compatible alternative remains held. Source, method, intended use, result identity and U remain exactly unchanged. Adding a registered measurement result likewise appends its full record to the result ledger; it neither filters earlier rows nor replaces their boundaries.

After target release, a record respects its registration precisely when its boundary equals the previously registered B. Equality of the whole boundary implies equality of U, result identity and intended use by projection. A changed upper limit, rebound result or changed intended use therefore contradicts registration. This is an explicit rejection condition, not a retrospective fit. For an arbitrary finite history of decision extensions, induction preserves the entire boundary and every prior row, giving
\[
B_{\mathrm{last}}=B_{\mathrm{first}},\qquad
U_{\mathrm{last}}=U_{\mathrm{first}}.
\]
The upper-limit and measurement rows remain comparison records; they do not enter the candidate derivation as proof values.

517. Chemical traceability: complete certified predecessor chains

Each chemical property record r retains material identity, separate sample identity, property identity, the held value, associated uncertainty and an identified comparison reference. A certificate c binds its complete subject record, predecessor record, certificate identity and source record. An initial anchor retains one such record and its certificate, with no predecessor, together with an admitted physical reference-realization process. The existing realization theorem proves that this process has a nonempty trace and retains every source record.

A registered link from r to r' requires
\[
c\in\Gamma,\qquad\operatorname{subject}(c)=r',\qquad
\operatorname{predecessor}(c)=\mathrm{some}(r),\qquad
\operatorname{property}(r')=\operatorname{property}(r),
\]
where Gamma is the retained certificate register. These equalities bind the exact predecessor, not merely a matching displayed value. Subject equality separately gives equality of the held value, uncertainty, material and sample identities. A changed material identity contradicts that equality; a broken predecessor contradicts the predecessor equation; a certificate outside Gamma contradicts registered membership.

The source chain is generated from its certified anchor and registered successors. Let R(P) be its ordered record list, C(P) its certificate list and L(P) its length. At the base these are singleton lists and L=1. A successor satisfies
\[
R(P')=R(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[r'],\qquad
C(P')=C(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[c],\qquad L(P')=L(P)+1.
\]
Induction, using the subject-binding equality at each step, gives
\[
\operatorname{map}(\operatorname{subject},C(P))=R(P),\qquad
|R(P)|=L(P)>0.
\]
Every record therefore has its corresponding complete certificate. Append-membership preservation retains all earlier records and certificates. The anchor record remains present at every finite depth. The property identity is constant along the chain: the base equality is reflexive, and each successor composes its same-property equality with the induction hypothesis. Every certificate is either the original anchor certificate or a member of Gamma. The complete trace consequently preserves its route to the same identified reference realization without adding an unregistered link.

518. Chemical element: the complete nuclear-count class

A nuclear proton carrier is generated as one held proton followed by a finite retained list of further protons. Its exact count is Z(n)=|protons(n)|, so Z(n)>0. An atom retains that nucleus, its positive mass-number coordinate and its electron record. Element identity is
\[
a\sim b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Z(n_a)=Z(n_b).
\]
For an anchor a, the class contains every generated atom b satisfying this equality. This quantification ranges over the atom carrier itself. A finite construction trace records class members without restricting the class to that trace.

Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from count equality. If two representatives share a count, their membership predicates agree for every atom. If their classes overlap at c, then Z(a)=Z(c)=Z(b), so the representatives have the same identity. Conversely, different counts exclude membership. The held nuclear count therefore determines the class without a supplementary equivalence rule.

Mass refinement replaces the retained mass-number coordinate while leaving the nucleus unchanged. Consequently
\[
Z(\operatorname{refineMass}(a,m))=Z(a).
\]
When m differs from the original mass number, projection onto the mass field proves that the two atom records differ, even though they belong to the same element. Changing the electron record likewise leaves the nuclear count unchanged. Equal mass numbers cannot merge atoms whose proton counts differ.

The original finite construction starts with one atom and a separate pure-substance correspondence. Appending an atom of the same nuclear count preserves the membership condition for every old member and the new member. It retains the entire member record, including its mass refinement, and leaves the substance correspondence unchanged. Replacing the separate correspondence does not select a different atom class. Induction over arbitrary finite histories preserves admission, the anchor and every prior member.

519. Atomic number: unique generated count and class order

Atomic number reads the exact count of the retained nuclear proton collection. For a singleton proton p and a nuclear carrier n, the construction gives
\[
Z([p])=1,\qquad Z(n\mathbin{+\!+}[p])=Z(n)+1>Z(n).
\]
The successor retains every prior proton in order. Finite-suffix induction builds any nucleus from its first proton and the remaining list, so this is a construction of every admitted positive-finite nucleus, not a table of selected atomic numbers.

To establish uniqueness, let v obey the source singleton and successor equations. At the singleton v=1=Z. If v(n)=Z(n), then
\[
v(n\mathbin{+\!+}[p])=v(n)+1=Z(n)+1=Z(n\mathbin{+\!+}[p]).
\]
Induction over the generated nucleus proves v(n)=Z(n) everywhere. An offset k preserving the first count satisfies 1+k=1 and hence k=0; a multiplier f preserving it satisfies f*1=1 and hence f=1. Neither provides a free relabelling of the order.

Generated natural-count order is total. If Z(a)<=Z(b) and Z(b)<=Z(a), antisymmetry gives Z(a)=Z(b), hence the same element class. More precisely,
\[
Z(a)=Z(b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\forall x,\;x\in[a]\Longleftrightarrow x\in[b].
\]
The forward direction uses the element representative theorem. For the reverse direction, take x=a: a belongs to its own class, and equality of membership predicates places it in b's class. Mass refinement and electron-record changes leave Z unchanged, proving both isotope and charge-state invariance of this coordinate.

520. Isotope family: shared element and retained complementary nuclear count

A nuclide retains its complete atom record, complementary non-proton nuclear record and observation record. Its exact nucleon-count relation is
\[
A=Z+|N|,
\]
where Z is the nuclear proton count, A the positive mass number and N the retained complementary nuclear list. The isotope distinction between a and b requires Z(a)=Z(b) together with A(a) differing from A(b). Shared Z gives the same element class. Projection onto A proves that the nuclide records are distinct. If their complementary counts were equal, substitution into the displayed equation would force A(a)=A(b), a contradiction. The mass distinction therefore retains its explicit nuclear-count difference.

The source base is two nuclides with common Z and different A. A family retains one element anchor, all members and pairwise-distinct mass coordinates. For a successor c, the registered conditions are
\[
Z(c)=Z(\text{anchor}),\qquad

\]
Appending c preserves common element identity by complete append-membership elimination. To prove mass distinctness, induct over the prior family: each head already differs from every old tail member, and the fresh-coordinate condition makes it differ from c; the induction hypothesis handles the remaining suffix. Every earlier nuclide record remains present. A new member with a different atomic number contradicts admission directly.

Observation records state the retained resolution correspondence. Re-recording those observations does not erase the proton or mass coordinates or change the isotope relation. Arbitrary finite histories of admitted successors preserve the complete family, every prior member and the distinct-mass invariant. The construction thus retains a common element identity together with resolvable isotope distinctions, rather than replacing one with the other.

521. Atomic weight: exact isotope-population reconstruction

A population retains every row, its source boundary and uncertainty, and a separately registered unified-reference-unit value u with its own record. The exact calculation is
\[
T=\sum_i w_i m_i,\qquad W=\sum_i w_i,\qquad
\overline m=\frac{T}{W},\qquad A_r=\frac{\overline m}{u}.
\]
Every row remains paired throughout this calculation. The mass and abundance values are the retained source records; the reference comparison does not select the population average.

The native positive-rational product is reduced exactly. If w=a/b, m=c/d and their computed contribution is t=n/e, its proved cross-product equation is
\[
(ac)e=n(bd).
\]
The finite population is represented by one first row and a retained remainder. Its total starts from the first contribution and accumulates each subsequent one through exact rational addition. For a current total x=a/b and next contribution y=c/d, the sum s=n/e obeys
\[
(ad+cb)e=n(bd).
\]
Structural induction over the remainder proves the append equations
\[
T(P\mathbin{+\!+}[r])=T(P)+w_r m_r,\qquad
W(P\mathbin{+\!+}[r])=W(P)+w_r.
\]
A proposed accumulator obeying the same base and recursive addition equations agrees with this accumulator at every finite length. There is no further adjustment term in the construction.

The average and reference comparison use the previously proved exact quotient operation. For x=a/b, t=c/d and q=n/e, it establishes
\[
(ad)e=n(bc),
\]
which is precisely q=x/t. Applying it first to T/W and then to the retained u proves the two displayed ratio reconstructions. All accumulated quantities and quotients remain positive.

The base equations both equal 1. The successor adds 1 to the coordinate and length and appends exactly one retained record. Thus each step is strictly later, every earlier complete row remains present, and every isotope support retains its common element identity. No additional permutation rule enters the construction. 523. Periodic recurrence: complete outer traces and counted return

The periodic recurrence entry retains the complete generated outer support at each atomic-number coordinate. For a prepared boundary p and generated trace family G, the admitted support is
  S(p,G) = {t in G : phaseAction(p,t) = p}.
Each retained transition has both endpoints in S(p,G). The existing finite-recurrence theorem supplies admission when the generated trace completes the held orientation cycle. The occupation record preserves exchange traces: identical constituent words in the same cell cannot satisfy the alternating exchange condition, because exchanging that pair fixes it while the opposite held orientation differs from itself. Thus the outer carrier retains the finite boundary closure and exclusion derivations already established in the quantum construction.

Let O be the complete registered family of outer chemical observations and let L_O(a) = [f(a) : f in O] retain every full transition trace. The equivalence relation is
  a ~_O b  iff  for every f in O, f(a) = f(b).
Induction over O proves both directions of
  a ~_O b  iff  L_O(a) = L_O(b).
The empty observation list contributes no distinction; adjoining an observation requires its equality together with equality of every previously held observation. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow componentwise. Equivalent representatives therefore define the same complete class. Any relation preserving all registered observations factors through this equivalence; no additional class rule is introduced.

At atomic-number coordinates Z(a) and Z(b), the return condition and its counted period are
  R_O(a,b) iff Z(a) < Z(b) and a ~_O b,
  P(a,b) = Z(b) - Z(a).
For every return, P(a,b) > 0 and P(a,b) + Z(a) = Z(b). The earlier complete class and the ordered successor distance jointly determine the witness; an assumed fixed period cannot replace the trace-equality test. A changed registered trace rejects the proposed return.

The complete finite search examines earlier records in their held order. At each record it tests the strict coordinate order and equality of the complete observation ledger. The first successful test returns that earlier record; otherwise it continues through the remaining records. Induction proves that a returned record belongs to the history and satisfies R_O, and that an empty result is equivalent to the absence of a return at every earlier record. 524. Group and period: complete class and counted reopening coordinates

A chemical group is the equivalence class of the complete outer observation ledger established in section 523. With O the registered observations and L_O the complete ledger,
  g(a) = [a]_O,
  a ~_O b iff L_O(a) = L_O(b).
Every element belongs to its own class. Equality of ledgers is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so overlapping classes coincide. A family name cannot merge records with different ledgers.

A closure-to-reopening witness retains an earlier element a, a closed return b and its successor c, with
  Z(a) < Z(b), L_O(a) = L_O(b),
  Z(c) = Z(b) + 1, L_O(b) != L_O(c).
The first such witness supplies the source base coordinate. If H records the subsequent reopening witnesses, its counted depth is
  d(H) = 1 + |H|.
An ordinary ordered successor retains H and hence its depth. A witnessed reopening appends one witness, yielding
  d(H ++ [h]) = 1 + (|H| + 1) = d(H) + 1.
The joint coordinate is (g(a),d(H)); its computable class representation is (L_O(a),d(H)). Both components are retained with the complete element record.

The history construction implements the source base, ordinary atomic-number successor and linked reopening successor. Mapping its complete record list to element/coordinate pairs assigns every retained element and preserves the list length. 525. Valence: attained maximum of complete joining and substitution support

The carrier is a retained atom or chemical fragment together with its declared chemical context. Every generated trace records whether it is a combination or substitution, its univalent partners and its source trace. One first partner and a finite remaining partner list give the positive realized count
  n(t) = 1 + |partners_rest(t)| > 0.
The complete support is a first realized trace t_0 followed by its ordered remaining traces. Selection compares actual counts:
  select(p,t) = t if n(p) < n(t), and p otherwise.
The running maximum follows the original enumeration in order:
  M(p,[]) = p,
  M(p,t::R) = M(select(p,t),R).
This preserves the earlier witness on a tie and replaces it exactly when the fresh realized count is greater.

Induction over the remaining support proves that M(t_0,R) belongs to t_0::R and that
  for every t in t_0::R, n(t) <= n(M(t_0,R)).
The result is therefore an attained maximum, not an imported or typical count. If another retained witness u also bounds the entire support, the two inequalities imply
  n(u) = n(M(t_0,R)).
The numerical valence is unique even when more than one trace realizes it. A proposed typical count smaller than a realized member contradicts the maximum bound and is rejected.

For an appended generated trace f, induction gives the exact successor equation
  M(t_0,R ++ [f]) = select(M(t_0,R),f),
  V(R ++ [f]) = n(f) if V(R) < n(f), and V(R) otherwise.
Appending preserves the complete earlier support, carrier and context. Combination and substitution use the same retained boundary and comparison carrier; no context-free value or correction is introduced.

526. Ion formation: closed transfer and held net orientation

The chemical carrier remains an atom or a molecular record with retained constituent nuclei and chemical identity. Each electric transfer records an incoming or outgoing direction, a held fibre label, its source identity and its full action trace. It creates one edge between the particle and its boundary. The same held label occurs at both ends of that edge. Applying the existing complete network conservation theorem yields equality of the full outgoing and incoming label supports, including multiplicities and source records.

Net accounting uses two natural tallies A and B, with cancellation represented by comparison rather than a signed proof magnitude. An incoming first-fibre transfer contributes to A and an incoming second-fibre transfer to B. An outgoing transfer contributes to the opposite tally. For a transfer t, write h(t) for its incoming held label or the opposite label when outgoing. The exact update is
  add((A,B),first) = (A+1,B),
  add((A,B),second) = (A,B+1),
  account(c,[]) = c,
  account(c,t::R) = account(add(c,h(t)),R).
Every contribution therefore has a paired boundary edge; it is not unpaired charge creation.

The net result is determined completely by the two tallies:
  net(A,B) = first-held with magnitude A-B when B<A;
  net(A,B) = second-held with magnitude B-A when A<B;
  net(A,B) = neutral when A=B.
The existing subtraction induction proves that the retained difference is positive in either charged branch. Antisymmetry of the natural order proves the converse neutral criterion. Thus an ion is exactly a carrier whose accounted tallies differ. The two one-unmatched-label bases, (1,0) and (0,1), establish the two held orientations; the empty tally is bookkeeping, not a negative proof quantity.

Induction over the complete transfer history establishes
  account(c,R ++ [t]) = add(account(c,R),h(t)).
The next charge state is the net classification of this exact updated pair. Appending retains the chemical carrier and every prior transfer. For an atomic carrier, the existing electron-change theorem explicitly preserves proton count: Z(changeElectrons(a,e)) = Z(a). Molecular constituent nuclei and the molecular identity record remain in the unchanged carrier. A transfer can also neutralize a carrier; the ion predicate follows the resulting tally equality rather than assuming permanent ion status.

The original grammar enumerates all 256 products of the eight ion axes, retaining the two held fibres, positive count domain, original eliminations, unique survivor and identity/conservation/signed controls. 527. Known periodic boundary: complete release census and extensible endpoint

  Z(first) = 1,

  |R| = Z(last) = z.
Induction proves that the final row belongs to R and every listed row r satisfies Z(r) <= z. The endpoint is therefore attained within the complete census. If another listed row bounds all rows, antisymmetry gives its coordinate equal to z; the greatest listed coordinate is unique.

A new officially validated row with coordinate z+1 extends the retained sequence:
  R' = R ++ [r_new],
  z' = z+1.
Every prior element row remains in R'. Since z < Z(r_new), the old upper-bound theorem proves that r_new is absent from R; the extension construction proves that it belongs to R'. This establishes precisely why absence beyond one release does not supply a theorem of impossibility. 528. Exact chemical composition: identity-bearing positive partition of One

Each composition component retains an identity and an ExactPart. The identity must contain a non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is preserved rather than used to merge distinct labels. The part is a reduced rational n/d with 0<n<=d and d>0. Thus a present component has a positive part, while an absent component is omitted from the support.

For the complete ordered component family C, the native operation preserves V3's two admission stages. First C must be nonempty and its identities distinct. Second its exact sum must equal One. No normalization correction is applied. Using an exact numerator/denominator accumulator, the initial arithmetic state is (N,D)=(0,1), and each component n/d updates it by
  N' = N d + n D,
  D' = D d.
Consequently N'/D' = N/D + n/d. Induction over the component list gives the exact total; closure is N=D. The existing positive-part partition proofs connect this same natural-number accumulation to the rational partition operation. The bookkeeping numerator at the initial empty sum is not a present zero-valued chemical component.

The complete admission condition is therefore
  accept(C) iff C is nonempty, every identity is distinct, and N(C)=D(C).
On acceptance the output is exactly C. Empty or duplicate support is rejected before the closure test; a nonclosing exact sum is rejected without altering any part. Equality of two part values does not imply equality of their constituent identities. The original Python operation and the native Lean operation agree on the source witness (A,1/3),(B,2/3), equal-part distinct labels, duplicate identities, underfilled and overfilled totals, blank and Unicode-whitespace identities, distinct whitespace/case-sensitive labels, and large exact fractions.

For a parent p and positive subparts a,b, exact splitting is the cross-product identity
  (n_a d_b + n_b d_a)d_p = n_p d_a d_b.
The previously proved partition refinement theorem implies
  sum(B ++ [p] ++ T)=1  implies  sum(B ++ [a,b] ++ T)=1.
If the refined component identities are distinct, the chemical operation therefore accepts the refined complete support. A singleton component equal to One supplies the base. Induction over the typed finite refinement history proves closure after every finite sequence of such splits. The source boundary is retained, and the parent component list is appended to the provenance history, preserving the identities and part records from which the refinement was derived.
