529. Elemental conservation through a complete reaction word

A reaction species retains a structural reactant/product side, a nonblank chemical identity, a positive multiplicity, and a nonempty list of distinct elemental identities with positive counts. The source side-family, side-label, identity and elemental-support guards are preserved. Every named boundary carrier must be present in this same complete word; there is no unrecorded correction to the totals.

For an element label e, the formula count of species s is
  E_e(s) = sum over its elemental rows (a,n) of n when a=e, and zero otherwise.
With positive species coefficient c_s, the total on held side q is
  T_q(e,W) = sum over s in W with side(s)=q of c_s E_e(s).
The zero in this accounting expression represents absence from the named support, not a participating species with a zero coefficient. All participating multiplicities remain positive.

The native dictionary operation follows the original ordered accumulation. For each matching-side species, it multiplies each formula count by the species coefficient, adds the contribution to an existing element key, or inserts that key at its first occurrence. The lookup proof first establishes
  lookup(e,addCount(a,n,D)) = lookup(e,D) + (n if a=e, else 0).
Induction over elemental rows then gives
  lookup(e,accumulateElements(c,F,D)) = lookup(e,D) + c E_e(F).
Induction over the species word yields
  lookup(e,sideTotalsFrom(q,W,D)) = lookup(e,D) + T_q(e,W).
Thus the actual source dictionary accumulation is connected to the per-element conservation theorem, rather than being replaced by a separately asserted balance label. Unknown side names produce an empty dictionary, as in the source operation.

Let L(W) contain every elemental label in every retained species formula. The finite checker tests T_reactant(e,W)=T_product(e,W) for every e in L(W). The proof also covers every label not in that list: induction over the complete word shows that both totals are zero there. Consequently
  checkAll(L(W)) iff for every element label e, T_reactant(e,W)=T_product(e,W).
Combined with the exact side and nonempty guards,
  reaction_is_balanced(W) iff W is nonempty, both held sides occur, and every elemental total agrees.
An unequal total at any element therefore rejects the word, even if other elements or a bulk mass comparison agree.

An identity-preserving pair consists of one species and the same identity, formula and positive coefficient on the opposite held side. It contributes equal amounts to both totals. Exact list composition gives
  T_q(e,W ++ V) = T_q(e,W) + T_q(e,V).
Hence appending such a paired carrier to a closed word preserves equality for every e. The complete prior word remains retained. This provides the source base and successor closure while preserving the original species/formula records.

530. Positive stoichiometric coefficients and primitive reduction

A reaction word retains each species identity, its reactant/product side, its element-count map and its positive integer multiplicity. For multiplicities c₁,…,cₙ, the original common-factor reduction is the fold
  g₁=c₁,  gⱼ₊₁=gcd(gⱼ,cⱼ₊₁),  g=gₙ.
Every cⱼ is positive, so g>0. Induction through the gcd fold proves both g∣cⱼ for every participating species and d∣g whenever d divides all cⱼ. Thus the reduced multiplicities pⱼ=cⱼ/g are positive integers and cⱼ=g pⱼ. Species identity, orientation and formula remain unchanged.

For any element label e, let aⱼ(e) be its retained count in species j. The total on side s is Tₛ(e;c)=Σⱼ:side(j)=s cⱼaⱼ(e). Substituting cⱼ=g pⱼ gives Tₛ(e;c)=g Tₛ(e;p). A balanced input satisfies g Tᵣ(e;p)=g Tₚ(e;p); cancellation of the positive g proves balance of the reduced word for every element label. The nonempty and both-side guards are preserved as well.

The gcd scaling identity gives gcd(c₁,…,cₙ)=g gcd(p₁,…,pₙ). Since the left side is g and g>0, cancellation yields gcd(p₁,…,pₙ)=1. This connects the reduction directly to V3's primitive_coefficients acceptance test: the reduced word is balanced and its common factor is One.

For any positive integer k, gcd(kc₁,…,kcₙ)=k g, and
  (k cⱼ)/(k g)=cⱼ/g=pⱼ.
Consequently all common rescalings have the same primitive representative. If a primitive vector and its common multiple are both primitive, their gcds give k·1=1, hence k=1. This is the source's explicit unique-up-to-common-multiple construction. Only participating positive multiplicities occur; side is retained structurally rather than encoded by signed counts.

The extension retains the same conditions on the entire enlarged word. Whenever the enlarged positive word balances all element constraints, the same gcd construction supplies its primitive representative. An unbalanced extension is rejected by the original balance guard. No new balancing exception or empirical adjustment enters that reduction.

531. Limiting component: complete tied support and consumption boundary

  rⱼ=aⱼ/cⱼ=nⱼ/(dⱼcⱼ).

  j∈L  ⇔  rⱼ≤rᵢ for every participating input i.

  (x≤y for every y∈R++[r]) ⇔ ((x≤y for every y∈R) and x≤r).

532. Reaction yield: retained exact product share and cumulative observations

V3's exact_yield operation preserves its supplied exact positive product share: Y(p)=p. The admitted part p=n/d has 0<n≤d, d>0 and reduced integer numerator and denominator. Hence Y(p) is positive, at most One and unchanged by the yield operation. No product is an empty observed outcome; it is not a zero-valued member of positive yield arithmetic.

For observations of the same product relative to the same registered support, adding a new share q=a/b to the current share p=n/d gives
  p+q=(nb+ad)/(db).

  N(db)=(nb+ad)D.

  (aₙb_d+bₙa_d)d=n(a_db_d).

542. Molecular geometry: complete relative pair support

  A(O,G)={norm(g.left,g.right) : g∈G, g.left∈O, g.right∈O}.

  |G|=|A(O,G)| and A(O,G)=P(O).

543. Isomer distinction: exhaustive identity-preserving relabelling

For a molecular carrier M=(O,L,B,Q), write C(M) for its exact composition signature and E(M) for its set of normalized undirected bonds. Two carriers with unequal signatures are rejected immediately. A candidate map is admitted precisely when

  L₁(u)=L₂(φₚ(u)) for every u∈O₁,
  {norm(φₚ(u),φₚ(v)) : norm(u,v)∈E(M₁)}=E(M₂).

The first equation retains every element identity. The second requires both inclusions of the complete bond set, so neither a missing bond nor an extra bond can be hidden by a relabelling. Consequently

  structurally_equivalent(M₁,M₂)
    ⇔ C(M₁)=C(M₂) and ∃p∈Perm(O₂), candidate_matches(M₁,M₂,p),
  molecular_isomers(M₁,M₂)
    ⇔ C(M₁)=C(M₂) and not structurally_equivalent(M₁,M₂).

The source witnesses have four equal-element occurrences. The chain has bonds (a,b),(b,c),(c,d), while the branched carrier has (w,x),(w,y),(w,z). Both composition signatures are [(E,4)]. For matched appended composition A, each element count obeys

  count(ℓ,L₁++A)=count(ℓ,L₁)+count(ℓ,A),
  count(ℓ,L₂++A)=count(ℓ,L₂)+count(ℓ,A).

Equal prior counts therefore remain equal. 551. Buffer response: conjugate conversion and exact finite capacity

The source reservoir retains an admitted conjugate pair P=(A_H,A,p) and positive finite support counts h and b for its protonated and deprotonated members. Neither a pH value nor a fitted equilibrium constant selects these modes.

For a source support of n units, the response derivation records k units used and r units remaining. Its base and successor rules are

  Consumption(n,0,n),
  Consumption(n,k,r+1) ⇒ Consumption(n,k+1,r).

Each successor therefore consumes exactly one retained source unit. Induction gives the exact balance

  k+r=n.

The base reduces to 0+n=n. At a successor, (k+1)+r=k+(r+1), so the previous balance gives the new one. consumptionBalance proves this equation. Since k≤k+r, finiteCapacity derives k≤n; cannotExceedCapacity excludes every purported response sequence with k>n. The count notation includes zero to represent exhausted support in the Lean bookkeeping, while the source reservoir's initial component counts remain positive.

The capacity is attained, not merely bounded. extendConsumption proves that adding u units carries a trace Consumption(n,k,r) to Consumption(n+u,k,r+u). Applying this with u=1 to a trace consuming all n units permits one more successor, yielding Consumption(n+1,n+1,0). Starting at n=0 proves exactCapacityAttained for every finite support. Thus the number of available one-unit responses is exactly the retained support count.

For an added-proton response, the base member accepts the original named proton and becomes its conjugate acid. A trace consuming k base units with remainder r gives

  (h,b) ↦ (h+k,r),    k+r=b,
  (h+k)+r=h+b.

For an added-base response, the protonated member supplies the original proton and becomes the conjugate base:

  (h,b) ↦ (h+u,b+v),
  h<h+u,    b<b+v.

552. The least preorder generated by retained affinity comparisons

The source theorem ranges over finite comparisons of two named atomic occurrences sharing one electron-labelled support. Its induction base supplies a pairwise comparison, and its successor appends another comparison while retaining all prior records. The complete observation register varies with that declared input boundary. The native statement keeps those inputs explicit and establishes the forced relation and tie construction for them.

V3 specifies transitive-preorder closure of the complete registered pairwise affinity comparisons. Let R be their retained directed relation, with an edge a→b recording the comparison orientation toward b. Its reflexive-transitive closure R* is generated by

  a R* a,
  a R* b and (b,c)∈R ⇒ a R* c.

The closure is reflexive by its identity constructor. To prove transitivity, fix a R* b and induct on a derivation of b R* c. The identity case returns a R* b. A successor appends the last registered edge to the induction result. AffinityClosure.transitive implements this induction using the existing DynamicsStability.Reaches representation.

The construction is least, so it introduces no optional extra order pairs. If Q is any reflexive, transitive relation containing every edge in R, induction on an R* derivation gives

  a R* b ⇒ a Q b.

leastClosure proves this statement. Consequently any other least reflexive-transitive closure containing the same complete comparison records coincides pointwise with R*: each leastness statement gives one inclusion. uniqueLeastClosure proves this pointwise equivalence. This is uniqueness of the closure construction from the registered relation.

Define mutual closure by

  a ~R b ⇔ (a R* b and b R* a).

Reflexivity follows from the identity paths; symmetry exchanges the two witnesses; transitivity composes the forward paths and the reverse paths. tieReflexive, tieSymmetric and tieTransitive establish these equivalence laws. For the complete registered visit ledgers, AffinityRecurrenceBinding.completeObservationTie identifies this mutual-closure class exactly with invariance of every retained observation under endpoint exchange, using the source's exclusion of cycles between distinct trace classes. The base pairwise comparison supplies its held orientation; AffinityRecordClosure propagates that original orientation into the relation.

For an appended collection of comparison edges E, every prior edge remains in R++E. Induction on a path therefore yields

  a R* b ⇒ a (R++E)* b.

retainedClosure proves this inclusion; applying it in both directions gives retainedTie. Thus all previously established comparison paths and mutual classes remain represented on extension. executableClosure connects these inductive derivations with the existing complete finite search implementation, through DynamicsStability.perturbationReachabilityIff.

553. Observation equivalence and orientation of comparable classes

The symbol-distinction dependency supplies a complete source-bound observation map O. For a retained canonical symbol s, observed_label(O,s) returns its unique held class label ℓ. For endpoints a and b with successful observations O(a)=ℓa and O(b)=ℓb, the original distinguishability operation gives

  distinguishable(O,a,b) = (ℓa ≠ ℓb).

Consequently

  a and b share an observation class ⇔ ℓa=ℓb
    ⇔ distinguishable(O,a,b)=false.

For a finite endpoint record list C, generate tie edges between every pair whose observed labels agree:

  T(C) = {(a.atom,b.atom) : a∈C, b∈C, ℓa=ℓb}.

Equality is symmetric, so a closed source distinction supplies both a→b and b→a. In the reflexive-transitive closure of T(C) together with the retained comparison edges, these two paths prove mutual reachability. sourceEquivalentTied constructs both paths. A strict comparison requires a forward path and absence of the reverse path; equivalentCannotBeStrict therefore excludes strict ordering of this tied pair.

The class order can also be constructed directly from the retained comparison records. Let C be the complete endpoint record list, B the retained source comparisons and e the source-orientation projection defined above. Form

  E = T(C) ++ map(e,B).

Write a E* b for the previously proved least reflexive-transitive closure. The finite cycle check has the exact meaning

  ∀a,b∈C, (a.atom E* b.atom and b.atom E* a.atom) ⇒ ℓa=ℓb.

cycleCheckExactly proves both directions between the executable check and this condition. Forward and reverse reachability use the existing proved complete finite search. The check therefore implements the source's exclusion of cycles between distinguishable classes. Equal observed classes already supply both tie edges, so under this check

  a.atom E* b.atom and b.atom E* a.atom ⇔ ℓa=ℓb
    ⇔ distinguishable(O,a.symbol,b.symbol)=false.

Define the induced relation between held class labels by

  x ≼ y ⇔ ∃a,b∈C, ℓa=x, ℓb=y and a.atom E* b.atom.

Reflexivity follows by choosing the same endpoint representative twice and using the identity path. For transitivity, suppose a→*b witnesses x≼y and c→*d witnesses y≼z. Since ℓb=ℓc=y, the generated tie edge b→c joins the two paths, yielding a→*d and hence x≼z. For antisymmetry, take witnesses a→*b for x≼y and c→*d for y≼x. The ties b→c and d→a give b→*a. The cycle check then forces ℓa=ℓb and therefore x=y. These proofs derive the class-order laws from E, rather than taking an independently chosen class order as a premise.

Changing representatives does not change this relation. If ℓa=ℓa′ and ℓb=ℓb′, tie edges connect a with a′ and b with b′ in both directions. Prepending and appending these paths gives

  a.atom E* b.atom ⇔ a′.atom E* b′.atom.

representativeIndependent proves this equivalence directly.

The executable direction first tests class equality, then forward reachability, then reverse reachability, retaining an incomparable outcome if neither path exists. forwardForcesSecond and backwardForcesFirst prove the two strict cases. The latter uses the cycle condition to exclude a simultaneous forward path for unequal classes. tiedDirectionExactly proves that the tie outcome occurs exactly when the observed labels agree.

For an original comparison record c∈B whose first and second endpoint names match a and b, its edge e(c) occurs in E. Consequently the pair cannot be incomparable. recordDirection proves the exact result:

  direction(a,b) = tied,                         if ℓa=ℓb;
                 first,                        if ℓa≠ℓb and c.preference=c.first;
                 second,                       otherwise.

The base source comparison supplies its retained orientation. This result proves its propagation through the complete relation and exact tie class; it does not introduce a separate predictor for the source witness's atom names.

Bond polarity: the shared partition forced by unequal affinity

Organic reaction families: minimal directed changes and complete equivalence classes

A complete generated reaction retains all carrier placements and all changed relations. For a local relation row r=(ℓ,s_in,s_out), define its change predicate and the minimal transition trace by
\[
\chi(r)\iff s_{\mathrm{in}}\ne s_{\mathrm{out}},\qquad
P(L)=\operatorname{filter}_{\chi}(L).
\]
minimalExactlyChanged proves r∈P(L) if and only if r∈L and its states differ. unchangedExcluded removes identity rows. omissionLosesChangedRow proves that deleting a changed row from a proposed trace makes it incomplete. Thus minimality removes unchanged rows without discarding any change. Both ordered state positions are retained; directionalChangeCannotBeItsReverse proves that a nonidentity row cannot equal its reversal.

Map retains the generated reaction, complete local rows, conditions, source and separate mechanism record. Its completeChanges correspondence identifies the extracted transition trace with the original reaction-change ledger. generatedChangesAlreadyMinimal proves by induction that each generated RelationChange already passes the predicate, using its established before/after inequality. fromReaction therefore constructs Map directly from an existing generated reaction, without adding a selected pattern table. constructedMapRetainsCompleteCarriers retains its complete placement ledger; patternLabelsComplete recovers exactly the source changed-relation labels.

Two maps share a family precisely when their minimal directed traces have the same members:
\[
A\sim B\iff
(\forall r\in P(A),r\in P(B))\land
(\forall r\in P(B),r\in P(A)).
\]
The relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Row equality compares the complete held relation identity and its ordered before/after states. rowEqualExactly proves equality of the four stored text fields is exact equality of BondRow, including its HeldLabel. containsRowExactly proves the finite existential test, and matchPatternExactly proves that the executable two-way all/any comparison is equivalent to A∼B.

For any finite generated support S, decisionTrace enumerates every ordered pair and its comparison result:
\[
D(S)=[(A,B,\operatorname{matchPattern}(A,B)):A\in S,\ B\in S].
\]
completePairDecision proves coverage of every pair. classOf(S,A) contains exactly the members of S equivalent to A, and equalClassesOnSupport proves that equivalent representatives determine the same class. No external reaction taxonomy selects membership.

The base consists of two distinct balanced map records with the same minimal directed trace. For a matching next map N, appendHistory proves H(F')=H(F)++[N], and completeFamilyMatch retains equivalence of every member with the first. If N does not match the representative, nonmatchingOpensDistinctClass proves that N matches no existing member: otherwise transitivity would contradict its failed representative comparison. everyMemberBalanced reuses exact carrier-flow conservation for every family member and every label test.

Mechanism is retained separately from the net pattern. mechanismDoesNotSelectPattern and mechanismDoesNotSelectClass prove that substituting either mechanism record leaves the pattern and family comparison unchanged. Equal net changes therefore do not assert equal mechanisms; conditions and source evidence remain explicit in each map.

Atomic orbit-cell capacity from complete orientation support

Let r be a positive orbit rank and let n=r−1 count its predecessor steps. The previously derived generator has period three. Its positive predecessor supplies both the two Fold labels and the rank-two boundary multiplicity:
    b = predecessor(3) = 2.
At rank One the carrier retains one central orientation. Each successor adds the complete boundary pair. Writing Oₙ for the orientation support, the construction and its count are
    O₀ = [central],
    Oₙ₊₁ = [(n, first side), (n, second side)] followed by Oₙ,
    |O₀| = 1,    |Oₙ₊₁| = |Oₙ|+2,
    |Oₙ| = 1+2n.
Induction proves that a boundary orientation (k,s) occurs exactly when k<n, for each of the two sides s; the central orientation remains present at every rank. Thus every predecessor pair is retained and no additional predecessor step is included.

For each orientation o, the complete state support includes (o, first label) and (o, second label). If C(O) denotes this construction, induction over O gives |C(O)|=2|O|. The existing exclusion theorem rejects duplicate occupancy with the same label and orientation under alternating exchange. Applying the complete support construction therefore yields
    capacity(r) = |C(Oᵣ₋₁)| = 2(1+2(r−1)),
    capacity(r+1) = capacity(r)+4,    capacity(1)=2.
The first five ranks give 2,6,10,14,18. This sequence is generated by the support recurrence; it is not supplied as a derivational premise. The executable operations retain V3’s boolean, nonpositive-count and negative-count rejection behavior.

Distinctness of the complete orbit-cell support

The orientation recurrence also proves that no orientation occurs twice. At successor n+1, either new boundary orientation has predecessor index n, whereas every earlier boundary orientation has index k<n. The two new sides are distinct constructors. Induction therefore proves that Oₙ contains no duplicates. Mapping every retained orientation to its two distinct labels preserves this property: equality of state pairs would require equality of both the orientation and the held label. Complete three-direction composition derivation of the oscillator closure

Let n=r-1 be the retained excitation multiplicity through positive shell rank r. Natural coordinates encode occurrence multiplicities along the three labelled directions; an empty coordinate is an empty direction, not a supplied scientific scalar. The exact-shell and filled supports are
    T_n = {(a,b,c) : a+b+c=n},
    F_n = {(a,b,c) : a+b+c<=n}.
The complete two-direction partitions separate the empty first direction from the positive first direction:
    P_0=[(0,0)],
    P_(n+1)=[(0,n+1)] followed by [(a+1,b) : (a,b) in P_n].
The same disjoint construction gives
    T_0=[(0,0,0)],
    T_(n+1)=[(0,b,c) : (b,c) in P_(n+1)]
             followed by [(a+1,b,c) : (a,b,c) in T_n],
    F_0=T_0,    F_(n+1)=F_n followed by T_(n+1).
Soundness and completeness prove both displayed support equalities for every n. The successor branches cannot overlap because their first coordinates are respectively empty and positive; distinctness is preserved within each branch. Successive shells are disjoint because their excitation totals differ. Each admissible spatial composition therefore occurs exactly once.

Writing p_n=|P_n| and t_n=|T_n|, induction gives
    p_n=n+1,    t_0=1,    t_(n+1)=t_n+n+2,
    2t_n=(n+1)(n+2).
Both exclusion-distinct Fold labels occur once on every spatial composition. The complete labelled filled-support count C_n obeys
    C_0=2,    C_(n+1)=C_n+2t_(n+1)
                       =C_n+(n+2)(n+3).
The base identity 3C_0=1*2*3 and successor calculation
    3C_(n+1)=(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)+3(n+2)(n+3)
             =(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)
prove 3C_n=(n+1)(n+2)(n+3) at every depth. Consequently
    C_(r-1)=r(r+1)(r+2)/3.
The native proof establishes exact divisibility: the original oscillator operation's divisibility guard passes for every positive rank and its quotient equals the complete labelled support. The complete-state membership theorem is
    ((a,b,c),label) in labelled(F_n) iff a+b+c<=n
for each of the two held labels, together with duplicate-free support. This binds the arithmetic result to the full spatial and label enumeration.

Material identity and retained extension records

The material-system obligation requires the constituent carrier, composition and bonding organization, and declared observation boundary to remain distinguishable. The retained-record argument makes explicit why erasing one required distinction cannot provide the same identity. Write R=(C,B,d,O), where C is the retained sequence of chemical constitution/isotope/context records, B the named bonding records, d the declared boundary, and O the observation/reference pairs. For this record,
    R=R' iff C=C' and B=B' and d=d' and O=O'.
Consequently any identification relation preserving all four coordinates implies record equality. Conversely, equality of the four coordinates suffices: the record introduces no additional identity test. If an encoding e collapses two unequal records and a recovery map q reconstructs both, then
    R=q(e(R))=q(e(R'))=R',
contradicting their retained distinction.

A constituent, relation or observation extension appends its record to the corresponding sequence and holds the other coordinates fixed. With E_x the extension and P_x removal of its final appended coordinate,
    P_x(E_x(R))=R.
Thus E_x(R)=E_x(R') implies R=R'. For a finite extension history h=[x_1,...,x_n], define E_h by successive extension and P_h by removing those extensions in reverse order. The induction is
    P_[](E_[](R))=R,
    P_(x::h)(E_(x::h)(R))=P_x(P_h(E_h(E_x(R))))=P_x(E_x(R))=R.
It follows that arbitrary finite histories retain every earlier constituent, bonding and observation record, keep d fixed, preserve nonempty constituent support, and cannot merge initially distinct records. Each retained constituent carries its complete chemical constitution, isotope and context; the proof does not impose uniform composition across different constituents.

The separate original candidate grammar has eight binary preservation coordinates: carrier, relation, organization, observation, record, provenance, generality and extension. Its literal Cartesian product contains 2^8=256 alternatives. Acceptance requires the admitted value on every coordinate; therefore the all-admitted tuple is the unique survivor. Exhaustion and each rejected-coordinate elimination are proved for the original product. The native program reproduces every pinned candidate, decision, control, closure, registration field and hash, and the original independent validator accepts the result and rejects the three adverse cases.

Generated subshell support and first occupation

For joint-cover bound B, the generated support is C_B = [(p,o): 1≤p, 1≤o≤p, p+o≤B], traversed by increasing joint cover and then principal rank, as specified by the original nested loops. At a fixed cover c, the loop retains exactly the principal indices p with 0<p<c and c−p≤p and emits (p,c−p). Thus every emitted cell satisfies p+o=c. Conversely, any positive pair with o≤p and p+o=c appears at its principal index p. Induction on B, using C_(B+1)=C_B concatenated with the cells of cover B+1, proves completeness over the entire stated support.

Every principal index occurs once within its cover. Different covers cannot share a cell: an earlier cell has p+o≤B, whereas a new cell has p+o=B+1. Therefore the generated support contains no repeated cell. These arguments apply to every natural bound B, not just the atomic endpoint used by the source operation.

The capacity of orbit rank o=n+1 is the upstream generated value q(o)=2(1+2n). For a remaining occupation R, filling emits min(R,q(o)) and passes R−min(R,q(o)) to the next cell, stopping when this remainder is zero. The implementation uses the admitted endpoint to generate C_(2·137); it does not add an atomic-number guard at137. The source comparison includes every atom1–137, larger inputs, closure prefixes and rejection cases. All266 compared cases agree with pinned V3.

G-block derivation: ordered support, conserved filling and closed predictions

The ordering is explicit. For cells a=(p,o) and b=(p',o'), write a≺b when p+o<p'+o', or when p+o=p'+o' and p<p'. Specimen: source-bound sampling and retained preparation

A specimen is a positive finite part of its material with an explicit sampling map, retained preparation history and declared representativeness boundary. Material phase: connected recurrence and symmetry classes

At declared conditions, let G be the retained support graph and R(x) the existing ordered-region record associated with a support cell x. The established stable-observation relation is

R(a) ∼ R(b) iff fibreView(R(a))=fibreView(R(b)) and sameSymmetryClass(R(a),R(b)).

Here sameSymmetryClass means equivalence of every reversible support-and-adjacency-preserving transformation, as defined by the existing Physics symmetry predicate. Reflexivity follows from equality and reflexivity of that equivalence. Transitivity follows by composing the fibre equality and, for each transformation pair, the two symmetry equivalences.

For root r, define phase membership of x by a valid finite path [r,…,x] in G whose every cell y satisfies R(r)∼R(y). The length-One path supplies the base for a held root. A valid adjacent successor in the same class extends the path, preserving every prior cell and appending the successor. Induction on these extensions proves closure for every finite successor history. Every member is connected to r and shares both the recurrence fibre and symmetry class. A different fibre or symmetry class therefore excludes membership.

Maximality follows without selecting a favourable subset. If H is any homogeneous connected support containing paths from r to each of its cells, each such path is valid in G and all its cells belong to H. Homogeneity supplies R(r)∼R(y) for every path cell. Thus every x∈H belongs to the constructed phase. No homogeneous connected support at those conditions can contain an omitted reachable member.

B(R)=B(R′), and, for every u,v, (u,v)∈Q(R) iff (u,v)∈Q(R′).

Opposed translation traversal and generated direction families
For retained pair p=(a,b), a generated translation t supplies p→(t(a),t(b)); opposed traversal reverses this same relation. Let I(p,q) mean w(p₁)=w(q₁), w(p₂)=w(q₂) and E(p)↔E(q). Exact factor-removal procedure for rotation orders
The source starts with positive remainder r=n and trial divisor d=2. While d²≤r, a divisible trial is retained once and the remainder is repeatedly divided by d; a nondivisible trial is skipped. The divisor then advances by one. At exit, the final remainder is retained precisely when it exceeds One. Boolean, noninteger, zero and negative host inputs are rejected by the original positive-whole guard.
For an exact division, r mod d=0 and r mod d+d⌊r/d⌋=r imply r=dq, q=⌊r/d⌋. Existing exact fraction-reduction proofs give q>0. Since d≥2, q<q+q≤dq=r. Therefore repeated division strictly decreases a positive remainder; its final value remains positive and no greater than its input. For the outer loop, use μ(r,d)=r+1−d as a natural-valued termination measure. The branch condition d²≤r implies d≤r, and every retained remainder r′≤r gives r′+1−(d+1)<r+1−d. This inequality is proved by induction over d with direct successor subtraction. Both recursive loops therefore terminate without a numerical search cutoff. The subtraction here belongs to the termination measure, not an added scientific scalar.

Complete prime support and coprime residue correspondence

\[p\in F(n)\iff \operatorname{Prime}(p)\land p\mid n.\]
The loop invariant excludes every divisor k with 1<k<d before trial d. Removing d preserves that exclusion and makes the remaining factor indivisible by d. An emitted trial divisor is prime: a smaller proper divisor would divide the original remainder, contradicting the invariant. When d² exceeds the final remainder r>1, any proper factorization r=ab would have a,b≥d, contradicting r<d². Conversely, a prime divisor survives removal of every different prime: p|d^k s implies p|d or p|s, and distinct primality excludes p|d. Induction on the actual decreasing loop measure therefore retains every prime divisor.
For the source residue list R(n), this gives

If a common divisor exceeds One, the same factor loop supplies a prime divisor of that common divisor; it belongs to F(n) and excludes c. Conversely, any excluded prime divides both c and n, and hence their gcd, so that gcd cannot be One. Thus the executable count |R(n)| counts exactly the coprime residue labels across the full supplied positive-order domain.

Crystallographic rotation restriction: unrestricted arithmetic closure

The rank-two rotation boundary counts coprime residue labels, not sampled angles. Let R(n) be the exact source residue list on 1,…,n and φ(n)=|R(n)|. The preceding prime-support and coprimality proofs identify this executable count with the complete reduced residue carrier. For n>1, n itself is excluded because gcd(n,n)=n; hence the existing Fold/orbit reduced-residue counting theorem applies without changing the carrier. For prime p, every positive label below p is coprime, giving φ(p)=p−1.

Complete residue blocks give the prime-power count. The interval 1,…,pk decomposes into k translated blocks, with translation by pj preserving remainders modulo p. In each block exactly p−1 labels have nonzero remainder. Thus
\[\#\{1\le c\le pk:p\nmid c\}=k(p-1),\qquad \varphi(p^{k+1})=p^k(p-1).\]
Prime support proves that the only prime divisor of p^{k+1} is p. This connects the block count to the actual source filter rather than introducing a new definition of φ.

For composite orders, lift the coprime labels for n across p complete blocks. The gcd is unchanged by adding a multiple of n, so the lifted list has pφ(n) elements. A label is coprime to pn exactly when it is coprime to n and is not divisible by p. If p divides n, the second condition already follows from the first. If p does not divide n, the excluded labels are precisely p times the original coprime labels for n: cancellation of the coprime factor p gives gcd(pc,n)=gcd(c,n). Injectivity and complete membership of that map give exactly φ(n) exclusions. Therefore
\[\varphi(pn)=\begin{cases}p\varphi(n)&p\mid n,\\(p-1)\varphi(n)&p\nmid n.\end{cases}\]
Both equations count the entire supplied carrier. No bounded order search or stored answer table supplies either recurrence.

Now let p be any prime divisor of n. Write n=pm with m=n/p<n. If p does not divide m, the second recurrence gives the factor p−1 directly. Otherwise the first recurrence and induction on m preserve that factor. Consequently
\[p\mid n\quad\Longrightarrow\quad p-1\mid\varphi(n).\]
Since φ(n)>0, the rank-two bound φ(n)≤2 implies p−1≤2. Every prime factor is therefore 2 or 3; in particular the only odd prime factor is 3. The recurrences also show φ(m)≤φ(pm), so a prime quotient of an admitted order remains admitted. Strong induction on that strictly smaller quotient closes all positive orders. Multiplying the admitted quotient forms by 2 or 3 produces the retained orders and possible exclusions 8, 9, 12, 18. Their degrees follow from the same recurrences:
\[\varphi(1)=1,\quad\varphi(2)=1,\quad\varphi(3)=2,\quad\varphi(4)=2,\quad\varphi(6)=2,\]
\[\varphi(8)=4,\quad\varphi(9)=6,\quad\varphi(12)=4,\quad\varphi(18)=6.\]
This is an induction over every positive n: the finite branch values arise from its prime-factor descent. The resulting equivalences are
\[\varphi(n)\le2\iff n\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}\iff\exists a,b:\ n=2^a3^b,\ a\le2,\ b\le1,\ \neg(a=2\land b=1).\]
The prime-power formula separately gives the binary and ternary exponent restrictions. Direct enumeration of the constrained exponent pairs proves the reverse implication. The original five-candidate guard is proved to pass, and the returned six-field certificate is proved equal to the exact source certificate. Order 5 is excluded, while every positive order below 5 is admitted; hence its least-excluded field is justified.

\[C_{X\mathbin{+}[x]}(p)\iff C_X(p)\land e_p(x)=s_p.\]
This retains the previous conditions and adds precisely the next site's return condition.  =\operatorname{positive}(o(s_p),q_x\oplus q),\]
where \(\oplus\) is the existing exact positive-fraction sum, preserving the cross-multiplied sum and denominator through normalization. For a nonempty complete carrier [x_1,...,x_n], induction on the full predecessor list yields
\[\operatorname{merge}(p,X)=\operatorname{positive}(o(s_p),q_{x_1}\oplus(\cdots\oplus q_{x_n})).\]
The result cannot be structural absence. Thus the retained coherent class supplies positive observation support while every contributing path remains recorded. Substitution populations and exclusion of a rational fixed scale

V3's quasicrystalline inflation construction generates the population recurrence A→AB, B→A. With positive population pair (a,b), the successor is
\[(a,b)\longmapsto(a+b,a),\qquad(a_0,b_0)=(1,1).\]
At positive depth d, the retained history has exactly d rows. Induction on the successor count proves this history length and the two population equations. The first six rows are (1,1), (2,1), (3,2), (5,3), (8,5), (13,8), reproduced directly by the Lean implementation and pinned V3 execution.

A positive rational fixed scale in lowest terms, p/q, would satisfy
\[p^2=pq+q^2,\qquad p>0,\ q>0,\ \gcd(p,q)=1.\]
The right side is q(p+q), so q divides p². If q>1, it has a prime divisor r. Then r divides p², hence r divides p, while r also divides q. This contradicts coprimality, so q=1. Since p divides both p² and pq, the equation also implies p divides q²=1; positivity forces p=1. The equation would then read 1=2, which is impossible. Thus no reduced positive rational fixed scale exists. This is a theorem for all positive p and q in the source domain, not a bounded search through candidate fractions, and it does not evaluate an irrational limit.

Grain identity and the exact grain boundary

The crystal carrier retains its complete site and edge sets together with an orientation label O(x) at each site. Connectivity follows the retained adjacency relation in either traversal direction; the underlying ordered edge record is preserved. Define x~y by finite adjacent continuation through sites with unchanged orientation. The base case is the held site itself; a successor appends an adjacent site z when O(y)=O(z):
\[x\sim x,\qquad x\sim y\ \land\ y\leftrightarrow z\ \land\ O(y)=O(z)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad x\sim z.\]
Induction on the complete path proves that both endpoints belong to the carrier and that O(x)=O(y). Concatenation proves transitivity. Reversing each adjacency and its orientation equality, then concatenating the reversed preceding path, proves symmetry. Thus the grain at a held root r is the complete region
\[G_r=\{x:r\sim x\}.\]
For x,y in G_r, reversal of the r-to-x path followed by the r-to-y path yields x~y, and their orientations agree. The construction retains an internal path for every member, including every intermediate site.

Maximality follows from the same path induction. Let R be any connected region with the root r and constant orientation. Every internal path from r to a member x starts at a held site; at each adjacent successor, orientation coherence supplies precisely the equality required by the continuation rule. Hence r~x and
\[R\subseteq G_r.\]
Since G_r itself is connected and orientation coherent, it is the maximal such region containing r. If G_a and G_b share a site c, the paths a~c and b~c compose with reversal to give a~b. Transitivity then proves both membership implications, so
\[G_a\cap G_b\ne\varnothing\quad\Rightarrow\quad G_a=G_b\]
as equality of membership predicates. Disconnected regions with the same orientation are not merged merely because their labels agree: membership still requires the complete adjacent path.

The boundary retains exactly the original ordered edges whose endpoints have different orientations:
\[\partial G=\{(a,b)\in E:O(a)\ne O(b)\}.\]
For a held edge, equality of endpoint orientations constructs the one-step coherent path; conversely every coherent path forces equal endpoint orientations. Consequently
\[(a,b)\in\partial G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(a,b)\in E\ \land\ \neg(a\sim b).\]
This is the exact adjacency where distinct grains meet, derived from their connectivity and orientation records. The filter preserves the original edge order and excludes every non-boundary edge without inserting a threshold or fitted orientation tolerance.

Carrier support follows by the same induction. Unmoved rows retain their original supported sites; the moved occurrence arrives at the declared held destination of its adjacent edge. Thus an initially supported complete state remains supported after every finite run.

Nucleation and phase growth: complete boundary persistence and least size

A candidate cluster retains its cells C, the lattice graph E, its phase identity and its condition record. Its complete boundary is the existing graph cut:
\[B_C=\{(a,b)\in E:\mathbf1_C(a)\ne\mathbf1_C(b)\}.\]
Every boundary edge has its retained recurrence row. The ordered projection of those rows equals B_C, so neither a missing boundary relation nor an extra internal relation is hidden by the persistence test. Each row binds its transfer endpoints to the actual edge and carries the before and after interior macrostates. The existing phase view is the pair of phase label and complete retained fibre. For a row r, its recurrence condition is
\[V(r_{\rm before})=V(r_{\rm after})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda_{\rm before}=\lambda_{\rm after}\ \land\ F_{\rm before}=F_{\rm after}.\]
The cluster persists exactly when this condition holds across every row of its complete boundary ledger. A changed phase label or fibre in any retained row rejects persistence. Since each before-label is bound to the cluster phase, the after-label remains that phase throughout the complete boundary comparison. The departure and arrival projections of the full transfer ledger coincide by the existing paired-transfer conservation theorem.

For the complete generated candidate family G, write P(C) for this boundary-persistence test and n(C)=|C| for the retained cell count. The nucleus family is
\[\mathcal N(G)=\{C\in G:P(C)\ \land\ \forall D\in G,
P(D)\Rightarrow n(C)\le n(D)\}.\]
A finite recursive witness search examines every candidate. A failed persistence test is skipped. A persistent candidate is retained when there is no persistent suffix witness or when its size is no larger than the suffix minimum; otherwise the suffix minimum is retained. Induction proves membership, persistence and the lower-bound condition together. If any candidate persists, the same recursion constructively returns a witness. The scientific output is the full filter defined above, so all equally small persistent clusters remain included. For any A,B in that output,
\[n(A)\le n(B),\qquad n(B)\le n(A),\qquad n(A)=n(B).\]
Thus the critical size follows from the complete persistence comparison; it is not inserted as an independent coefficient or selected by discarding equal-sized candidates.

A compatible growth step appends a fresh cell x:
\[C_{k+1}=C_k\mathbin{+\!+}[x],\qquad x\notin C_k,\qquad
|C_{k+1}|=|C_k|+1.\]
The step retains the phase and declared condition, checks persistence of the resulting cluster against its complete boundary, and records the arriving transfer with destination x. Every preceding cell remains in the new support. Induction through the joined growth history H establishes
\[\lambda_{\rm final}=\lambda_{\rm initial},\qquad
\text{condition}_{\rm final}=\text{condition}_{\rm initial},\qquad
C_{\rm initial}\subseteq C_{\rm final},\]
\[|C_{\rm final}|=|C_{\rm initial}|+|T(H)|,\qquad
|\operatorname{clusters}(H)|=|T(H)|+1.\]
Here T(H) is the complete ordered growth-transfer ledger. Electronic bands and structural gaps

The complete material network and its prepared constituent support are linked in both directions: every held lattice constituent belongs to the prepared support, and every prepared constituent is represented by a held lattice site. For declared observation depth d, the existing generator enumerates exactly the positive-length site words
\[G_d=\{p:0<|p|\le d\ \land\ \text{every site of }p\text{ is held in the lattice}\}.\]
Each word is tested for complete adjacency and phase recurrence. With prepared state S and phase action A, the allowed band support is therefore
\[B_d=\{p\in G_d:\operatorname{pathValid}(p)\ \land\ A(S,p)=S\}.\]
The source-bound membership proof establishes both directions, so every compatible generated path appears and no incompatible path is inserted. This uses the complete generator at each declared depth, not a selected sample of paths.

Let O(p) be the retained observation reading class and I the declared interval test on those readings. Interval support is the complete filter
\[B_{d,I}=\{p\in B_d:I(O(p))\}.\]
Combining the interval filter with the existing band-membership theorem gives the exact criterion
\[p\in B_{d,I}\Longleftrightarrow
p\in G_d\ \land\ \operatorname{pathValid}(p)\ \land\ A(S,p)=S\ \land\ I(O(p)).\]
In particular, a gap is precisely
\[B_{d,I}=\varnothing\Longleftrightarrow
\forall p\in G_d,\ \operatorname{pathValid}(p)\land A(S,p)=S\Rightarrow\neg I(O(p)).\]
For the forward direction, any compatible path whose reading lies in the interval would be a member of the empty support, a contradiction. For the reverse direction, any first element of a nonempty interval support would supply exactly such a path, again contradicting the stated absence. Every admitted path whose reading is inside I is included by the same equivalence. The declared interval classifies observed readings after the full compatibility support is constructed; it adds no scientific rule selecting a surviving path.

Conductor, semiconductor and insulator distinction

Let B be the complete phase-compatible band support already derived from the generated lattice traces. A state label belongs to the retained support precisely when it is the observed class of a trace in B. Occupied labels O and accessible labels A are retained subsets of that support. Thus every endpoint has a generated band trace; activating access does not substitute a new state carrier.

For the direct relation Gd, enumerate every endpoint pair O × A and retain exactly those connected by a generated path:
  Pd = {(o,a) ∈ O × A : Path(Gd,o,a)}.
The carrier product membership proof proceeds by induction on O. The reachability/path equivalence then identifies every retained pair with a full path witness, not a selected path sample. Consequently,
  Pd = ∅ ⇔ ∀o∈O ∀a∈A, ¬Path(Gd,o,a).

When the declared conditions admit finite activation, retain its relation Ga and its positive exact gap Δ = n/d, n>0 and d>0, and construct
  Pa = {(o,a) ∈ O × A : Path(Ga,o,a)}.
When no activation is held, Pa is empty and no numerical gap is assigned. Both relations retain the complete band-state support; filling, gap and conditions remain in the output record.

The distinction follows by exhausting these support cases:
  conductor      ⇔ Pd ≠ ∅;
  semiconductor  ⇔ Pd = ∅ and Pa ≠ ∅;
  insulator      ⇔ Pd = ∅ and Pa = ∅.
These alternatives are exhaustive and disjoint. In the insulating case every occupied-to-accessible direct path, and every such path under the retained activation, is excluded. The gap records the declared activation boundary; it is not a fitted transport coefficient or an added universal threshold. The construction introduces no conductivity formula.

Electron and hole carrier duality

The exclusion result already establishes that identical constituent words at the same cell cannot admit alternating exchange: the exchange is fixed, whereas alternating orientation must be opposite and cannot equal itself. For the resulting binary occupation carrier, let S retain every local state and O its occupied support. The held absence is the full complement within that carrier,
  H(S,O) = {s ∈ S : s ∉ O}.
The filter-membership derivation yields
  s ∈ H(S,O) ⇔ (s ∈ S and s ∉ O).
Therefore every s ∈ S has exactly one of the occupied and absent descriptions. No state is removed when its occupation is absent. Provided O ⊆ S, taking the dual description again recovers occupation:
  H(S,H(S,O)) = O
as equality of membership for every state. The forward implication excludes absence from both descriptions; the reverse implication uses occupation to rule out its complement.

For a retained transfer from s to t, write O and O′ for occupation before and after. Its endpoint conditions are
  s ∈ O, t ∉ O; s ∉ O′, t ∈ O′.
Applying the complement equivalence gives
  s ∉ H(S,O), t ∈ H(S,O);
  s ∈ H(S,O′), t ∉ H(S,O′).
Thus the same event is an occupation transfer s→t and an absence transfer t→s. At any unchanged local state, occupation membership before and after is equivalent, hence absence membership is also equivalent. This is a dual description of the retained transition, not a second constituent created by removing a site.

The existing electric distinction represents charge as a positive magnitude and a held orientation. Its dual retains the magnitude and reverses that orientation. The two orientations differ and reversing twice recovers the original charge. Complete occupation and absence ledgers both project to the full original state carrier, proved by induction over every finite support list. After the prediction seal the original observation correspondence names these two descriptions electron and hole carriers.

The original eight-axis grammar contains 2^8 = 256 forms. Every candidate, decision, closure record, control and original operational witness is retained; applicable independent positive and adverse validation cases are checked against the pinned source.

Exclusion-bounded canonical mode occupation

Take any finite occupation list L for one canonical constituent word w and one canonical cell c. Every occupant a in this list retains a.word = w and a.cell = c. The list domain includes every finite length. Exclusion requires alternating exchange for every pair of retained occupants.

If L begins with two occupants a,b, their equal word and cell imply
  exchange(a,b) = (a,b).
Alternating exchange would also require
  orientation(exchange(a,b)) = opposite(orientation(a,b)).
Together these make one held orientation equal to its opposite, contradicted by the previously derived distinction of the two orientations. Hence every list with two or more occupants is rejected. The remaining list cases are exactly
  admitted(L) ⇔ L = [] or L = [a].
The empty and singleton cases admit no pair requiring exclusion and satisfy the predicate. Canonical identity then forces a = (w,c), giving
  L = [] or L = [(w,c)].
These outcomes are distinct: held structural absence and one retained indistinguishable occupation. Thus binary occupation follows from exclusion applied to the full finite-list domain, rather than from preselecting a binary candidate list. No numerical zero occupation scalar or additional capacity parameter is introduced.

Occupation-majority and absence-majority semiconductor classes

The complete source-bound doping record retains gained occupation support G and lost occupation support L, the latter providing the opposed absence description. Count every retained carrier in these supports and write g = |G| and l = |L|. The carrier imbalance has two possible strict orientations:
  l < g  ⇔ occupation-majority;
  g < l  ⇔ absence-majority.
For g ≠ l, finite whole-count ordering proves that one of these inequalities holds. They cannot both hold: strict order is asymmetric. The selection therefore has exactly one of the two held orientations for every imbalance. When g = l, no imbalance is present and no majority orientation is assigned. This balanced record does not add a third majority class.

The implementation computes g and l from the full prior/result support difference, rather than receiving a preselected carrier class. It proves both displayed equivalences and the exhaustive result under g ≠ l. Interchanging gained and lost counts interchanges the inequalities and hence reverses the held orientation:
  select(l,g) = opposite(select(g,l))
whenever a majority orientation is present. The quantities remain whole counts and the direction remains a held orientation; no signed carrier magnitude or fitted majority coefficient is required.

The original 256-form preservation grammar, three operational witnesses, controls, elimination/closure records and source-isolated validation are retained in their original order and domain.
